in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account that the french authorities have requested that the scope of the council decision be extended to cover the tax on alcoholic beverages in respect of their overseas territories. i think that the intention to allow a lower rate than the traditional rum produced in the four french outermost regions to be applied is valid and that it benefits the local economy of the region. i am in favour of this initiative and of the commission's proposal, which allows france to apply, during the period 2014-2020, a reduced rate of excise duty and a vss up to 50% of their minimum rates. i also support the proposal to france to draw up an interim report to the european commission by 31 july 2017. i consider it important that france should make an overall assessment of the impact of the granting of the tax benefit granted. it is important to take stock in 2017 to determine whether there is still an interest in continuing the application of this measure. it should also be examined whether this measure is sufficient in itself to support the competitiveness of the rum-cane value chain in guadeloupe, french guiana, martinique and réunion.
in writing. since december 2011, traditional rum produced in the french overseas departments has benefited from a special derogation which allows it to have a reduced rate of excise duty. however, this derogation expired at the end of december 2013. however, the european commission, at the request of the french government, and considering that the minimum assumptions are met, has proposed that this derogation be applied again for the period 2014-2020.
in writing. - this measure is intended to compensate producers in the french overseas departments for the competitive disadvantage they face, caused by the persistence and combination of factors such as remoteness, insularity, small size, difficult topography and climate. the economic dependence on a small number of products, in particular the sugar cane-rum value chain, is also a determining factor, which severely restricts its development. this proposal seeks to extend for a further seven years the application of decision 2007/659/ec authorising france to apply, in its metropolitan territory and in respect of traditional rum produced in the french overseas departments, a reduced rate of excise duty which may be lower than the minimum rate of excise duty but which may not be more than 50% lower than the normal national rate of excise duty on alcohol. the reduced rate of excise duty is limited to an annual quota of 120 000 hectolitres of pure alcohol. the french authorities also requested that the scope of the council decision be extended to include the tax on alcoholic beverages. these are justified measures, and we have therefore voted in favour of them.
in writing. − council decision 2007/659/ec of 9 october 2007 authorises france to apply, in the territory of metropolitan france and in respect of traditional rum produced in the french overseas departments, a reduced rate of excise duty which may be lower than the minimum rate of excise duty provided for in council directive 92/84/eec but which may not be lower by more than 50% than the normal national rate of excise duty on alcohol. this measure is intended to compensate producers in the french overseas departments for the competitive disadvantage they face, caused by the persistence and combination of factors such as remoteness, insularity, small size, difficult topography and climate, and their economic dependence on a limited number of products, in particular the cane-sugar-rum value chain, which severely restrict their development. with this proposal, we will extend this authorization for another seven years. i think that this reduction is fair, because it helps the peripheral regions, and i therefore voted in favour of it.

in writing. - i approve the present report, considering that the defence of immunity can only be applied if the immunity of a member is compromised under the legal order of his own state (by police action or by the judicial authorities of the member's state of origin) and if no request for the waiver of that member's immunity has been made. i therefore believe that in such cases the member may request the defence of his immunity in accordance with the rules of procedure of the european parliament. i believe that a review of these rules of procedure will be beneficial, as it will increase the transparency of the european parliament's decisions and procedures concerning the parliamentary immunity of its members.
in writing. − the immunity of members of parliament must be understood as an essential guarantee of the regular and free functioning of legislative assemblies. if it does not seem possible today that in most member states freedom of movement and expression, as well as the health and even the lives of members of parliament, could be jeopardised, this has not always been the case. there is therefore a relevant historical backdrop to this legal form which should not be overlooked, but its importance does not stop there. with the increasing judicialisation of political life, it is not uncommon for political leaders to be sued in court, not for a judicial conviction but for a political sanction and suspicion which are not always appropriate. it is therefore urgent to strike a fair balance between the possibility for members to request the waiver of parliamentary immunity when they or the house consider it justified, and at the same time to ensure that this prerogative which is intended to defend each member and the house as a whole is not called into question for irrelevant reasons. i hope that the amendments introduced will strengthen this sense of balance and help to give the parliamentary function a more prestigious status.
in writing. - this report deals with issues relating to the application of the immunity regime for members. the committee on legal affairs of the european parliament (juri - committee on privileges and immunities) has proposed a recast of the existing rules on immunity in the rules of procedure in order to reflect both the case law of the court of justice and the practice of that committee. this report follows the recommendations of the juri committee. the report focuses on four points, based on the case law of the ecj: 1) the defence of parliamentary immunity is a way for the ep to intervene, at the request of a member, when national authorities violate or are preparing to violate the immunity of one of its members; 2) a clarification that parliamentary immunity is not a personal privilege of a member but a guarantee of the independence and integrity of parliament as a whole and of its members; (3) the repeated use of requests without new evidence must be avoided. finally, the report specifies the right of members to be heard by the commission, providing for the prevention of the use of this right as a tool to delay the procedure. we have voted in favour of this, following the position of our group.
in writing. - i have tabled my vote in favour of the amendment to parliament's rules of procedure concerning the waiver and defence of parliamentary immunity. a reformulation of the rules has been proposed to bring them up to date with recent case law and the practice which has been established in the committee responsible for the subject under consideration. as the diploma in question states, parliamentary immunity is not a personal privilege of a member but a guarantee of the independence of parliament and its members, and updating the rules governing this matter was therefore of the utmost importance in order to defend the prestige of this institution.
in writing. − on the basis of the draft opinions and the final opinions of the juri committee, the european parliament proposed that the relevant rules on the defence of parliamentary immunity be recast in order to make their structure more coherent and to adapt their substance to recent case law and the practice of the committee responsible. parliamentary immunity is not a personal privilege of the member but a guarantee of the independence of parliament and its members. the rules of procedure should therefore regulate this matter in a legally unassailable manner and in sufficient detail to protect the prestige of the institution in which the citizens of the union are directly represented. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - parliamentary immunity is not a personal privilege of the member but a guarantee of the independence of the whole parliament and its members. i believe that immunity should be waived in all cases where it is necessary to clarify legal situations, and that only the appearance in court should not affect the parliamentary work of members.

in writing. - i approve this report, considering that the cultivation of gmos has not been authorised in the european union since 2010. another reason for my view is that there are no studies to safely assess the long-term risks of gmo cultivation and the consequences for human health and the environment. i reiterate that there is a need for a more rigorous assessment of the effects of gmos through independent research. i would point out that today, in the face of a lack of information, the vast majority of consumers are concerned about genetically modified food. i do not think that the cultivation of genetically modified maize 1507 brings any advantages to consumers. for these reasons, i am opposed to the adoption of the proposal for a council decision on the placing on the market for cultivation of genetically modified maize (zea mays l., line 1507), by giving priority to the interests of consumers, the safeguarding of public health and the protection of the environment.
in writing. − efsa issued, at the request of the commission, three scientific opinions updating its previous risk assessments and recommendations in which, in february 2012, it disagreed with the applicant's conclusion that the study it cited provided satisfactory evidence that maize 1507 poses a negligible risk in the eu to non-target lepidopterans, and instead drew attention to the fact that highly sensitive non-target moths and butterflies may be at risk due to their exposure to maize 1507 pollen. i also recall that the cultivation of gmos has not been authorised in the eu since 2010, when the cultivation of the amflora potato was authorised and even the authorisation to cultivate this potato was annulled by the general court of the european union on 13 december 2013. i therefore believe that the proposal for a council decision concerning the placing on the market for cultivation of a genetically modified maize (zea mays l., line 1507) should be carefully reviewed, always keeping in mind the health of consumers.
in writing. - the resolution opposes the adoption of the proposal for a council decision concerning the placing on the market for cultivation of maize genetically modified to give it resistance to certain lepidopterans. it is requested that no new varieties of gmos be authorised and that old authorisations not be renewed until the methods used for risk assessment have been considerably improved. in particular, this type of gmo has known consequences on highly sensitive non-target insect species. impact studies on other organisms are lacking. in the risk assessment, efsa admitted that it had not taken into account the potential risks associated with the tolerance of this maize to the herbicide ammonium glufosinate, classified as toxic for reproduction, which could lead to an increase in the use of this herbicide. in addition to the risks to biodiversity posed by the proliferation of gm crops, which have a competitive advantage over other non-modified species, the release of these gmos into the environment can have serious consequences for ecosystems, in particular compromising conventional and organic crops, it adds that at present it is not possible to provide scientifically credible assurances of the safety of gm products in food and feed. we voted in favour.
in writing. - the proposal for a resolution opposes an exceptional derogation allowing the placing on the market for cultivation of maize (zea mays l., line 1507) genetically modified to confer resistance to certain lepidopterans. i am in favour of this derogation and i support the position of the ppe group, which is why i voted against this motion for a resolution, which was nevertheless adopted by the european parliament. in this context, i would stress that a fundamentalist overall position on the part of the european union with regard to gmos has created a situation of severe competitive imbalance between european farmers and, for example, north american farmers, in addition to the continuing inconsistency of prohibiting the cultivation of gmos in the european area, but importing them from other geographical areas, such as north america, for the feed of our livestock.
in writing. − the cultivation of genetically modified organisms (gmos) has not been authorised in the european union since 2010, with only monsanto mon 810 maize authorised, but the authorisation of which has been pending for some years. i am voting in favour of opposing the proposal for a council decision concerning the placing on the market for cultivation, in accordance with directive 2001/18/ec of the european parliament and of the council, of a maize (zea mays l., line 1507) because this product, when genetically modified, confers resistance to certain lepidopterans.

mr president, bulgarian and romanian citizens are being expelled from france, spanish and portuguese citizens are being ordered to leave belgium because they are considered an excessive burden on the state, judicial officers in the united kingdom are being given government rewards in vouchers, depending on the number of foreign nationals they manage to expel from their country, and these are just some of the images of the picture we have of the european union today. the dream of free movement is turning into a nightmare, and the reason is very simple. it is austerity, austerity which corrodes everything and which places an unbelievable burden on these citizens when they leave their countries out of necessity because they cannot find work there. but the other side of the mirror is the golden visa, because after all in this european union it is also accepted that there can be free movement and residence in the countries, provided that citizens can pay for it. we can't accept that. this is a very, very unfortunate picture of the state the union has reached.
in writing. - i approve this report because i reject completely any proposal to limit the number of migrants in the european union, as this would be a breach of the principle of free movement of citizens enshrined in the treaty on european union. the mobility of workers contributes to the competitiveness of the economy and to limit it would be a clear setback in the process of european construction. i urge the commission and the member states to ensure the strict application of union law in order to guarantee equal treatment for all citizens of the european union, in this context, i believe that discrimination in respect of fundamental rights such as access to employment, equal working conditions, pay, dismissal conditions, social and tax benefits, etc., must be combated. i call on the national authorities in the member states not to allow any unjustified restrictions or obstacles to the right of workers to free movement, and any form of exploitation of workers.
in writing. - freedom of movement is one of the main achievements of european integration. it is important to preserve and strengthen it. in fact, some 60% of european citizens consider it the most important expression of the european project. all eu citizens are entitled to enjoy this right without exception. the european institutions and the member states have a common duty to protect it. mobile workers are net contributors to the social security systems of the country where they work. we cannot therefore link the right to freedom of movement for work purposes to allegedly illegitimate claims for social assistance and social security and to abuses of these benefits. any abuse must be combated within the framework of anti-fraud legislation, but never in breach of the principle of free movement in practice. i support the approach presented by the commission, with a list of actions aimed at helping national and local authorities to effectively apply the rules on free movement and prevent and combat abuses. it is important to denounce and condemn populist speeches without factual basis, which are intended to influence public opinion negatively. the fact is that so far the ec has never received evidence from any member state confirming the existence of a situation of systematic abuse of their social security systems.
in writing. − the fundamental right to free movement within the european union is one of the basic principles of the european integration process and one of the most important factors in its attractiveness. every citizen of a member state not only expects to be able to move freely within the union but also expects that his movement will be safe and protected by the states to which he travels. but free movement also implies the possibility of living and working in other states, and is much more than a simple facilitated right of visit. that said, it is not unreasonable for some member states to fear an excessive influx of immigrants into their countries and for this influx to put their social balance and the viability of their social support systems under stress or even into crisis and for them to seek, in the event of a potential conflict, to give priority to their own nationals. however, in normal circumstances, free movement within the union must prevail and this can have beneficial consequences for all the countries that are part of it, provided that this right is not exercised in an abusive manner and for illicit or illegitimate purposes that are contrary to the reason why it was created.
in writing. − the right to free movement is one of the four fundamental freedoms of the eu. but the movement of capital and goods on the one hand and of people on the other has always been governed by different rules and criteria. in the name of defending the same interests: those of capital, not those of the people. this resolution defends freedom of movement and strongly opposes calls for changes and restrictions on the free movement of citizens. fair and necessary criticism. we have always defended the principle of free movement of persons within the european area. our reasons are, however, quite different from some of those put forward in this resolution. the resolution says that the mobility of workers contributes to the competitiveness of the european economy - a good summary of a vision that looks at mobility (which forgets that today is, in the overwhelming majority of cases, a forced mobility, determined by the absence of prospects of work and a decent life in the country of origin) and that plans for it and allows it, to the exact extent, and only to the exact extent, that it serves the interests of capital. the resolution also contains positive aspects, such as the defence of equal treatment and non-discrimination for workers hosted by a member state.
in writing. − the right to free movement is one of the four fundamental freedoms of the eu, enshrined in the treaty on the functioning of the european union, as a cornerstone of european integration directly linked to eu citizenship. free movement is a core element of the eu's values, giving its citizens the choice of where they want to live and work and creating conditions for mobility and development in the labour market, education and other areas. nothing should therefore be done to alter these fundamental rights. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution calling on the member states to comply with the treaty provisions on eu legislation on free movement and to ensure respect for the principle of equality and the fundamental right to freedom of movement in all member states, and also calling on the commission and the member states to ensure the strict application of union legislation in order to ensure equal treatment of all eu workers and that they are not discriminated against in terms of access to employment, working conditions, remuneration, dismissal and social and tax benefits.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this joint document in which the european parliament calls on the member states to comply with the treaty provisions on free movement and to ensure respect for the principle of equality and the fundamental right to freedom of movement and which challenges the position taken by some european leaders in calling for changes and restrictions to the freedom of movement of citizens.
in writing. - this resolution defends freedom of movement and recognises the benefits it brings and strongly challenges the position taken by some european leaders in calling for changes and restrictions to the freedom of movement of citizens. however, the idea that the mobility of workers contributes to the competitiveness of the european economy is a hypothesis that masks the real causes of the movement of workers, such as the high levels of unemployment and the poor living conditions that a large proportion of eu workers face today. the document expresses the importance of the free movement of mobile workers for the development of the host country, especially in the areas of health care, agriculture and construction, areas where portugal has very high levels of emigration. the resolution also defends equal treatment between workers hosted by a member state and national workers with regard to contributions to the social protection system of the host member state, adopting the principle of equal treatment or non-discrimination between all citizens, assigning the same rights and obligations as nationals of the host country, correctly stating that all member states are free to decide on these principles and conditions.

in writing. - i approve this report, starting by expressing concern at the implications of the sale of european citizenship through a system recently created and made available by several member states of the european union. i recognise that residence and citizenship issues are a matter for member states; however, european identity and space are a concern for the union as a whole. i think it is important to stress that issues of the sale of citizenship have transnational implications and therefore concern all member states. i call on the member states to exercise caution in exercising their powers in this area, taking into account possible collateral effects which imply risks to the security of eu member states and may facilitate the commission of tax, financial or other illegal crimes. i would also remind you that european citizenship must not be turned into a commercial commodity.
in writing. - citizenship should not be granted lightly, let alone to those who do not prove themselves worthy of it. it's a circumstance we don't choose but it defines us and accompanies us, except in exceptional cases, throughout our lives. the idea has been wrongly conveyed that all programmes aimed at attracting foreign investment to member states of the union are motivated by a less scrupulous purpose and that they would allow the sale of the nationality of their respective countries to those who have the means to acquire it even to criminals. this assessment is not accurate and, instead of highlighting the good examples of balancing requirements and rights by the member states, it amalgamates the programmes, creating the same suspicion for all of them, which, in addition to undermining the attractiveness of those operating legitimately, will inevitably have negative consequences for the european economy as a whole. investment schemes which do not contend with schengen, which strictly respect european and national legislation and which do not discriminate positively against beneficiaries of the scheme in the event that they wish to obtain nationality should be welcomed and not demonized, especially in a europe where the economy is sluggish and jobs are lost almost every day.
in writing. - this resolution rightly criticises the granting of citizenship in some member states, the main criterion being the financial capacity of applicants. they grant citizenship rights to holders of capital to attract the development of economic activities (some of which, by their nature, may be involved in or give rise to fraud, tax evasion and avoidance and money laundering). this is a form of granting rights in keeping with the eu's emigration policy and its discriminatory, elitist and repressive character of workers with lower qualifications and training and without means, favouring all those who can somehow give profits to big capital. and that is not and could not be recognised in this resolution, hence a certain hypocrisy in the criticisms made here. we voted in favour of the first paragraph of this resolution because we too condemn these practices and the legislation which allows them. but there are aspects of this resolution that we clearly distance ourselves from. the concept of european citizenship is a very controversial and artificial concept, with real objectives that contradict many of the stated objectives, always wrapped in the cellophane of supposed rights, which are faced in practice every day.
in writing. - despite the vote in favour, i would point out that the maltese case has nothing whatsoever to do with the portuguese case. it is a definitive sale of nationality, contrary to all the principles of solidarity between states, which should be a disgrace to europe. in portugal, there is a common investment-raising process with most other countries, granting a temporary residence visa for a period of one year, renewable for two further periods of two years each, in return for investment in companies, job creation or purchase of real estate worth more than eur 500 000, all preceded by the necessary european consultation process and verification of the non-conviction of offenses with a sentence of more than one year for applicants.
in writing. − considering that there are concerns on the part of some member states about the creation of conditions for the acquisition of european citizenship by third-country nationals in circumstances which favour the wealthiest and without regard to the normal criteria for the granting of citizenship, the european parliament voted this resolution which states that european citizenship is one of the eu's greatest achievements and that, according to the eu treaties, residence and citizenship issues are the exclusive competence of the member states. however, parliament expressed concern that this form of citizenship, as in the case of malta, and any other national system which might involve the definitive sale, direct or indirect, of european citizenship, would undermine the very idea of european citizenship. i therefore voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.

in writing. - the proposal to amend regulation 2368/2002 aims to allow greenland to participate in the kimberley process, a certification scheme for rough diamonds. for the purposes of the certification scheme, greenland would be considered eu territory for the purposes of the kimberley process certification scheme and would be prohibited from accepting imports or exports of rough diamonds from or outside the eu territory without a valid certificate. i welcome this inclusion, which is a further step towards bringing that country closer to the union and means that it will be included in a certification system which is considered appropriate.
in writing. - the purpose of this proposal for a regulation is to include greenland in the application of the kimberley process certification system. the objective is to enable greenland's participation in the kimberley process certification scheme (kpcs) for international trade in rough diamonds through its cooperation with the european union. the scheme provided for in the proposal allows for the import and export of rough diamonds between greenland and the european union, as well as between greenland and other participants in the certification scheme, provided that all imports and exports of rough diamonds are verified and, as regards exports, certified by the union authorities. the kimberley process (pk) is a joint initiative of governments, industry and civil society to end the trade in war diamonds - rough diamonds used by rebel movements to finance conflicts against legitimate governments. i voted in favour of the rapporteur's position.
in writing. - council regulation (ec) no 2368/2002 on the application of the kimberley process certification system to international trade in rough diamonds establishes a community system for the certification and control of imports and exports of rough diamonds. greenland is not part of the eu territory but is included in the list of overseas countries and territories. the council decision lays down the rules and procedures enabling greenland to participate in the kimberley process certification scheme for international trade in rough diamonds through its cooperation with the eu. this association would strengthen economic relations between the eu and greenland in the diamond sector and, it is also said, contribute to greenland's economic development. consequently, greenland will be subject to compliance with the provisions of the kimberley process. regulation (ec) no 2368/2002 should therefore be amended to allow for the entry into force of the council decision and in particular to ensure the inclusion of greenland in the certification scheme. since the proposal originated in the member state concerned (denmark) and is the result of its sovereign choice, we do not object.

in writing. - the kimberley process certification scheme is an initiative that emerged within the united nations in 2003 and brings together voluntarily governments, industry and civil society, with the aim of ending the trade in so-called blood diamonds from conflict and used to finance them. this kimberley process has 54 members, representing 81 countries, who undertake to import and export diamonds between the participating countries by issuing a certificate which should accompany the transactions. greenland has used its status as an overseas territory of the union to participate in the kimberley process, as only countries can issue the certificate. i am voting in favour of this report, which will provide another source of wealth for the territory and the people of greenland.

in writing. - the cape town agreement of 2012 on the implementation of the provisions of the protocol of 1993 relating to the international convention on torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment of 1977 was adopted in october 2012 at a diplomatic conference convened by the international maritime organisation (imo). the agreement should allow the application of the torremolinos international convention for the safety of fishing vessels, signed in 1977, and the 1993 protocol thereto, which have never entered into force because of the insufficient number of states which have ratified the convention and the protocol thereto. the torremolinos convention and the protocol of 1993 thereto lay down safety standards relating, inter alia, to life-saving equipment, radio communications, fire protection, machinery and electrical installations, as well as specific requirements for seagoing fishing vessels of 24 metres in length or more. i voted in favour because i agree with the cape town agreement, insofar as it should contribute to the promotion of safety of fishing vessels, and with the authorization for member states to sign, ratify or accede to the agreement as appropriate.
in writing. - the international maritime organisation (imo) estimates that some 24 000 people lose their lives every year in the fishing sector, and the safety of fishing vessels is one of the relevant factors in minimising this scourge. this report welcomes the cape town agreement concerning the implementation of the provisions of the torremolinos international convention on the safety of fishing vessels, adopted in october 2012 at the imo, and should allow for the implementation of the convention on the safety of fishing vessels, which never entered into force due to the insufficient number of states that have ratified the convention and the protocol thereto. this convention lays down safety standards for, inter alia, life-saving equipment, radio communications, fire protection, machinery and electrical installations, and minimum requirements for seagoing fishing vessels of 24 metres in length or more. the agreement allows member states to exempt vessels from their flag if they consider it unreasonable or impractical to do so, taking into account the type of vessel, the weather conditions and the absence of any danger to navigation. the inspection and survey regime has also been tightened up and some of the surveys have become compulsory.

in writing. - the purpose of this report is to approve the draft council decision authorising the member states to sign, ratify or accede to the cape town agreement of 2012 on the implementation of the 1977 torremolinos international convention and its 1993 protocol on safety of maritime fishing vessels. the international maritime organisation (imo) estimates that around 24 000 people die each year in the fishing industry worldwide, which reinforces the importance of the entry into force of the torremolinos protocol, which lays down safety standards for life-saving equipment, radio communications, fire protection, machinery and electrical installations, and other specific requirements for fishing vessels of 24 metres in length or more. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the entry into force of the cape town agreement could make a decisive contribution to the safety of fishing vessels of 24 metres or more in length and could serve as a basis for resolving the safety issues of fishing vessels of less than 24 metres in length, which constitute the overwhelming majority of the fishing fleet in the european union.
in writing. - the cape town agreement allows the application of the torremolinos international convention for the safety of ships, which lays down safety standards for life-saving equipment, radio communications, fire protection, machinery and electrical installations, and the requirements for seagoing fishing vessels of 24 metres in length or more. this agreement amends certain provisions of the torremolinos protocol in order to introduce greater flexibility as regards the timing of the application of the measures. it also introduces a stricter inspection and survey regime, making initial, annual and intermediate surveys compulsory. since the european union is not a party to the convention of the international maritime organisation, it cannot be a party to the cape town agreement. but on the other hand, member states cannot decide autonomously whether to ratify the draft agreement, since it is a matter of exclusive competence of the union (article 3 (2) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union), unless the council authorises it, after approval by parliament, on the basis of a commission proposal. the rapporteur therefore encourages the adoption of this document, which will allow member states to sign, ratify or accede to the agreement.

in writing. - the eu cannot achieve its policy objectives if the member states do not effectively apply eu law, and it is the ec, as guardian of the treaties, which has the power and the duty to supervise its application and to bring infringement proceedings against member states which do not comply. i am glad that the number of infringement cases has decreased over the last few years. unfortunately, the same was not true of late transposition procedures, which increased by 60%. petitions submitted by eu citizens also show that there are frequent and widespread cases of incomplete transposition or misapplication of eu law, with an increase in complaints in this regard, with italy, spain and germany being the most targeted countries in the areas of fundamental rights, the environment, the internal market and property rights. it must become a real political priority. citizens, businesses and organisations need, especially in the context of the current economic situation, a simple, predictable and reliable regulatory framework to foster confidence and economic growth. the eu pilot initiative could be an added value in solving problems, avoiding the initiation of formal infringement proceedings; however, a greater degree of transparency is needed in the whole process.
in writing. - the european union cannot achieve its objectives if the member states do not implement their legislation in a concrete and effective way. member states are responsible for the correct application of the acquis and must transpose directives correctly and in a timely manner. the report analyses key aspects of the application of union law and provides an overview of the main strategic issues currently facing the union. we must not fail to assess critically and in a more systematic and consistent way the fundamental aspects of the application of european law, its necessity, adequacy and effectiveness, its compliance with the principle of subsidiarity and the respect for the exclusive competences of the member states.
- the number of new infringement cases has decreased over the last few years, with the commission opening 2900 such cases in 2009, 2100 in 2010 and 1775 in 2011. there was, however, an increase in late transposition cases during these years (1185 in 2011, 855 in 2010 and 531 in 2009). i note that the four areas with the highest incidence of late transposition cases are the environment (17 per cent), the internal market (15 per cent), transport (15 per cent) and taxation (12 per cent). it should be noted that article 17 teu defines the fundamental role of the commission as guardian of the treaties, with the power and duty to supervise the application of eu law and, in particular, to bring infringement proceedings against member states which fail to fulfil any of their obligations under the treaties. there is a decreasing number of infringement cases (60,4%) closed in 2011 before reaching the court of justice, compared to 88% in 2010. i agree that it is essential to continue to monitor closely the actions of the member states, given that some of the petitions to the european parliament and complaints to the commission concern problems which persist even after the procedure has been closed.

in writing. - this commission proposal is of the utmost importance for freedom of movement and the strengthening of european citizenship. indeed, according to eurostat estimates, in 2011 there were around 12 million union citizens residing in a member state other than their home state. many more still reside temporarily in another eu member state - for example, for study, work or simply for holidays. it is necessary to eliminate, or at least reduce, the bureaucratic difficulties and obstacles experienced by these citizens in contacting the administration of the host member state. in addition, such contacts with the administration are further complicated by the fact that it is often necessary to overcome additional obstacles when documents from other member states are presented, for example certified translations or an apostille may be required. these are formalities which, in addition to being very time-consuming, can also become, in some cases, quite onerous, both for citizens and for businesses. i voted in favour of this regulation, which aims to reduce bureaucracy and simplify. it should be noted that this regulation concerns only formalities and not the recognition of facts or legal relationships originating in other member states.
in writing. - the purpose of this regulation is to reduce crossborder formalities in respect of documents in order to facilitate the free movement of citizens. it does not require a member state to recognise the content of a document from another member state, but states do not require additional formalities for the presentation of the document, for example in the form of a certified translation. the rapporteur considers the commission proposal to apply the regulation only to certain public documents, in particular those relating to civil status, to be insufficient. it therefore proposes that this regulation cover personal identification documents, certificates of education, proof of disability, as well as tax and social security documents. the commission is proposing that simple copies of a document be accepted and, in the case of certified copies, that they be valid in all member states. the commission also proposes the creation of 10 new multilingual eu forms covering what it considers to be the most frequent problematic cases: name, parentage, adoption, divorce, dissolution of a registered partnership, nationality, lack of a criminal record, residence, level of education and disability. we believe that these measures are designed to make life easier and simpler for citizens travelling to a member state other than their own, so we voted in favour.

in writing. - i approve of this report, considering that the market abuse directive, adopted in early 2003, has not achieved its objective of strengthening investor confidence and market integrity, even though it has introduced a comprehensive framework to combat insider dealing and market manipulation. the commission's impact assessment, on the other hand, emphasises that the sanctions currently in force in relation to the fight against market abuse are not effective and sufficiently dissuasive, which results in an ineffective implementation of the directive. in addition, the definition of what constitutes a criminal offence of insider dealing or market manipulation differs considerably from one member state to another. since market abuse can take place across borders, this divergence is detrimental to the internal market and leaves a certain margin for market abusers to seek the most favourable forum shopping. the impact assessment concluded that it was essential to impose on member states the introduction of criminal sanctions for the most serious market abuse offences in order to ensure the effective implementation of the union's market abuse policy.
in writing. - this report aims to combat insider dealing and market manipulation, which will help restore confidence in eu financial markets and increase investor protection. there is a great deal of fragmentation in the european union's legislation on this matter. this report will harmonise the rules to be applied in the 28 member states within two years, allowing for effective penalties for infringers across the eu. in serious cases of insider dealing and market manipulation, the sanction to be applied may involve a maximum prison sentence of not less than four years. in the case of unlawful disclosure of inside information, a maximum penalty of imprisonment of not less than two years. this report will contribute to maintaining the integrity of securities markets and to the confidence of those involved in their functioning. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - this proposal for a european commission directive aims to combat insider dealing and market manipulation, in order to restore confidence in eu financial markets and increase investor protection. due to differences in legislation across eu countries, these bad practices often escaped effective punishment, leading to significant losses for investors and distortions for the real economy. in this regard, this directive harmonises the rules to be applied in all 28 member states and ensures that within a maximum of two years, this legislation will be harmonised and will allow for the application of effective sanctions to infringers throughout the eu. the penalties to be applied may, in serious cases of insider dealing and market manipulation, involve a maximum prison sentence of not less than four years and, in cases of unlawful disclosure of inside information, a maximum prison sentence of not less than two years. i am voting in favour of this legislative proposal because i believe that it contributes in a positive and active way to maintaining the integrity of securities markets and to the confidence of the players in the functioning of securities markets.
in writing. - the introduction of criminal sanctions to combat market abuse is an important innovation and a valuable reinforcement of the instruments to combat abusive behaviour. the current definition of what constitutes a criminal offence of insider dealing or market manipulation differs considerably between states and, since market abuse situations may involve more than one state, this divergence is detrimental to the internal market and leaves some scope for market abusers to seek the most favourable forum. it is therefore important to introduce uniform criminal sanctions for the most serious market abuse offences in order to ensure the effective implementation of the union's market abuse policy.
in writing. - this proposal for a european commission directive aims to combat insider dealing and market manipulation, in order to restore confidence in eu financial markets and increase investor protection. due to differences in legislation across eu countries, these bad practices often escaped effective punishment, leading to significant losses for investors and distortions for the real economy. in this regard, this directive harmonises the rules to be applied in all 28 member states and ensures that within a maximum of two years, this legislation will be harmonised and will allow for the application of effective sanctions to infringers throughout the eu. the penalties to be applied may, in serious cases of insider dealing and market manipulation, be a maximum of a four-year prison sentence and, in the case of unlawful disclosure of inside information, a maximum of a two-year prison sentence. i am voting in favour of this legislative proposal because i believe that it makes a positive and active contribution to maintaining the integrity of securities markets and to the confidence of those involved in the functioning of securities markets.
in writing. - as defined in this report, criminal sanctions for insider dealing and market manipulation have a limited impact, demonstrating that the aim of this proposal for a directive is above all to harmonise sanctions so as not to distort competition in the eu's internal market. the majority of meps do not support the conditions for dealing seriously with illegal behaviour - often in the criminal sphere - on financial markets. the increasing financialisation of the economy, the free movement of capital and financial speculation which is a fundamental component of the capital markets are never called into question. the turbulence of the financial markets is the inevitable result of these processes and the insatiable greed of big capital for profits, trying to counteract the tendency of the profit rate to fall. the backlash against financial speculation is reaching an unprecedented level, particularly with public debt, with the consequence of the destruction of social and labour rights of a civilizational dimension in countries such as portugal. thus, by excluding monetary activities and the management of public debt from its scope, some of the most impactful activities are left out, which only shows that with this directive, crime will continue to pay off.
in writing. - investors who trade on the basis of inside information and manipulate markets by spreading false or misleading information can now avoid penalties by taking advantage of the differences in the laws of the 28 eu member states. in some countries, the authorities do not have effective sanctioning powers, while in others there is no provision for criminal sanctions for certain offences related to insider dealing and market manipulation. the new directive, already agreed with national governments, sets out a set of eu-wide rules to ensure that criminal sanctions are applied to insider dealing and market manipulation activities. member states should also impose criminal penalties for instigation and complicity in market abuse and for attempting to commit such offences. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the mccarthy report on criminal sanctions for market abuse (in financial markets) because this legislative initiative has become necessary to combat such serious criminal acts as the manipulation of euribor rates. the market economy is not a laissez faire economy. it is a regulated economy, whose rules need to be defended, including by criminal repression in the most serious cases. as the famous sarbanes-oxley act of 30 july 2002 in the united states has shown, only criminal law can adequately defend the economic and social values on which the market economy is based. moreover, if there is a single eu market for financial services, a minimum of common rules at union level is required. a market without frontiers requires a european economic criminal law, for which there is a constitutional basis in the treaties (tfeu, article 83 (1) and (2)). the principle of subsidiarity clearly does not apply here.
in writing. - this proposal is based on the market abuse directive which introduced a comprehensive framework to combat insider dealing and market manipulation, together known as market abuse. the proposal aims to increase investor confidence and market integrity, and to prohibit practices such as the dissemination of false information or rumours and the pursuit of activities that raise prices to abnormal levels in the markets. however, this proposal, in addition to following this approach, also adopts the approach of ensuring the use of criminal law for the effective implementation of eu policies in the interests of the principles of necessity, proportionality and subsidiarity. in view of all this, i voted in favour of this proposal on criminal sanctions for insider dealing and market manipulation.
in writing. - i know . directive 2003/6/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 28 january 2003 on insider dealing and market manipulation has completed and updated the legal framework of the european union to protect market integrity. i am in favour of this directive which lays down minimum standards for criminal sanctions for the most serious infringements committed, in particular insider dealing and market manipulation. member states shall ensure that competent authorities have the power to detect and investigate market abuse situations and that appropriate administrative measures or administrative penalties are taken against persons responsible for breaching the national rules implementing that directive. i therefore vote in favour of this report, which ensures greater integrity of the financial markets in the european union and greater protection for investors.
in writing. - this report is more of a statement of good faith based on the good faith with which some financial activities are done. the proposals for criminal sanctions for insider dealing and market manipulation have limited effect. the report does not create the conditions necessary to deal seriously with illegal behaviour - in many cases criminal - in the financial markets. the increasing financialisation of the economy, the free movement of capital and the financial speculation which this enables on the capital markets are never called into question. the fact that the origins of the turbulence in the financial markets are the inevitable result of capitalist speculation, based on the financialization of the economy and the strengthening of the conditions of global exploitation with a view to obtaining maximum profit margins, is never mentioned. it is assumed that the problems are rooted, solely and essentially, in greed or in the breach of rules by some managers. it is the logic of speculation that must be eradicated. to assume that sanctions can correct the errors of speculative activity is to agree with it. and we won't accept it.

in writing. - the union comprises an area of justice, with respect for the different legal systems and traditions of the member states, and it is therefore essential to improve the quality, independence and effectiveness of national judicial systems in order to enable citizens, businesses, judges and authorities to trust, respect, recognise and enforce decisions taken by the judicial system of another member state, thus contributing to greater trust, sustainable growth and social stability. the eu justice scoreboard should therefore provide objective, reliable and comparable data on the functioning of judicial systems in all member states, in order to help the eu and the member states to improve their effectiveness. it should help identify possible gaps and best practices in order to support both member states and the eu institutions in developing more effective justice policies with a view to developing independent, fast, easily accessible and cost-effective justice systems. it is undoubtedly a positive step towards the development of a genuine european area of justice that can meet the expectations of citizens and contribute to sustainable growth, based on the rule of law and other values on which the union is founded.

the european project in which we are involved was born on the basis of steel, with the creation of the european coal and steel community in 1951 with the aim of integrating and coordinating the production and distribution of steel and coal. the steel industry remains essential for the whole european industrial sector, in particular for the automotive, construction, mechanical, electrical and renewable energy industries. as the cornerstone of the european industrial chain, the commission presented an action plan to strengthen and develop a sector which has suffered setbacks as a result of the economic crisis. this requires a transparent energy market with fair costs, allowing the sector to compete with its international partners. we must also monitor the market to prevent illegal agreements, the abusive control that some countries have over the flow of raw materials. finally, i would stress the need for a clear commitment to r & d, thus differentiating itself from its competitors, and a comprehensive strategy involving environmental protection, energy and competitiveness. i am in favour of this report because we need an industry which knows how to find new market sectors and which is able to position itself globally.

- seasonal workers from third countries are periodically needed in certain sectors of activity in the eu, such as agriculture and tourism, where many work in precarious conditions. according to commission figures, some 100 000 seasonal workers enter the eu every year. i therefore think it is very important that the rights and duties of these workers are clarified, as well as a set of rules that can make this labour exchange profitable for both parties. it seems reasonable to me that the admission of a seasonal worker to an eu country should be made conditional on the existence of a valid employment contract or a binding offer of employment specifying the place and type of work, the duration of the employment, the remuneration and the number of hours of work per week or month, the duration of paid holidays and, where appropriate, other working conditions.

in writing. - this report aims to reduce the exploitation of seasonal workers and their working and living conditions. this view, while improving the existing legislative framework, is still reductive, impregnated with a utilitarian approach to migrants and lacking in solidarity, since the eu uses these workers while their work is useful and returns them to their countries of origin after they have become expendable. that is why we have reservations about this report. however, the directive establishes a rapid procedure for the admission of seasonal workers, provides for the conditions governing the granting of a residence and work permit valid for a maximum period of six months per calendar year and lays down the rights of seasonal workers, ensuring equal treatment to safeguard wage and working conditions. admission will depend on the existence of an employment contract or a binding job offer specifying the salary to be paid and other working conditions. it also provides for sanctions against employers, taking into account the vulnerable situation of seasonal workers, in particular as regards compensation if their authorisation has been withdrawn because their employer has failed to comply with its legal obligations.
in writing. - this directive guarantees a set of rights for seasonal workers from third countries. the new rules ensure that these workers are treated equally with nationals of the host european country as regards working conditions and the right to decent housing. the aim is to prevent their exploitation in the eu and, at the same time, to prevent a temporary stay from becoming permanent. the admission of a seasonal worker to an eu country will depend on the existence of a valid employment contract or a binding job offer specifying the place and type of work, the duration of the employment, the remuneration and the number of hours worked weekly or monthly, the duration of paid holidays and, where appropriate, other working conditions. seasonal workers will be entitled to equal treatment with nationals of the host country with regard, for example, to the minimum age for admission to employment and to working conditions relating to pay, dismissals, working hours, holidays and leave, and to health and safety requirements at the workplace. that is why i am voting in favour.

in writing. - unlike weapons of mass destruction and landmines, the trade in conventional weapons is not the subject of any global legally binding instrument. the arms trade treaty (att) aims to fill this gap. the arms trade treaty establishes a common international standard for the regulation of international trade in conventional arms and, to some extent, in munitions, related parts and components. the treaty also aims to prevent and eradicate the illicit trade in such weapons. let us hope that the countries which have not acceded to this treaty, namely north korea, iran and syria, will do so later.

in writing. - the united nations arms trade treaty aims to regulate the international trade in conventional arms and to eliminate the illicit arms trade. the treaty also requires parties to control exports of conventional arms to ensure that they are not used for terrorist purposes or in violation of human rights. since the union is not a party to the united nations arms trade treaty, the council will adopt a decision authorising the member states to ratify the said treaty as regards matters falling within the exclusive competence of the union, and the european parliament, with my positive vote, has shown a favourable position to this.
in writing. - i approve of this report, starting by stressing that the long-term success of the arms trade treaty regime depends on the participation of as many countries as possible, including the main actors in the field of the international arms trade. it is welcome that most of the member states of the united nations have already signed the treaty. i urge other member states to follow suit and ratify the same as soon as possible. i urge the european external action service to add to its objectives in external affairs and to the set of subjects to be included in bilateral agreements a call for third countries to accede to the treaty in question. at the same time, however, i stress that illegal or unregulated arms transfers cause human suffering and fuel armed conflict, instability, terrorist attacks and corruption with consequences for socioeconomic development, violation of democratic order and the rule of law, human rights law and international humanitarian law.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of this report because the european union has increased responsibilities in this area, not only because it is a pioneer in adopting a mandatory system for monitoring the trade and transfer of arms, military equipment and technology to third countries (the common position adopted in 2008), but also because there is still much to be done between member states to ensure transparency and compliance with publicity in the arms trade.
in writing. - at a time when the arms race is being revived, with increased military spending and investment in new weapons by the us, nato and the eu - with the hypocritical talk of their reduction - this resolution underlines the importance of this and other arms reduction treaties. the resolution raises concerns about the vagueness of definitions and the need for member states to apply more precise and restrictive legislation to combat arms trafficking and their use by organised crime or other criminal activities. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. we cannot but stress that the regulation of the import, export and transfer of arms will be all the more relevant if it is accompanied by a process of multilateral and reciprocal disarmament, in particular the dismantling of the huge existing nuclear arsenals, starting with the world's largest nuclear powers - such as the usa - and the complete destruction of chemical and biological weapons.
in writing. - the conclusion of the negotiations on this treaty under the auspices of the united nations after seven years of protracted negotiations was important. it is a legally binding arms trade treaty, dealing with the international trade in conventional arms. i hope that this treaty will establish common international regulatory standards, with the highest possible level of demand, for the international trade in conventional arms in order to prevent and eradicate the illicit trade in conventional arms, with the aim of contributing to peace, security and stability at international and regional level. effective implementation of the treaty could make a significant contribution to greater respect for human rights and international humanitarian law throughout the world.

in writing. - i approve of this report, given that the commission proposes to eliminate the rule of the lower duty in anti-dumping cases where there are structural distortions at the level of raw materials and in all anti-subsidy cases, on the grounds that such elimination will improve the effectiveness of the instruments. however, it remains difficult to define where this conclusion arises. in accordance with the wto, dumping per se is not illegal, only dumping that causes injury is considered illegal. the commission therefore concluded that the union industry suffered material injury within the meaning of article 3 (5) of the basic regulation. in addition, the lack of a precise definition of structural distortions at the raw material level may prove problematic. the commission has so far not put forward a uniform definition, which has led to speculation. it has been suggested that the definition should be determined on an ad hoc basis, but labour and energy costs should be included in this concept.

in writing. - the proposal we are voting on today aims to modernise the anti-dumping and anti-subsidy regulations and involves four key changes: (i) the elimination of the lesser duty rule in anti-dumping cases where there are structural distortions at the level of raw materials and in all anti-subsidy cases; (ii) the obligation for union producers to cooperate in ex officio investigations; (iii) the reimbursement of duties collected during expiry reviews; and (iv) the two-week notice in relation to the introduction of provisional duties, commonly referred to as the transport clause. those amendments are intended to increase the effectiveness of the instruments, reduce the threat of retaliation by third countries and increase transparency and predictability.

in writing. - this report aims to amend regulation (ec) no 1224/2009 establishing a community regime for monitoring compliance with the rules of the common fisheries policy (cfp), in the light of the changes in the comitology resulting from the treaty of lisbon and the new distribution of legal powers and the reorganisation of the powers of the european institutions. this requires the harmonisation of european legislation, which implies the choice and allocation of the legal instruments established in a hierarchical manner by the treaty, namely implementing acts, which are essentially technical in nature; delegated acts, which allow the european commission a margin of appreciation; and the codecision procedure, which is a more political procedure. this realignment of powers and competences requires increased vigilance by the council and the european parliament, which must limit the attribution of legal acts and exercise regular and effective control over their application. i voted in favour of this report because i consider that the rapporteur's proposals contribute to effective compliance with the cfp rules, maintaining a reasonable balance in the distribution of these powers and competences, without, however, compromising the spirit of the legislative acts, and limiting the delegation of powers to the european commission for a period of three years.

in writing. - airlines too often fail to recognise the rights of passengers in the event of denied boarding or of considerable delays, cancellations or problems with luggage. this is because there are still gaps in existing european legislation, but mainly because of the incomplete and inconsistent application of these regulations by carriers and national authorities. this situation creates legal uncertainty and confusion for both the industry and passengers, who are not properly informed about their rights, and the number of passengers claiming their rights or actually compensated is very low. i therefore support this proposal for a revision of the 1997 and 2004 regulations, which clarifies the basic principles and passenger rights that have been the subject of dispute and aims to strengthen passenger rights in general, in particular the right to quality of service, the protection of economic interests and information. it should also ensure that air carriers provide a high level of protection in the event of disruption to travel and that they can operate under uniform conditions in a liberalised market.
in writing. - the present proposal aims to keep pace with transport developments and to strengthen air passengers' rights. the proposals aim to ensure that (i) the role of national enforcement bodies is better defined, having been extended to cover baggage complaints; (ii) a clear time-bound complaint procedure with clearly defined functions for a new body responsible for handling complaints; (iii) new provisions for cases of denied boarding, missed connecting flights or significant delay; (iv) a non-exhaustive list of extraordinary circumstances to clarify cases where airlines are exempt from compensation; (v) a strengthened obligation for air carriers to inform passengers in an appropriate and timely manner; (vi) new provisions on the carriage of mobility equipment and musical instruments. whatever the means of transport used, passengers have the right to a quality and safe service, which is why i welcome the intention to introduce improvements in legislation on passenger rights in air transport.
in writing. - the report aims to amend regulation (ec) no 261/2004 laying down common rules for the compensation and assistance of air passengers in the event of denied boarding and of cancellation or long delay of flights, and regulation (ec) no 2027/97 on air carrier liability for the carriage of passengers and their baggage. the amendments to those regulations are due to significant changes in the aviation sector in recent years, some of which have resulted in an increase in unfair practices and reduced quality of service, with negative consequences for passengers due to existing gaps in legislation and its uneven application in the member states, as well as difficulties for passengers to assert their rights against non-compliant air carriers, whose statistics show that only a small percentage of those injured are effectively compensated. i voted in favour of this report because i consider that the rapporteur's proposals in general promote an improvement in the level of protection of the rights of consumers as air transport users, in particular in the event of denied boarding for not having completed part of the journey, the right to compensation and access to basic hygiene and health conditions during flight delays.
in writing. - the entry into force of regulation (ec) no 261/2004 has led to a number of complaints and uncertainties, resulting from the non-uniform application in the member states, with regard to compensation and assistance to passengers and in the event of refusal and cancellation or delay of flights. the european court itself has been called upon to clarify numerous situations which show how difficult it is for passengers to assert their rights against air carriers. the amendments will improve consumer protection by removing a certain legal uncertainty. i would like to highlight the changes to the right to compensation in the event of long delays, to the rights in relation to connecting flights, to denied boarding, to protection in the event of multiple flight cancellations, to the mandatory contingency plans for airport entities, to the list of criteria defining extraordinary circumstances, to the right to accommodation, to the right to information, to price transparency, to checked baggage, to lost, damaged or delayed baggage, to the complaint procedures and to delays on the tarmac. a report which benefits passengers in the union by creating an area of safety and consumer protection.
