on behalf of the s&d group. as has been said here, about 140 million women have already been subjected to fgm. every year, 3 million girls and teenagers are mutilated. one every six minutes. in the past, mutilation was done around the age of eight or nine. now, the victims are only 2 and 3 years old. this is the sad reality in third countries, in many countries, but it is also the case in certain communities in some countries of the european union. in mali, for example, 98 percent of women and girls are mutilated, in a ritual that involves the victim's family, including the parents themselves. pressure to subject girls to fgm comes from families and communities, both in the countries of origin and in europe. coordinated efforts are needed to put an end to this scourge. fgm is a serious violation of human rights. member states cannot tolerate criminal practices which, in the name of a purported tradition, endanger the integrity and physical and psychological health of women. women and adolescent girls who undergo fgm suffer very serious consequences: death from bleeding or infection, transmission of diseases such as aids, hepatitis, and tetanus, incontinence, sexual dysfunction, and serious complications during pregnancy and childbirth, to name a few. and then there are the devastating psychological effects, similar to the effects of rape. states should therefore promote social and psychological support services and take measures to improve health conditions, including sexual and reproductive health, in order to assist girls who are subject to this type of violence. there is much to be done: we have an obligation to do more for these young people, for these teenagers.
in writing. - i approve this report because i believe that the aviation sector has undergone significant changes in recent years, associated with an increase in the number of passengers and flights on the liberalised european market. however, this overall positive development was accompanied to some extent by unfair practices and a reduction in the quality of services, with negative consequences for passengers. in addition, since the entry into force of the regulation in 2004, problems have arisen from the different interpretations resulting from the shadow zones and gaps in the current regulation, from the non-uniform application in the member states and from the difficulties experienced by passengers in asserting their rights when air carriers do not comply with the legislation. parliament had already expressed its views on several of these points in the context of its resolutions adopted in 2012. i can however highlight several elements of the commission's proposal as a step forward in the application of air passenger rights.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of this report to increase the levels of protection, it must not be possible to prevent passengers from boarding a flight leg of a return ticket on the grounds that they have not made the return journey or have not used all the segments of the ticket. manufacturers should draw up an eu declaration of conformity in order to provide the information required by this directive on the conformity of a measuring instrument with this directive and with other applicable union harmonisation legislation.
in writing. - air carriers are expected to have a contact person at each airport at which they operate to provide information and assistance to passengers in the event of flight cancellations or delays, denied boarding and lost or delayed baggage. passengers may also address their complaints to this contact person directly at the airport. it is argued that the information on baggage allowance will have to be clearly indicated at the initial stage of the booking process and at check-in. the european parliament is of the opinion that passengers should be able to carry essential personal items or belongings such as coats and hand luggage on board the aircraft, free of charge, in addition to the maximum allowable cabin baggage, including at least one standard-sized bag with items purchased at the airport. in addition, in the event of cancellation or delay of departure, the air carrier shall inform passengers of the situation, including the cause of the disturbance, as soon as this information is available and in any event no later than 30 minutes after the scheduled departure time. the proposal obliges airlines to ensure the re-routing of passengers.
in writing. the commission has also adopted a proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. this amendment reveals improvements in the protection of air passengers' rights, in particular the guarantee of protection of their legitimate interests, the right to quality of service, the right to protection of their economic interests and the right to information. the commission proposal did not ensure a high level of consumer protection in some areas, such as the reinforcement of the right to compensation for long delays and the total ban on the so-called no-show clause, preventing boarding from being unjustifiably refused and passengers who do not use the full amount of the transport ticket or even from being charged any additional fees for the same. it also includes duties on airlines to inform consumers about hand and hold baggage, and clarification of concepts used to exempt airlines from liability for damage, in particular the so-called 'extraordinary circumstances' so often used for their ambiguity. we voted in favour.
in writing. - the adoption of this new proposal will give air passengers new rights in the field of assistance, re-routing and information whenever they are detained at airports. the rules, which have yet to be negotiated with national governments, also strengthen the right to compensation for passengers who suffer long waits or baggage problems. the less clear aspects of the current legislation need to be deleted. the adoption of this report will make this possible in matters such as better airport assistance, baggage allowance in the cabin, delay, cancellation, rerouting, complaints and airline bankruptcy. that is why i am voting in favour.
mr president, the report we adopted here yesterday on a road map for energy and energy policy and climate change shows clearly the backwardness of the european institutions and parliament over the last five years. the european union considered itself the world leader in defending environmental issues and we managed yesterday, with great difficulty, to approve a report by a narrow majority which sets out only some of the fundamental and previously unquestionable targets in this house, namely on co2 emissions and on renewable energy. unfortunately, it seems that with the crisis all this has been called into question and the environment has been relegated to a secondary role. i voted in favour of this report, although it is much less ambitious than it should be, because i still believe that there can be no development unless we consider environmental and sustainability issues as an integral part of any model.
in writing. - i approve of this report, starting by noting that the share of wages in the low-carbon sector has declined less than in the 15 main polluting industries, especially in recent years. i therefore call for measures to be taken to allocate resources from the economic recovery plan to green, quality employment and sustainable growth. it stresses the need to support in particular small and medium-sized enterprises in creating quality green jobs for highly qualified workers as well as for the least qualified. i also stress the need to provide a platform for member states to coordinate their efforts and incentives in creating high quality green jobs and sustainable growth.
in writing. - i would first like to congratulate the rapporteur on the level of ambition reached in this resolution. the european energy and climate strategy must combine the protection of the planet and the fight against climate change with security of supply and the competitiveness of the economy. in order to achieve the proposed objectives, it is necessary to define a future framework which provides guarantees and greater certainty to investors and industry. this requires a medium- and long-term policy to encourage investment in science and innovation in order to reduce the costs of technologies. these policies allow the european union to lead by example in climate and energy, but it is essential to have a global agreement that reconciles planetary preservation, economic growth, poverty eradication and the sustainability of the well-being of present and future generations.
in writing. - as we approach 2020, it is important to think about the period ahead for a number of reasons: to get ahead in terms of international strategy, to build on the excellent work already done by the european commission, but above all to be able to have a real impact on the fight against climate change. at the same session we voted for financial support to deal with the increasingly frequent natural disasters. we must instead focus on work that can at least reduce the impact of these disasters, which often cost lives as well as money.
in writing. - the current climate and energy legal framework, with binding targets for the share of renewable energy, reducing energy consumption and ghg emissions, expires in 2020. we must therefore renew these three binding targets so that the efforts made so far are not wasted. i think a target of 40% for ghg reduction, 40% for energy efficiency and 30% for renewable energy by 2030 is a good compromise. the focus on renewables is a plus in terms of reducing dependence on fossil fuel imports, in terms of job creation, and in creating competitive low-carbon sectors. to continue along this path, i believe we must give clear signals to investors. finally, i believe that deepening the european energy network by encouraging greater interconnections between member states brings undeniable advantages, as well as increasing security of supply, improving intermittency management of renewables, diversifying supply, even leading to a reduction in energy costs.
in writing. - this report looks at the eu's climate and energy policy framework up to 2030, a subject which is prone to the usual rhetoric the need for job creation and economic recovery, a transition to a sustainable growth model, etc. and the usual contradictions. new targets are put forward, with the objectives of reducing greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions by 40% (based on 1990 emissions) and ensuring a 27% share for renewable energy. many have spoken of the lack of ambition of these goals. indeed, in the face of the wild climate rhetoric to which the eu has accustomed us, one would expect more. but numerical targets are worth what they are worth, and it is essential to assess the path to reaching them, the methods, instruments and criteria used. here the eu has long since made clear the way forward and this report insists on it: the carbon market which has been confirmed to be, besides ineffective, perverse. here, what matters and what prevails is business as usual... we support ambitious targets for reducing ghg emissions and for the transition to low-carbon technologies, but we do not share the apology for green capitalism which is once again made in this report.
in writing. - i did not vote in favour of the amendments to the delvaux/szymański report (on the 2030 climate and energy targets) on the exploitation of shale gas and on the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions to 50% compared to the 1990 level. as regards the first, there is no evidence that, with the appropriate safety guarantees, shale gas exploitation has intolerable negative environmental effects and there is no reason to disregard this energy source which is causing a significant reduction in energy costs in the usa. as for the second, although i am personally in favour of binding environmental targets, it seems to me that the proposed limit is overly ambitious and perhaps unrealistic (20% in 2020 to 50% in 2030). the union must maintain its leadership in reducing ghg emissions (co2 and others), but it must not be an isolated vanguard without followers in the rest of the world. in any case, a reasonable balance must be struck between environmental ambition and the competitiveness of the union's economy, which is already suffering from much higher energy costs than our direct competitors, such as the us.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on a 2030 framework for climate and energy policies in which the european parliament welcomes the commission's green paper on a 2030 framework for climate and energy policies and expects the european council to address these issues with ambitious, realistic and cost-efficient solutions. parliament hopes for flexible solutions that will maintain a sustainable competitive advantage for the european union, with its general and specialised energy know-how, and that will work both in the short and long term.
in writing. - i am in favour of a 40% reduction in greenhouse gases, 40% energy efficiency and 40% of energy from renewable sources. i believe that in portugal the renewable energy potential, particularly wind and solar, is still to be exploited and that this new impetus could boost economic growth and job creation in the area. however, it will be necessary to review the mechanisms for subsidising renewable energy as the technologies become more mature, to give a clear signal to investors of the strategy outlined and to deepen the european energy networks so that portugal has the possibility of discharging the electricity produced.
since the start of the economic and financial crisis, european public money that has been used to recapitalise european commercial banks represents 10% of all wealth produced in the european area. it represents, to give you an idea, twenty times the amount of the bailout allocated to portugal and on which absolutely cheap interest is being paid, but it is twenty times that bailout. so public money has been used to fund banking directly, being taken from work, from pensions, directly to the banking system. the governments and the commission are not interested in solving this problem, they are not interested in creating a common european bank resolution fund, in which banks pay for their own problems, and they are even less interested in defining a deposit guarantee system which could be common. and so this ends up being a farce, because there is no political will to tell the european citizens that it is the banks' turn to pay for their difficulties and that they have already paid more than they should. public money is used for growth, for promoting employment. it can no longer be used to save the financial system.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that it is in the interests of the community to create an institutional framework with a single resolution mechanism and a single resolution fund. this mechanism, complementary to the single supervisory mechanism proposed by the commission in september 2012, will allow for the centralisation of core banking crisis management competences and resources in the euro area and will lead to the creation of an integrated resolution mechanism at the european union level. this framework will be supported by the single resolution board, the national resolution authorities of the participating member states and the european commission, which raises very important institutional issues which should be brought to the attention of the committee on constitutional affairs and forwarded to all members of the european parliament.
in the case of the united kingdom, the commission has already taken the initiative in the form of a proposal for a regulation on the european banking authority. this proposal, which is one of the fundamental building blocks of banking union, aims to break the contagion link between sovereign and banking debt once and for all, protecting the taxpayers of the member states from the financial problems of their banking institutions. parliament supports the creation of a single resolution fund, financed by bank money, which should be operational as soon as possible in order to safeguard the health and stability of the european financial system. the commission is also proposing that the solution to bank resolution in the eu be kept within the community method and legislative framework. i therefore support parliament's decision to postpone the final vote on this report until the negotiations with the council have been concluded, in order to safeguard the stability and soundness of financial markets and the interests of european citizens and taxpayers.

in writing. - the legislative initiative on the single bank resolution mechanism and the corresponding resolution fund - on which the report by elisa ferreira was voted on today - is certainly one of the most important legislative instruments that mark the union's response to the failures of the institutions of the single market and the euro area, revealed by the financial crisis of 2009. the single banking resolution mechanism is one of the pillars of the banking union, together with single supervision - which is the responsibility of the ecb - and the integrated deposit guarantee scheme. the banking union will finally overcome the asymmetry between the deep cross-border integration of the banking system on the one hand and the national fragmentation of banking supervision and resolution systems on the other. it is therefore an essential part of the economic and monetary union launched in 1992 and which the crisis has threatened to shake to its very foundations. slowly but surely, even in the aftermath of the crisis, the european union is strengthening the institutions of economic and financial governance. it's important to learn from crises.
in the case of the united kingdom, the commission has already taken the initiative in the form of a proposal for a regulation on the european banking authority. this proposal, which is one of the fundamental building blocks of banking union, aims to break the contagion link between sovereign and banking debt once and for all by protecting the taxpayers of the member states from the financial problems of their banking institutions. parliament supports the creation of a single resolution fund, financed by bank money, which should be operational as soon as possible in order to safeguard the health and stability of the european financial system. it also wants the solution for bank resolution in the european union to be kept within the community method and legislative framework. in this context, i voted in favour of parliament's decision to postpone the final vote on this report until the negotiations with the council have been concluded, in order to safeguard the stability and soundness of financial markets and the interests of european citizens and taxpayers.
in the case of the euro, the european union has moved towards the creation of the euro and the euro zone without first developing the necessary mechanisms to supervise the banking entity and any action arising from it that could harm the economic activity of the member states. after the euro crisis and the need for several member states to support bank restructuring and subsequently to adopt severe austerity measures, the european union recognised the need to go further in banking supervision by creating a single resolution mechanism and a single bank support fund. i am in favour of a more integrated internal market for banking services and increased supervision, dictated by a single mechanism which would allow uniform rules to be implemented in all the member states.

in writing. - this report argues that labels should indicate the country of origin or provenance of the food, in particular with regard to the determination of the life points of the animal: (a) place of birth; (b) place of rearing; (c) place of slaughter. however, it excludes the labelling of pigmeat, sheepmeat, goatmeat and poultrymeat and minced and minced meat, where the indication of the country on the labelling is not mandatory and only whether it is from the european union or not, or whether it was raised and slaughtered in the eu and not in the eu. only beef and beef products meet these requirements and should serve as a model for other fresh meat. the inclusion of the three points in an animal's life may sometimes be the only means for the consumer to decide between meat products. on the other hand, the horse meat scandal has brought to light how complex and interconnected the flow of meat commodities is. the reference to the place of birth of the animal on the label allows for greater transparency and traceability, making fraud more difficult and making it easier to verify those indications.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution of the european parliament setting out its position on the rules for implementing the regulation on the indication of the country of origin or place of provenance of fresh, chilled and frozen meat of swine, sheep, goats and poultry. parliament called on the commission to draw up a revised version of the implementing regulation, including a requirement for mandatory labelling of the place of birth, rearing and slaughter for unprocessed meat of swine, poultry, sheep and goats, in accordance with the existing legislation on labelling of the origin of beef.
in writing. - the requirements on the origin of beef and beef products are fundamental, since they create expectations on the part of consumers as regards the quality and transport of the foodstuffs concerned. however, the commission does not elaborate on this legal requirement of food origin, does not include mandatory labelling in relation to the place of birth, and does not list the places of rearing and slaughter for unprocessed meat of swine, poultry, sheep and goats, in accordance with the legislation in force on labelling the origin of beef. i therefore vote in favour of the motion for a resolution calling on the european commission to withdraw the regulation in question and to submit a new proposal which is more complete and which protects consumers.

in writing. - this joint motion for resolution on the situation in syria replaced six different texts and it thus expresses the opinion of six different political groups in the european parliament. in response to a catastrophe of such significance and complexity, it is extremely important to share a common view in order to take stronger measures and adopt more effective common positions. i would therefore like to draw attention to the fact that the european parliament has spoken with one voice since the beginning of this tragedy. according to the un, since the start of this terrible calamity, more than 130 000 people, most of them civilians, have been killed; 9 million are in need of humanitarian aid inside syria, including more than 6.5 million internally displaced people; and there are more than 2.3 million syrian refugees. as chair of the delegation for relations with the mashreq countries, i would like to express my full support for the geneva ii conference on syria, which must (as the resolution states) be the ‘first step in a process that will lead to a political and democratic solution to the conflict’, and i would like to remind mr assad’s regime that, as parliamentarians, we will continue to be attentive and proactive.
in the light of the recent events in syria, the commission has decided to extend the mandate of the european union to the whole of the region. the brutality that has been inflicted on its people is absolutely intolerable. more and more reports are coming in of real crimes against humanity perpetrated by the authorities and their supporters against defenseless men, women and children. despite the talks which are taking place without any tangible result, the result, also, of some inconsistency and the risk of radicalization and instrumentalization of the opposition, the regime remains committed to hardening its reaction and to using all the means at its disposal to survive. equally disturbing are the reports that many foreigners have flocked to the theatres of operations and have become involved in the conflict, aggravating its implications and extending its effects. the european union must be at the forefront of those seeking to promote solutions to this conflict and be particularly vigilant in monitoring the situation with regard to human rights violations.
in writing. - once again, the majority in the ep reveals its hypocrisy regarding the situation in syria, by dodging the support of the eu, us, nato and gulf dictatorships to the rebels, by training, financing and arming those it now accuses of being criminals. it could be a tactical change by imperialism, turning yesterday's democratic opposition into a reason - any reason - to attack syria tomorrow, to sow more destruction and to violate its sovereignty. the reasons for imperialist military aggression are not the aspirations of peoples for freedom, sovereignty, social and economic progress of countries and peoples, and the fight against the use of chemical weapons. the reasons are the recolonization of the planet and of course of the central region of energy reserves which is the middle east, as well as the guarantee of the regional impunity of imperialism, of israel and its policy of state terrorism and occupation of palestine. the european union is also concerned about the influx of refugees into syria's neighbouring countries and the eu, while maintaining pressure and interference on syria in the face of a military attack, which is the main reason why thousands of refugees continue to leave syria.
in writing. - violence in syria is escalating and the death toll is rising steadily. according to the united nations, since the beginning of the violent crackdown on peaceful protesters in syria, more than 130 000 people, mostly civilians, have been killed, according to estimates by the united nations office for the coordination of humanitarian affairs (ocha), some 9 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance in syria, including more than 6,5 million internally displaced persons, and there are more than 2,3 million syrian refugees, mainly in turkey, jordan, lebanon, egypt and iraq. in the face of this increasingly catastrophic scenario, we must seek a political solution that safeguards the unity, territorial integrity, sovereignty and independence of syria. we must stop this escalation of violence which only harms people and solves nothing.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on the situation in syria, which reiterates parliament's support for the efforts of the vp/hr catherine ashton and commissioner kristalina georgieva to ensure better coordination in the field of humanitarian aid.
in the light of the limited progress made at the second summit on how to achieve peace and manage the war in syria, it is necessary to continue to put pressure on the regime to allow humanitarian aid to reach those who need it most. this conflict, which took place in the framework of the arab spring, was initially aimed at the overthrow of bashar al-assad, but at the moment it is a sectarian struggle between shiite supporters of the government and sunni rebels who support the fall of this same government, which ended in a civil war. since the beginning of the conflict, 130,000 people have been killed and there are 9.5 million displaced persons and refugees. the union needs to support the neighbouring countries which are receiving thousands of syrians every day. the lack of food and the insecurity in the refugee camps create anger and put syrians in an unimaginable situation. i am in favour of this proposal because it is urgent that the international community put an end to this war scenario so that the syrian people can start a new life.
in writing. - i approve this resolution, beginning by strongly condemning all acts of violence, terrorism, incitement, hate speech and censorship that are taking place in egypt. i call on all political actors and the security forces to exercise the utmost restraint and to avoid provocations, in order to prevent a further escalation of violence, in the interests of the country. i offer my deepest condolences to the families of the victims. i call on the provisional authorities and the egyptian security forces to guarantee the safety of all citizens, regardless of their political views, affiliation or religion. it is essential to ensure respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, to protect the right of association, peaceful assembly, freedom of expression and freedom of the press. it is essential that there is a commitment to resolve the situation through dialogue and non-violence, in accordance with the respect and fulfilment of the country's international obligations.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this joint motion for a resolution on the situation of egypt. first of all, i strongly believe that the eu must monitor, in loco, the upcoming electoral processes and must react firmly in all cases where the rules of democracy are breached, following the announcement of presidential elections by april and fresh parliamentary elections by the end of july. i also believe that, as european legislators, we must respect the people’s vote and be prepared to work with the public institutions that emerge from these elections. the new european neighbourhood policy makes european action conditional on the principle of ‘more for more’, so egypt must prove to us that it will embrace the fundamental values of democracy (such as the rule of law, judicial independence, tolerance and the sovereignty of the people) as well as freedom and solidarity. if the state does not observe these values, the eu should continue to support only those who are willing to observe them. in conclusion, and to quote the resolution, i call on the egyptian interim authorities ‘to ensure the security of all citizens, irrespective of their political views, affiliation or confession, to respect human rights and fundamental freedoms, to protect the freedoms of association, peaceful assembly, expression and of the press’.
in writing. the so-called arab spring surprised the west and opened an opportunity for the democratization of several states. they overthrew their former rulers and initiated electoral processes and constitutional revisions aimed at political openness and greater citizen participation. despite the initial momentum for change, particularly evident in tunisia, egypt and libya, there is now a retreat from the initial momentum and, in some cases, a setback with serious consequences for populations already battered by the violence and instability that accompanied the revolutions. the ousting of president morsi, who was largely a victim of his own intransigence and authoritarianism, and the removal of the muslim brotherhood from political life by the egyptian army, denote the tension between various sectors of society and prove that the ousting of mubarak was not enough for egypt to find a new path towards democracy, peace and stability. the christian communities, in particular the copts, have been particularly and unjustly targeted by the latent brutality and the union should strongly condemn it. i hope that the new constitution adopted in a referendum will contribute to the necessary stability of the country and that egypt can rise up again without excluding anyone, rejecting intolerance, violence and authoritarianism.

in writing. recent events in ukraine demonstrate the extent to which there appears to be a geostrategic tension between the union and russia. i believe that this is more due to a certain russian unease about europe's approach to its vital space, to the core of its zone of influence, than to a european attempt to combat russia's role in countries with which it has longstanding and solid historical relations. it should be remembered that the origin of the russian state lies precisely in the grand duchy of kiev. i believe that russia would gain more by understanding the union as a potential partner and seeking to establish a non-competitive, complementary relationship with it than by seeking to challenge it and the values it represents. these are understood and loved not only by the people of the neighbouring states but also by the russian people themselves. russia is a great power with an inescapable historical and civilizational role. the union must continue to deepen and develop its relationship with russia, without relinquishing the necessary rigor and rigour in defending its interests and paying particular attention to the conduct and procedures of the russian authorities.

- the regulation on implementing acts was adopted at the end of 2010. the commission then undertook to align all provisions relating to the regulatory procedure with scrutiny under articles 290 and 291 tfeu by the end of the current legislature. parliament's position on aligning the regulatory procedure with scrutiny concerns the adaptation of 30 legislative acts (omnibus iii). the commission has concluded that some of these measures do not fall within the scope of article 290 tfeu. it proposed that, where it considers that such measures do not meet the criteria of article 291 tfeu, it should be empowered to adopt implementing acts itself. in other cases, it considered that the powers conferred on it were not in conformity with the treaty and therefore proposed that those provisions be deleted. the rapporteur and the specialised committees consulted do not agree with most of the conclusions and i voted in favour of the european parliament's document.

in writing. - the report by mr thomas ulmer deals with the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 443/2009 to define the ways of achieving the 2020 target for the reduction of co2 emissions from new passenger cars. this report sets a target of 95 g co2/km of average emissions for the fleet of new cars registered in the eu in 2020. this objective will apply to manufacturers producing more than 1000 vehicles per year. this implies reductions of 27% in annual fuel consumption compared to the target of 130 g in 2015. i would remind you that motor vehicles have a significant impact on climate change, as they account for 12% of the eu's overall co2 emissions. i also stress the added value of a new, more realistic and reliable test procedure to ensure that it represents real driving conditions and to avoid underestimating real co2 emissions and fuel consumption.
in writing. - super credits are still advocated in this report as measures to encourage the production of new, less polluting vehicles, although at lower rates than under the previous legislation. in other words, car manufacturers are allowed to offset the sale of electric vehicles by the sale of polluting vehicles that escape the emission limits defined in the legislation. for each electric car sold, car manufacturers are entitled to 1,3 supercredits, i.e. the permission to sell 1,3 highly polluting cars, without the emissions of these vehicles being counted in the calculation of the average emissions of the manufacturer. the proposal also changes the minimum number of new cars produced by a company so that it is exempted from co2 emission reduction obligations from 500 to 1000. the report also stresses the need for market solutions, which reveals a political and ideological choice. we voted against it. we agree and advocate the urgent need to reduce dependence on fossil fuels by developing and implementing energy alternatives but in the public domain, alongside increased energy efficiency. we advocate the strengthening, development and encouragement and expansion of all public transport, particularly electrically driven transport, especially in cities.

in writing. - i approve this report, considering that the european police office (europol) was first established by a convention on 26 july 1995, the only instrument available at the time of its creation under the maastricht treaty, which required ratification by all member states to enter into force. this mechanism meant that any amendment to the europol convention could only be made by means of a protocol, an instrument which had to be submitted to national parliaments for subsequent ratification. the entry into force of the treaty of amsterdam has made it possible to respond to europol's need for a more effective regulatory legal instrument, which would enable it to have a better capacity to react to the increasingly globalised crime. the european police office is thus reorganised as a european agency and given a community budget and staff. to this end, on 6 april 2009 the council adopted the decision establishing the european police office, repealing the previous europol convention.

in writing. - in recent years, serious and organised crime has increased in the european union, an increasingly dynamic and complex phenomenon that threatens the security and prosperity of the union and of europeans. crime in the broad sense is now a concern for european citizens and businesses who feel that their decisions are affected by phenomena with increasing impact, such as cybercrime. organized crime networks are increasingly diverse and global. terrorists operate and cooperate on a cross-border scale causing ever-increasing damage. i believe that there is an urgent need to make the european police office more effective and efficient in cooperation and exchange of information, and i therefore vote in favour of this report. i would remind you that, under the provisions of the lisbon treaty, europol's activities are subject to the control of the representatives democratically elected by the european citizens, and i stress the importance of strengthening the effectiveness of the mechanism for monitoring its activities by the european parliament and national parliaments. i would also stress the crucial importance for the union of having a more effective europol, with greater responsibility and streamlined procedures, capable of ensuring that our fundamental rights are respected and safeguarded.
in writing. - the commission proposal extends the scope of europol's powers. in addition to terrorism, organised crime and other forms of serious crossborder crime, it now aims to cover crimes affecting common interests covered by eu policies. in other words, the door is opened to a substantial widening of the scope of europol's activities. the commission wants to see a clear obligation for member states to provide data and to increase their cooperation with europol so that it can fulfil its objectives, also giving it more powers of initiative. in the commission proposal, europol may propose to the member states to set up joint investigations and to receive personal data from private individuals, which raises serious data protection issues. the proposal includes information sharing with the european parliament and a merger between the eu bodies cepol and europol. we see serious risks in the proposals put forward in this report. we voted against it.
in writing. - europol's mission is to support national police services and their mutual cooperation in preventing and combating serious crime and terrorism. europol facilitates the exchange of information between the competent authorities of the member states and provides criminal analysis to assist national police forces in their transnational investigations. the lisbon treaty ensures that europol's activities are subject to the control of representatives democratically elected by eu citizens. the mechanism for scrutiny of europol's activities by the european parliament, together with national parliaments, should be carried out through a parliamentary scrutiny cell, with a small specialised structure, formed by the competent committee of the european parliament (libe), together with a representative of the committee on home affairs or similar from each of the national parliaments of the member states. in order to ensure effective control of this agency, i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. - the european police office (europol) was first established by a convention on 26 july 1995, the only instrument available at the time of its creation under the maastricht treaty, which required ratification by all member states to enter into force. this mechanism meant that any amendment to the europol convention could only be made by means of a protocol, an instrument which had to be submitted to national parliaments for subsequent ratification. the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon on 1 december 2009 implied the recognition of the co-decision power of the european parliament. article 88 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union provides that the european parliament and the council, acting by means of a regulation adopted in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure, are to determine europol's structure, functioning, field of action and tasks. the draft proposal clearly defines europol's field of action, its tasks and the way in which cooperation with the member states is to be carried out. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. - i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that the lisbon treaty has introduced the possibility for parliament and the council (together referred to as the legislator) to delegate part of their powers to the commission by means of a legislative act (the basic act); that delegation is a delicate operation whereby the commission is entrusted with the exercise of a power which is intrinsic to the role of the legislator itself; that it is therefore responsible for ensuring the correct application of the treaty, in order also to ensure a sufficient level of democratic legitimacy for delegated acts; that the starting point for examining the question of delegation must therefore always be the freedom of the legislator; that according to established case law, the adoption of the essential elements of a legislative act is reserved to the legislator, which is why the adoption of provisions requiring political decisions from the legislator's sphere of competence cannot be delegated; that such delegated power can therefore only supplement or amend non-essential elements of the legislative act; that delegated acts thus adopted by the commission shall be non-legislative acts of general scope.
- the high expectations set out in the reports on the delegation of legislative powers and in the regulation on implementing acts in 2010 have not been fulfilled as initially envisaged. the drafting of delegated and implementing acts, as well as the correct and most appropriate choice of provisions to be included in the basic act, are issues that have become an integral part of most negotiations on legislative proposals. that is why i am in favour of this report.

in the first place, the commission has to be able to take account of the fact that the single market is a major economic and social issue. this report aims to maintain the necessary focus on the way the single market is functioning in the european union, with comments on previously made recommendations, an updated position on the content of the next annual growth survey and priority actions at national and european level, as well as the recent efforts made by the commission with regard to the multiplicity of instruments for the governance of the single market. the new policies include the creation of the single market online assessment panel, which aims to ensure consistent communication, analysing strengths and weaknesses and offering various incentives for improvement. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. - i approve this report, agreeing with the view that the economic, financial and social crisis has put a stop to the convergence process and may have led to a setback, widening disparities between regions and ending a long period during which regional disparities in gdp per head and unemployment in the european union have been declining consistently, while the most vulnerable regions of the union are being the most affected. fiscal consolidation policies are insufficient on their own to boost growth and promote investments capable of generating quality and sustainable jobs. the commission and the member states need to increase investment in entrepreneurship, business creation and self-employment to create more jobs. it should be noted that smes and microenterprises employ about two thirds of the total private sector in the european union. it is important to take into account the considerable needs of many regions with low development rates in terms of investment in infrastructure projects in key sectors such as transport, telecommunications and sustainable energy.
in writing. - the development disparities between european regions have increased as a result of the economic and financial crisis that has gripped europe since at least 2008. in the interests of pursuing a triple growth objective (smart, sustainable and inclusive growth) based on research and innovation, the optimal and rational use of european energy resources and potential, and a proactive policy of job creation, the commission intends to take action under cohesion policy, with the support of the european regional bodies. however, the report's conclusions highlight the fact that convergence regions are not able to overcome their difficulties on their own and that the interaction between cities (economically vibrant but where the risks of poverty and exclusion are greater) and regions must be strengthened in order to pursue a common interest. the draft report aims to support the ongoing monitoring of the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy. the dependence of some member states and regions on cohesion funds is a cause for concern, with regional disparities and the effects of the crisis on groups at risk of poverty and exclusion to be tackled.

in writing. - the ecall system, which automatically calls the emergency services (112) in the event of a serious accident, will be available to all of us, drivers and passengers of light vehicles. in order to protect personal data of each individual, manufacturers shall ensure that vehicles equipped with the ecall in-vehicle system are not traceable and are not subject to a constant location in their pre-emergency state of operation of the service. i am sure that this system will save lives all over europe, which is why i am in favour of it.
in writing. - this proposal addresses the public safety answering point (psap) infrastructure part of the commission's strategy on the interoperable eu-wide emergency call service (ecall), which follows a tripartite regulatory approach covering in-vehicle system, telecommunications networks and psaps. road safety is one of the major aspects of the european union's transport policy. in 2011, some 30 000 people died and more than 1.5 million were injured in some 1.1 million road accidents on eu roads. in addition to the tragedy of loss of life and injury, this reality also entails an economic cost to society of around eur 130 billion per year. we believe that the implementation of the ecall system will help to combat this serious problem by contributing to significantly reducing the arrival times of first aid to the accident victims. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - the commission has been working on ecall since 2005 and has tried to roll it out on a voluntary basis. since this voluntary approach has not worked (currently only around 0.7% of vehicles are equipped with an ecall system), the commission has started to adopt legislation to make ecall a mandatory service in new vehicles. the ecall system shall be activated automatically as soon as the sensors in the vehicle detect a major accident. once activated, the system dials the european emergency number 112, establishes a telephone link with the appropriate emergency call centre and sends information about the accident to the rescue services, including the time of the incident, the exact position of the vehicle involved and the direction in which it was travelling. the ecall call can also be activated manually by pressing a button in the car, for example by a witness to a serious accident. road safety has always been a very important issue for the european parliament, and i have therefore voted in favour of this report. in fact, an automated call can lead to a faster response by emergency services, resulting in fewer fatalities and less serious injuries for drivers and european citizens.
in writing. - ecall in passenger and commercial vehicles should be operational in all member states from 2015, the so-called interoperability of the 112 system. despite the proximity of the october 2015 date, both the commission and parliament believe that member states will be ready, as the heero pilot project has been developed and the different countries have already applied much of the necessary work. the proposal also calls on the member states to take measures to raise awareness of the importance of the number '112' among the general public. to ensure coordination, the commission will monitor and support the organisation of these campaigns. i am in favour of this report which will standardize the implementation of ecall in the 28 member states of the union.
in writing. - the ecall system proposed in the report is an emergency telephone service for first contact with an accident-involved vehicle and for dispatching first aid. the ecall system shall be activated automatically as soon as the sensors in the vehicle detect a major accident. once activated, the system dials the european emergency number 112, establishes a telephone link with the appropriate emergency call centre and sends information about the accident to the rescue services, including the time of the incident, the exact position of the vehicle involved and the direction in which it was travelling. one of the problems is the issue of privacy and data protection, since the system will have information on the location of vehicles and even, in the event of an accident, the possibility of accessing the car's interior audio system. on the other hand, it should be mandatory to be linked to the national health system to avoid economic exploitation. there seems to be no credible guarantee that this big brother of road accident assistance cannot be used for other interests, particularly if it is handed over to the private sector.

in writing. - i approve this report, first of all by congratulating myself on the aim of the commission's proposal to increase the efficiency of vat collection. this action, in my view, will simultaneously reduce bureaucracy and the costs associated with the tax administration of the member states and for taxable persons. i also welcome the aim of limiting the information requirements to what is strictly necessary for vat control and collection. the proposal therefore ensures a reasonable balance and proportionality between the need to reduce the burden on business activities and to remove obstacles to the smooth functioning of the internal market. i also share the view that all companies should be allowed to provide up to 26 standard pieces of information to the tax authorities of the member states in which they operate, in a common format and preferably electronically. this initiative should save time for all those involved in the vat return and help to avoid or correct errors easily. this will increase the control capacity of the union tax administrations.
in writing. - vat is an indirect tax on consumption, ultimately borne by the final consumer. this tax represents about 21% of the national tax revenues of the member states. however, given that an amount equivalent to 12% of vat revenues is left uncollected annually, it will be necessary to implement a more effective vat system, which adequately prevents or eliminates the various forms of vat fraud. the commission has therefore proposed simplification measures for the collection of this tax. it proposed a standard vat return, which will reduce the administrative burden associated with the collection of vat, increase the efficiency of vat collection, while reducing red tape and the associated costs for member states' tax administrations. paying agents will also benefit from a simpler and less costly procedure. as the declaration will be completed electronically, member states should make available all the information necessary for its correct completion so that the declaration is handed over in an appropriate manner. in view of the above and the benefits of more effective collection of this tax at european level, i have supported this report.
in writing. - i am pleased that you voted in favour of this report in order to further reduce the burden on businesses and improve the functioning of the internal market. the information requirements in the standard vat return should be made uniform across the member states and, within five years from the date of entry into force of this directive, the commission will assess its application in this respect and make appropriate proposals.
in writing. - bearing in mind that vat represents 21% of the official revenue of the member states and that half of this amount is not collected annually, which translates into a considerable loss of revenue with a significant budgetary impact, i vote in favour of this report, which advances the need to implement a more efficient vat system with a view to eliminating in the medium term the various forms of evasion in the collection of this tax. i welcome the proposal to introduce a standard vat return, which will reduce, according to european commission estimates, up to eur 15 billion per calendar year in unnecessary administrative costs. this is a measure which contributes to the much-needed relief on the expenditure side of the public budgets of the member states of the union, especially in times of economic crisis such as the one we are going through and, in particular, in the case of countries with adjustment programmes such as portugal.
in writing. - a set of rules has been adopted today on the information to be required on vat refund declarations. these rules will have to be adopted and actively implemented by all the member states of the union, allowing for a harmonisation of the minimum rules in this area. i believe that this is an important step which will allow for a substantial reduction in red tape and will actively contribute to the implementation of the european policy to combat fraud.
in writing. - vat is an indirect tax on consumption, ultimately borne by the final consumer. this tax represents about 21% of the national tax revenues of the member states. however, given that an amount equivalent to 12% of vat revenues is left uncollected annually, it will be necessary to implement a more effective vat system, which adequately prevents or eliminates the various forms of vat fraud. the commission has therefore proposed simplification measures for the collection of this tax. it proposed a standard vat return, which will reduce the administrative burden associated with the collection of vat, increase the efficiency of vat collection, while reducing red tape and the associated costs for member states' tax administrations. paying agents will also benefit from a simpler and less costly procedure. the report also stresses that the introduction of this standardisation is very positive for the better collection and payment of vat at union level, as well as for the control of the payment of this tax, combating tax evasion and fraud. as the declaration will be completed electronically, member states should make available all the information necessary for its correct completion so that the delivery of the declaration is carried out in a secure and appropriate manner. in view of the above and the benefits of more effective collection of this tax at european level, i support this report, which has my vote in favour.
in writing. - the vat system requires companies to complete the periodic vat returns with the detailed information necessary for the payment and control of vat, which can be particularly complex if vat returns are submitted in different member states. such complexity is the result of different information being provided, the fact that the information does not include harmonised definitions, the lack of good common guidelines, the existence of various rules and multiple procedures for the submission of declarations and for any corrections, and the need to use the national language. all this leads to an increase in the burden on businesses, to a lower accuracy and timeliness of vat returns, and further restricting cross-border trade. of the options assessed in detail, the preferred option is the standard vat return, which is mandatory for member states and for companies, and which presents a list of standard information of which only a small number is required in all cases. this option maximises the reduction of burdens for businesses while limiting costs for member states. the preferred option is expected to reduce administrative burdens by up to eur 15 billion per year. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - value added tax (vat) is an indirect tax on consumption ultimately borne by the final consumer, and represents about 21% of member states' tax revenues. however, as an amount equivalent to 12% of vat revenues is left uncollected annually, a more effective system is necessary to implement, which adequately prevents or eliminates vat fraud. the commission has therefore proposed the introduction of simplification measures in the collection of this tax, through a standardised vat return, which will reduce the administrative burden and increase the efficiency of vat collection, while reducing red tape and the associated costs for member states' tax administrations, while taxpayers will also benefit from a simpler and less burdensome procedure. the report also stresses that this standardisation is very positive for improving the collection and payment of vat at eu level, as well as for monitoring the payment of this tax, combating tax evasion and fraud. in view of the above, and in view of the benefits of more effective collection of this tax at european level, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - the proposal to reduce the burden on businesses through the harmonisation of vat returns is essentially aimed at further reducing the costs of the large economic groups - those that carry out the most transactions in the context of the eu single market. the objective of combating vat fraud by limiting the information requirements to what is strictly necessary is contradictory, since this simplification gives companies greater leeway to evade taxation, especially since the free movement of capital, goods and services remains untouched. contrary to what the dominant political forces in the eu would have us believe, the fight against fraud and the increase in tax revenue in the member states is not to be done by strengthening the single market and tax harmonization in the eu, but by increasing the taxation of the large economic groups and by effectively combating fraud, which must go beyond the end of tax havens and the dogmas of the single market and the free movement of capital.

in writing. - the european commission and turkey were finally able to reach an agreement in 2012 on the text of this readmission agreement after eight years of negotiations. this agreement provides for obligations to readmit persons residing without authorisation on a strictly reciprocal basis, and defines technical and procedural criteria for such readmission. it is important to take into account that a high number of irregular migrants enter the eu territory through turkey, which is the main transit country for illegal immigration into the union, contributing to the enormous migratory pressure on greece. it is therefore essential to strengthen cooperation with turkey in the areas of migration management, the fight against trafficking in human beings and border control. this agreement should also have an impact on the process of gradual visa liberalisation in the long term and will constitute an important step forward on the roadmap towards a visa-free regime.

in writing. - the purpose of this proposal for a decision is to extend rule 147 of parliament's rules of procedure until the end of the eighth parliamentary term. under rule 146, all parliament documents must be written in the official languages and all members have the right to address parliament in the official language of their choice, with interpretation for the other official languages, although under rule 147 derogations from the previous article are allowed until the end of the seventh parliamentary term, when there are not enough linguists for an official language. despite all the efforts made to this end, it is not to be expected that the interpretation capacities (translators and legal linguists) in the irish, maltese and croatian languages will be sufficient to enable a full interpretation service in these languages to be provided as early as the beginning of the eighth parliamentary term, which is why i voted in favour of this proposal for a decision extending article 147 until the end of the eighth parliamentary term. i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in this, but i am saying that it should be involved in the work of the european parliament.

in writing. - i approve of this report, considering that in the last decade there have been three 'railway legislative packages' aimed at progressively opening up national markets and making the railway more competitive and interoperable. however, the modal share of rail transport in total intra-eu transport has remained modest, and many technical barriers remain. the fourth railway package aims to address the obstacles to the effectiveness of railway markets, in order to improve the performance of the sector and create a single european railway area. the commission notes that the obstacles still existing relate primarily to market access for national passenger services, which limit the development of the sector and create disparities between member states which have already opened their markets and those which have not yet done so. a second set of problems concerns governance issues for infrastructure managers. given their nature as natural monopolies, infrastructure managers do not always meet the needs of the market and its users, thus affecting the performance of the sector as a whole.

in writing. - in the context of the fourth railway package, the commission proposes to repeal council regulation (eec) no 1192/69 on common rules for the standardisation of the accounts of railway undertakings. this regulation allows member states to compensate railway undertakings for charges which undertakings in other modes of transport do not have to bear for various reasons. these obligations may relate, for example, to special payments in the event of accidents at work which a railway undertaking is obliged to make but which in the case of other modes of transport are borne by the state, to pensions for railway workers who normally retire earlier because of certain arduous work, or to payments for costs incurred in level crossings. the repeal of this regulation will benefit the railway sector by making it more transparent. that is why i am voting in favour.

in writing. - in voting on the honeyball report on sexual exploitation and prostitution, i could not support the idea of criminalising clients of prostitution. whatever judgement we make about prostitution itself, i am certain that criminalising clients in a voluntary sex service between adults would not be an appropriate solution, however positive (and far from consensual) the so-called nordic solution may be. i have always argued that criminalisation is always a last resort and that there are areas where it can be a problem rather than a solution. this is one of them. in the case of prostitution, criminalisation would only contribute to clandestine prostitution and make prostitutes (and now prostitutes...) even more vulnerable to exploitation by organised gangs and pimps. all that is necessary to punish in this area is already a crime: trafficking in women, forced prostitution, economic exploitation of prostitution. let's leave the penal code out of it where it's not called for.
- prostitution is an ancient reality in the history of mankind which undoubtedly contributed to sexual exploitation and often diminishes the dignity of women (although there is increasing male prostitution, and there is also female prostitution outside of basic economic needs). prostitution requires an approach from different perspectives and in several areas and should be considered as involving all the actors. hence its complexity and the subsequent failure of many measures aimed at reducing it. in this context, i think that the narrow and simplistic approach, starting with the criminalisation of the client, is frankly wrong. that is why i abstained from voting on this report.

on behalf of the s&d group. we are seeing an exponential increase in the use of drones in attacks and assassinations of judicial structures by powers like the united states of america, occurring outside the legal context of the laws of war, that is, in violation of international law. this type of technology, which is more precise than many other weapons used in combat, could offer even greater guarantees of compliance with the laws of war, since it limits the destruction and deaths to the battlefield, but the truth is that when used in situations and areas where there is no declared armed conflict, its use is unequivocally illegal and in violation of international law and human rights in particular, including humanitarian law. that is why, at a time when several member states of the european union are preparing to develop this technology, it is imperative that this be accompanied by explicit regulation of the policy of using drones and the inherent responsibilities within the framework of international law and criminal law, international criminal law. the revision of international humanitarian law, which governs conduct during armed conflict, is important and must safeguard the fundamental value of the right to life by excluding the use of drones outside the context of war, by making it illegal and unequivocally prohibiting it in the absence of armed conflict. this means that any extrajudicial execution outside the context of war is a summary execution, punishable by criminal law, and may even constitute a territorial infringement of third countries. because this technology is semi-autonomous, remotely operated, often controlled from far away from the battlefield, legal testing is all the more important. it is therefore also urgent that the in writing. - the harmonization of law, particularly as regards buying and selling, is always a sensitive matter which is subject to natural caution on the part of the member states and which threatens to conflict with their legal systems and traditions. it is understandable that the increasingly cross-border nature of purchases and sales and the need to protect consumers suggest that we can move towards a genuine european contract law, but i believe that this path must be followed with safety and caution, otherwise it may have a more negative than positive impact on european trade. i hope that the step taken will demonstrate the virtues of this standardisation and that its results, if they prove positive and credible, will encourage policy-makers to take a more integrated approach in this respect.
in writing. - the differences in contract law between the various member states often prevent traders and consumers from carrying out certain crossborder transactions within the internal market. the obstacles created by these differences discourage traders, especially small and medium-sized enterprises (smes), from engaging in cross-border trade or expanding their activity to new markets in the member states. consumers are also harmed by not having access to products offered by traders from other member states. the general objective of this proposal is to improve the establishment and functioning of the internal market by promoting the expansion of crossborder trade for businesses and by facilitating crossborder purchases by consumers. this can be achieved by providing an autonomous and uniform set of contract law rules, including consumer protection provisions the common european sales law which can be seen as a second contract law regime within the national law of each member state. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the berlinguer/lehne report because i believe that a common law on crossborder contracts for the purchase and sale of goods and services is an important contribution to the creation of a genuine internal market in the eu. cross-border acquisitions in the eu should no longer be governed by the national laws of the member states, given the uncertainty created by the potential conflict of laws. the ideal solution would be to have an eu law on sales contracts that would replace the different national laws. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. on the other hand, it is important to support the imaginative solution of this report, because the idea of voluntary application of eu law in cross-border relations according to the will of the parties can become a model for other areas of contracts in civil or commercial law, and be the genesis of a real eu code for contracts.
in writing. - this report concerns the proposal for a regulation on the common european law of sales and purchases (cepc), which is an innovative initiative of great importance to consumers and businesses operating in the internal market. this document is the result of the initiative on european contract law, which has been discussed for many years and aims to solve the problems of the internal market caused by the existence of divergent contract laws at national level. the main aspects addressed in this report include the confirmation of the optional nature of this instrument, so that the esdc and national legislation can coexist and be developed together. the scope has been restricted to distance sales but includes digital contracts. the level of consumer protection is consistent with the requirements of the treaty, is legally satisfactory and introduces improvements in the level of commercial guarantees for consumers. in view of the above, and because i consider that this proposal for a regulation is advantageous for consumers and businesses in the internal market, particularly in this digital age, i voted in favour of this report.
in the case of the united kingdom, the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's internal market is not affected by the introduction of the single market. the optional nature of the document has been confirmed, so that a common european law of sale and purchase and national law can coexist and be developed together. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the document.

in writing. - the report by mrs linda mcavan deals with the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on the approximation of the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the member states relating to the manufacture, presentation and sale of tobacco and related products. the measures taken by the eu over the years to combat smoking have helped to reduce the number of smokers in the european area from 40% in 2002 (in the eu15) to 28% in 2012 (in the eu27). nevertheless, smoking remains the leading cause of preventable deaths in the eu, killing around 700 000 people a year. public health expenditure in the eu for the treatment of tobacco-related diseases amounts to some eur 25.3 billion per year. given that 70% of smokers start smoking before the age of 18, this directive aims primarily to include measures to dissuade young people from smoking, such as the use of stronger health warnings and the prohibition of packaging and fragrances that may be particularly attractive to young people.
in writing. - the revision of the current tobacco products directive, which dates back to 2001, aims mainly to include measures to dissuade young people from smoking, such as the use of stronger health warnings and the prohibition of packaging and flavourings that may be particularly attractive to young people. the new measures include increasing health warnings to 65% on both sides of packaging, banning certain flavourings and regulating e-cigarettes as medicines only if they are presented as having curative or preventive properties. this legislation introduces new rules on how tobacco products are produced, presented and sold and covers other products that were not yet regulated at eu level, such as e-cigarettes. we hope that we have taken a decisive step towards reducing tobacco consumption, particularly among young people.
