in writing. - solvit is a european network, set up in 2002, for the informal settlement of crossborder disputes concerning the incorrect application of the single market rules. this network has proven its effectiveness and usefulness, receiving over three thousand complaints per year and with an 89% success rate. the european parliament has today argued that there is room for improvement in the solvit network, in particular to enable it to deal with more complex issues and to focus on greater network specialisation, for example in the business sector.
in writing. - solvit was set up in 2002 as an informal online dispute resolution network for crossborder disputes arising from incorrect or inaccurate application of single market rules between citizens or businesses and national administrations across the eu, insofar as such disputes are not subject to judicial proceedings at national or eu level. solvit is an online dispute resolution mechanism and at the same time a network of cooperation between national administrations, which contributes to improving the enforcement capacity of eu law at national level by promoting the correct application of eu law. solvit as an instrument has achieved tangible results and has proven its usefulness and value for the single market. however, there is still a huge room for improvement in helping citizens and businesses to benefit from their rights in the single market through solvit and other measures. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - the proper functioning of the single market for the benefit of citizens and businesses requires improving the information available on their rights in the single market and on the rules in force in the different member states, as well as providing the necessary assistance for solving problems at cross-border level. solvit, established in 2002, is an online network for the informal resolution of crossborder disputes arising from the incorrect application of single market rules between citizens or businesses and national administrations across the european union. in september 2013, the commission presented a recommendation aimed at improving the solvit network and mentioning that the action plan your europe should help to improve the availability and quality of information on rights in the eu single market and to raise awareness of their rights among citizens and businesses, in particular smes, by referring them to the solvit network whenever they encounter such problems. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that solvit is a mechanism with great potential for solving problems for citizens and businesses.
in writing. - i know . solvit was set up in 2002 as an online network for the informal resolution of crossborder disputes concerning the incorrect or inaccurate application of single market rules. the network is also a cooperation network between national administrations, helping to improve the enforcement capacity of eu law. the solvit network has achieved good results, proving its usefulness and value for the european single market. however, there is still a great deal of room for improvement in supporting citizens and businesses to fully benefit from their rights in the single market through solvit. in order to make the most of the potential of the single market, it is necessary to close some gaps, such as the fact that some national rules in member states are contrary to european law. the document also proposes that a formal framework for solvit be established, alongside the adoption of relevant targets for the performance of the network.
in writing. - solvit is an online network for informal dispute resolution for cross-border disputes. the european parliament's previous annual reports on solvit have focused on analysing the functioning of this network and proposed measures to improve its work within the single market. these measures have so far focused on improving information for citizens about their rights and information for businesses about rules and laws. however, the report voted on today goes further. it is a harsh criticism of the member states. stresses that the main reason for the various problems in the operation of the solvit network is that the rules in many member states are contrary to eu single market legislation. more specifically, one of the main problems mentioned is the late or incorrect application of european union legislation or the conflict between national and european law. we voted against it.
in writing. - i approve this report. given the inadequacy of traditional judicial cooperation in relation to the current european reality, the adoption of this directive is undoubtedly a positive step forward, clearly conducive to the reinforcement of the construction of the european criminal area. it crystallizes the tension between progress in terms of transfer of sovereignty in the name of security and protection of fundamental rights. the challenge to the european criminal justice system is, of course, to be able to do so in a way that respects and guarantees fundamental rights. it is significant that the preamble to the charter of fundamental rights expressly refers to the area of freedom, security and justice, given its particularly sensitive nature in terms of fundamental rights and freedoms. and needless to say, your guarantee must be real and not formal. the deliberate and well-considered creation of the european criminal area implies that judicial review of respect for fundamental rights is ensured in the union.
in writing. - the european investigation order (eio) is a judicial decision issued by a competent authority of a member state (the issuing state) to have one or more specific investigative measures carried out in another member state (the executing state) with a view to gathering evidence. parliament, thanks to the excellent work of my colleague nuno melo, whom i congratulate on the quality of his report, has seen its main objectives achieved in striking the right balance between the need for strong and efficient judicial cooperation between the member states in combating crime and the defence of the rights of the accused and suspects. it is right to recognise the need for swift and efficient cooperation between member states and i hope that the european investigation decision can make a positive contribution to improving the european response to crossborder crime. it will be for the judicial and police authorities of the member states to give practical and operational content to this instrument which is of great importance and interest for the proper conduct of the difficult investigative work.
in writing. - after a long and intensive period of negotiation, an important instrument to combat organised and crossborder crime in the european union has been created. the european investigation order allows one member state (the issuing state) to require the execution of a certain investigative measure (such as dna collection, telecommunications interception, supervised deliveries, covered investigations) from another member state (the executing state). the investigative measure requested by the authorities of another member state should be carried out with the same speed and priority as similar national proceedings and within a fixed period of 90 days, with a member state being able to refuse to carry it out only in a limited number of cases laid down in the directive. this instrument has allowed for enhanced protection of the fundamental rights of suspects and accused persons in the relevant proceedings. the judicial authorities of a member state may refuse a european investigation order if there are substantial grounds for believing that the execution of the investigative measure would be incompatible with their obligations under the charter of fundamental rights.
in writing. - this report concerns the adoption of the directive on the european investigation order in criminal matters. in view of the acknowledged inadequacy of traditional judicial cooperation in relation to the current european reality, this proposal for a directive constitutes a positive step forward and is conducive to the revitalisation of the construction of the european criminal space, including aspects related to the transfer of sovereignty, security, respect for and guarantee of the protection of fundamental rights. in practice, the creation of the european criminal area implies ensuring judicial control of respect for fundamental rights and freedoms in the european union. after the european union promoted police and judicial cooperation to compensate for the disappearance of internal borders, the importance of the european criminal space and the benefits of the progressive construction of a homogeneous criminal space in the european space are now evident. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the measures proposed contribute to the promotion of freedom, security and justice in the european union.
in writing. - a european investigation order (eio) is a judicial decision issued or validated by a judicial authority of a member state for the purpose of carrying out in another member state one or more specific investigative measures with a view to obtaining evidence in accordance with the directive in question. i am voting in favour of the dei report because i believe that evidence already in the possession of the competent authorities in the executing state should be obtained, that specific rules are required which are better dealt with separately and that it is essential to facilitate access to evidence existing in other member states. finally, i would like to congratulate my colleague, mr nuno melo, on his hard work, and above all on having achieved a satisfactory result for the citizens of europe.

in writing. - i approve this report, considering that the conclusion of the agreement with indonesia is an important step for the european union in its efforts to improve sustainable forest management worldwide, to put an end to deforestation and forest degradation and to stimulate systematic changes in the forestry sector by rewarding the efforts of diligent operators who source timber from legal and reliable sources and protecting them from unfair competition. first of all, it's the third largest tropical forest area in the world. this heritage is, however, threatened by the uncontrolled massive destruction of tropical forests and carbon-rich peatlands for palm oil and paper production, making indonesia the world's third largest emitter of greenhouse gases, which have an impact on climate change. however, only 10% in value of indonesian timber and timber products exports are currently destined for the european union, with the remainder being exported mainly to asian countries. i am very interested in the spillover effects that a sustainable indonesian forest governance system could have on timber exports to these markets as well.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are not used for the purpose of exploiting the resources of the developing countries. it is therefore necessary to ensure that products and raw materials from developing countries comply with the relevant rules and respect the environment and the rights of the people. in the case of imported wood products, it is necessary to ensure their traceability and the fairness of the way in which they are produced, treated and transported.
in writing. - the voluntary partnership agreement (the agreement) focuses on governance and enforcement and, through a licensing system, ensures that indonesia's timber is produced legally. this agreement represents a major commitment by indonesia to tackling the persistent problem of illegal logging. the flegt licence will ensure to the eu market that indonesian timber products come from verified legal sources. it is important that indonesia's timber resources be preserved. only with adequate legislation can the interests of the indonesian forestry sector be protected. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - this recommendation concerns the proposal for the conclusion of the voluntary partnership agreement (vpa) between the european union and the republic of indonesia on forestry law enforcement, governance and trade in timber products imported into the european union. this spa, concluded in september 2013, aims to establish a legal framework to meet the following main objectives: to ensure the traceability of timber products throughout the supply chain; to implement a process to verify and certify that timber products shipped to the eu have been legally acquired, harvested, transported and exported, ensuring proper management and legal exploitation of indonesian forests; to strengthen the validity of the european union action plan on forest law enforcement, governance and trade (flegt). i believe that the conclusion of this gpa is another step in the eu's efforts towards sustainable forest management on a global scale, helping to reduce deforestation, stimulating change of practices in the forestry sector and rewarding and protecting operators who purchase timber from legal and reliable sources from unfair competition, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - the voluntary partnership agreement between the republic of indonesia and the european union aims to establish a legal framework to ensure the traceability of wood products, implement a verification process to certify products shipped to the european market, ensure good management and legal exploitation of indonesian forests and strengthen the eu action plan for forest law enforcement, governance and trade. it is an important step towards improving sustainable forest management worldwide and ending deforestation. indonesia is the third largest tropical forest territory in the world and is under great threat from the massive destruction of its forests and peatlands. the rapporteur has serious concerns about the indonesian timber legality assurance system (tlas). the system does not require the separation of tlas-certified and non-certified wood, impeding legal certainty on exit, a problem exacerbated by the fact that tlas auditors do not necessarily audit all stages of the supply chain. the tlas constitutes a bureaucratic barrier to justice and it is therefore necessary to eliminate the gaps found.

vice-president of the commission. - mr president, i would like to thank all the members who have insisted that much has been done, but also that so much remains to be done. it is true that the crisis has not helped women to develop further but has rather weakened the weakest part of our workforce. concerning specific issues, i would like to thank those members who have emphasised the great effort that has been made in recent years to combat – in a concrete way and in places where we can legislate – violence against women and to create directives that would help those who have become victims of such violence. concerning the equal pay directive, you might remember that in december[nbsp ]2013 the commission adopted a report on the implementation of this directive in real terms. the findings of this report indicate that the main challenge for the member states is the correct application and enforcement of rights in this directive. it is therefore the practical application of the directive and the way it is applied in real terms in the member states that needs to be changed, not the directive itself. one of the main findings of the report is that the implementation of the principle is hindered mostly by the lack of transparency in pay systems. that is the reason why we have presented the recommendation: in order to strengthen this principle of transparency. the measures include the entitlement of employees to request information on levels of pay broken down by gender for categories of employees doing the same work or work of equal value; the employer’s regular reporting of wages by category of employee or position, broken down by gender – this would, of course, be limited to large and medium companies, because we do not wish to be hard on smes; conducting pay audits in large companies; and, most importantly, including equal pay issues and pay audits in collective bargaining. if this were to be implemented in accordance with the report which we have seen, it would help the equal pay directive to be implemented in a more transparent way in real life. i would like to thank all the members for their strong commitment to promoting equality between women and men. over the last few years, the combination of gender mainstreaming with specific measures to promote gender equality have borne fruit. we have achieved a great deal and we should continue with this dual approach in the future. we should also take on the main challenges still to be faced, which are laid out in the parliament’s reports and the amendments.

issues, as well as religious freedom, must be the unwavering focus of the european union's dialogue with riyadh. as i noted during my visit to saudi arabia last november, the political, social and economic life of the country is based on the segregation of women. despite the high level of qualifications afforded by the large number of women entering higher education: only last year were the first 30 women appointed to the shura and only in 2015 will women be able to vote in municipal elections. it is an attack on their dignity and a gross violation of human rights for a system to grant legal guardianship over women to a male relative, father, husband, brother, or even son. a recent law aimed at protecting women from domestic violence will be a mere piece of paper if this subjection is not abolished. the european union must commit itself to supporting all those in saudi arabia who are working to eliminate discrimination against women, whether in the economic field, in access to education, the labour market, justice, including the still persistent obstacles leading to: the argument that such restrictions are based on religious reasons or are intended to protect women must be dismantled. but it's not just women who suffer from the denial of basic rights in saudi arabia: the death penalty continues to be applied in a medieval judicial system without basic safeguards, hostage to judges of religious extraction and without even being based on a written penal code. the statistics on executions include not only adult nationals but also minors and foreigners. it is imperative to persuade saudi arabia to put an end to arbitrary and extrajudicial tensions, the institutionalized practice of torture and corporal punishment, and the harassment of human rights organisations and defenders. it is imperative that it guarantees the rights of minorities, including the shi'a, including the permitting of the public exercise of religious freedom, and also stresses the need to abolish the practice of kefala and the abusive treatment of migrant workers. we would not have taken the trouble to draw up this report in the european parliament if we did not consider the role of saudi arabia to be relevant in regional and global security and if we did not consider that the european union's interaction with the various saudi partners can result in progress, which is of course fundamental to resolving many of the contradictions and intentions facing saudi society itself, with a population that is mostly young, vibrantly active on social networks and increasingly suffocating in an anachronistic system that restricts opportunities. i would like to conclude, mr president, by saying that nothing could be more decisive regionally than the outcome of the negotiations to bring the nuclear programme of neighbouring iran under international control: instead of being sidelined or hampering the process, riyadh can make a decisive contribution to its success by establishing mutually beneficial neighbourly relations and thus contribute to ending the proxy war in the martyred syria, to the stabilisation of iraq, pakistan and afghanistan and to finally advancing the israeli-palestinian peace process.
mr president, i should like to begin by thanking the rapporteurs for these four important pieces of legislation which will now provide an updated framework for the european union's fight against money laundering. it is often said, including in this parliament, that democracy has a cost and that european democracy has a cost. well, that cost, when you do the math, for example of this european parliament divided by all european citizens is one and a half euros a year. but if, on the other hand, we take account of the costs of money laundering, tax evasion, aggressive tax planning and all these activities which are closely linked, but not only to the criminal world, to arms, drugs and human trafficking, these costs, as has already been said, in the case of the european union can amount to 1 billion, that is to say, one million million euros, which is about 2 000 euros per european citizen. if these pieces of legislation we are discussing here can recover at least some of that money, that money which is needed for schools, for parks, for libraries, for hospitals, for the sustainability of our social security systems, then we will be doing one of the most relevant services we could do to the european citizen and, although these things are not measured by money alone, we will be making a lot of profit. the costs of democracy are much lower than the costs of non-democracy. every time democracy advances, the citizen gains in monetary terms, of course, but also in terms of trust in institutions and in terms of moral and human progress. we need, as these reports say, to be able to identify, say, the faces behind these bank transfers, we need to end this system of biombs where one company is owned by another company that hides another company that is then in turn owned by a company in an offshore country behind which the actual faces of the last beneficiaries are hidden. legislation to establish a european register of last beneficiaries is therefore absolutely essential. we're going to need more. in my view, we need a special european unit for the investigation of economic and financial crime and we also need to know exactly who is making each transfer. but these are good advances. i would like to congratulate and thank my colleagues, also as a citizen.
in writing. the amendments voted in the libe and econ committees to the commission's proposal for the revision of the anti-money laundering directive represent a decisive step forward in the fight against corruption and tax evasion and all other forms of crime. i would like to congratulate the libe and econ rapporteurs and the shadows for having managed to agree on a difficult compromise on the need for transparency of the real beneficiaries of companies based in europe. this legislation is very important because it sets a new paradigm - the creation of a public register of the real owners of companies, combating the phenomenon of the creation of opaque structures and shell companies used by criminals to hide the proceeds of crime and evade tax. the eu must promote this standard of transparency in the world by cutting off the fuel that fuels tax havens and secrecy jurisdictions from the united states to the cayman islands, from switzerland to hong kong. the european parliament has played its part: it is now up to the member states to assume their responsibilities to the european citizens, accepting that this is the only way forward if we are to be serious about fighting organised crime, corruption and tax evasion.

in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account that the nagoya protocol guarantees greater legal certainty and greater transparency for both suppliers and users of genetic resources. i also believe it helps to ensure benefit-sharing and creates conditions for access to the most predictable genetic resources. by enhancing legal certainty and promoting benefit-sharing, the nagoya protocol encourages progress in research on genetic resources, which can lead to new discoveries that are beneficial for all. in addition, the nagoya protocol creates incentives for the in situ conservation of genetic resources and their sustainable use, thereby enhancing the contribution of biodiversity to human well-being and development. in my view, the european union plays a central role in the use of genetic resources, both because of its numerous collections and research centres and because of its important industries which use these resources. sustainable access to genetic resources is essential and therefore needs to be enhanced by greater trust in our international partners and a clear legislative framework.
in writing. - the nagoya protocol is an international treaty on access to genetic resources and the fair and equitable sharing of the benefits arising from their use. the protocol has already been signed by the european union. this important agreement on the international governance of biodiversity is the result of long negotiations since the adoption of the cbd in 1992 in rio de janeiro, and comes in the context of a global biodiversity crisis, which continues to intensify with increasing species loss. to reverse this trend, it is necessary to mobilise the necessary resources, especially financial resources, at local and international level to preserve the biodiversity that is vital to our societies. the nagoya protocol is intended to contribute to these objectives. in view of this, i welcome the ratification of the nagoya protocol by the european union.

in writing. - the nagoya protocol is an international treaty on access to genetic resources and the fair and equitable sharing of the benefits arising from their use. signed today by the european union and its 26 member states, it establishes an international scheme to support one of the three objectives of the convention on biological diversity, to preserve biodiversity and its sustainable use. this protocol is based on three pillars: access to genetic resources, subject to the sovereignty of states, which establish national measures to ensure legal certainty through clear legislative frameworks and the issuance of documents such as licenses for granting access; sharing of benefits arising from the fair and equitable use of genetic resources, subject to conditions agreed by mutual agreement between supplier and user, which should contribute to the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity worldwide; and compliance with specific obligations to ensure compliance with the national legislation of the contracting parties and contractual obligations under mutually agreed terms. the nagoya protocol will enter into force as soon as the signatory countries have ratified it, and the report recommends that the eu and all its member states ratify it as soon as possible. we voted in favour.

in writing. - i support this report because i believe that in order to combat money laundering, which costs many millions a year, a coordinated response by law enforcement agencies in the member states is essential, as is a standardised procedure for financial institutions and payment service providers. by complementing the anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism package, this regulation aims to achieve the same overarching objective of more effective combating money laundering and terrorist financing. this measure enhances the transparency of transfers of funds of all types - domestic and cross-border - with the intention of making it easier for law enforcement authorities to track electronically transferred funds by criminals and terrorists. i therefore consider this piece of legislation to be of great importance for greater transparency in the financial world and the fight against terrorism and crime.
in writing. - the objective of this report is to improve the traceability of payments, prevent, investigate and detect money laundering and financial terrorism in relation to transfers of funds. to that end, it lays down rules on the transmission by payment service providers of information on the payer and the payee throughout the payment chain. in some areas, information transparency gaps remain and can be addressed by setting out control rules such as making information on the payer and payer of payments more widely available, extending the scope of payment registries to credit and debit card transactions, internet and mobile payments, and strengthening the sanctioning powers of the relevant authorities. tackling this problem is crucial, as global money laundering is estimated today to be about 2.7% of global gdp. this regulation is part of the wider package on combating money laundering and terrorism, and it is widely understood that insufficient protection of financial systems against misuse by criminals or terrorists can cause serious damage to economic prosperity. that is why i supported this report.

in writing. - while the report contains aspects which we consider to be positive, in particular all the assumptions and the three pillars of the protocol, namely the duty to contribute to the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity worldwide, it is certain that the negotiations with the council have weakened and removed a large part of the points of defence of biodiversity and protection of the patenting of biological processes. the proposal for a regulation, which is intended to amend the nagoya protocol, is intended to cover up the desire to patent biological resources and the appropriation of natural resources and biodiversity by large multinationals. the commission's motto is to accuse european companies of acts of bio-piracy, and it is based on the principle that the privatisation or patenting of genetic resources is no longer reprehensible if compensation is granted to the countries of origin of genetic resources. it concerns who owns the sources of genetic material, who markets it, who is allowed to enter the chain of marketing and use, and how the sharing of monetary and knowledge benefits is ensured, and only a contract on the list, agreed by both parties, ensures that there is no bio-piracy, nor the illegal sale and exchange of genetic material.

in writing. - the loss of biodiversity is accelerating. one in four mammal species, one in eight bird species and more than one in three amphibian species are known to be threatened with extinction globally (iucn, 2012). some 60% of ecosystems have been degraded in the last 50 years (fao, 2010). paradoxically, it is in biological diversity that lies an inexhaustible source of innovation and discovery in the field of scientific research, technological applications or health, food, cosmetic and other products. in this way, the preservation of biodiversity is not only essential for the future of all humanity, both in the north and in the south of the planet, but also for the socioeconomic vitality of europe and of all citizens, who directly benefit from its use. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report on access to genetic resources and the fair and equitable sharing of the benefits arising from their use, which stresses the need for the fair and equitable sharing of the benefits arising from the use of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge, thereby contributing to the preservation of in situ biological and cultural diversity and ensuring its sustainable use by local populations.

in writing. - the report contains aspects which we consider positive and argues that traditional knowledge should enjoy the same level of protection as genetic resources when implementing the nagoya protocol, as well as all the assumptions and the three pillars of the protocol, namely the duty to contribute to the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity worldwide. however, under the pretext of amending the nagoya protocol, the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council masks the fact that large multinationals are patenting biological resources. the commission is particularly concerned about the accusation of european companies of acts of bio-piracy, and is of the opinion that only by authorising or awarding compensation to the countries of origin of genetic resources can the privatisation or patenting of genetic resources be considered to be wrong. the proposal is concerned only with who owns the sources of genetic material, who markets it, who is allowed to enter the chain of marketing and use, and how the sharing of monetary and knowledge benefits is ensured, and only a contract, agreed by both parties, ensures that there is no bio-piracy, nor the illegal sale and exchange of genetic material.

in writing. - the purpose of this proposal, which is part of the motor vehicle technical inspection package, is to support and enforce the technical inspection of motor vehicles with a view to improving road safety and protecting the environment. the proposal improves the application of roadworthiness and roadworthiness inspection schemes, in particular where the technical conditions of vehicles create an imminent risk to road safety, through measures such as suspension or cancellation of vehicle registration. to be marketed, vehicles must meet the applicable requirements for type approval (either of the model or individual) - ensuring an optimal level of safety and environmental performance standards. all member states are obliged to register vehicles which have obtained european type-approval on the basis of the certificate of conformity issued by the manufacturer. the registration constitutes the official authorisation for the vehicle to be used on public roads and the confirmation that the vehicle meets the requirements applicable at the date. i voted in favour of this proposal, which, in the spirit of the above, introduces new and more precise definitions of the location of vehicle registration and the introduction of the suspension and cancellation of registration certificates.

in writing. - i support this report because i believe that transparency is fundamental to the european union as a democratic political union, in order to enable its citizens to participate fully in the democratic process, with access to all the information necessary for informed participation. secrecy and discretion belong to an era when the construction of europe was done by diplomats and civil servants. transparent administration is in the interest of citizens, combats corruption and gains political and legislative legitimacy, and strengthens citizens' trust in the european project. the european union needs to take further steps to increase the transparency of the administration and the legislative process if it is to achieve greater involvement and participation of citizens in the democratic and legislative decisions of the union. there are many new and interesting initiatives, made possible only by new technologies, which provide a better understanding of the activities of the eu institutions and bring citizens closer together. situations such as leaks of information, which reveal problems and irregularities in the institutions, seriously undermine citizens' trust in the european institutions and alienate them from the european project, which is reflected in very high abstention rates in the european elections, for example.
in writing. - transparency is fundamental to a democratic european union of citizens, in which they can fully participate in the democratic process and exercise public scrutiny. citizens have the right to know how the decision-making process works and how their representatives act, to hold them accountable and to know how public money is distributed and spent. transparency is thus the general rule and any decision to deny access to documents should be based on clearly and rigorously defined legal exceptions, be accompanied by a reasoned and concrete justification that enables citizens to understand the refusal of access and to use effectively the legal remedies at their disposal, while it is equally important to ensure that there is a fast and simplified appeal procedure in order to reduce time-consuming and costly litigation. it is also important to ensure that official documents are not given a higher classification than they should have been and that any closed meetings are accompanied by appropriate justification. i therefore support the existence of an open, efficient and independent european administration, which serves the interests of citizens and combats corruption.
in the first place, the european union is built on treaties, it is made up of states and it is at the service of the people. that is why their participation in the process of european integration is so essential. this is also why the lisbon treaty aims to simplify procedures, bring the language of the treaties closer to the citizens and strengthen transparency and public access to the institutions' documents. these mechanisms are fundamental and the key to an informed and participatory european democracy. for these intentions to be put into practice and for the european union to become truly close to europeans, transparent and accessible, there must be real access to documents, which safeguards the right of citizens to information without jeopardising the necessary confidentiality and protection of classified information.
in writing. - this report assesses the years 2011 to 2013 with regard to the importance of public access to documents, noting that increased transparency and transparent administration benefits the interests of citizens and the fight against corruption. the commission is proposing new measures to increase the transparency of its administration and legislative process, in particular by improving communication with citizens who want specific information, which in many cases is not being provided. the report also calls for the establishment of a european independent authority for the classification of documents and the examination of requests for closed meetings, recommending that each institution appoint a transparency officer. we voted yes.

in writing. - this report deals with the difficulty of public access to european union documents relating to the years 2011-2013. the eu needs to do more to increase the transparency of its administration and its legislative process, as this is a key element for a democratic political union of citizens. i agree that an independent authority should be given the task of classifying documents and that all eu institutions should appoint a transparency officer to simplify access to documents. i hold the same view with regard to documents arising from international agreements, since these also have an impact on eu law and should therefore be in the public domain. i therefore support the measures proposed to clarify the situation for the citizens of the union.

in writing. - the report stresses the importance of transparency and access to documents, and states that a transparent administration benefits the interests of citizens, the fight against corruption, and the legitimacy of the union's political system and legislation. it is proposed that further measures be taken to increase the transparency of its administration and legislative process, in particular by improving communication with citizens who wish to obtain specific information, which in many cases is not being provided. the current legislation is not properly applied by the union institutions. as the case law shows, the institutions often apply the exceptions to transparency in a generalised way, rather than in a specifically justified way. often, partial access to documents is not considered. similarly, official documents are often given higher classification than they should be and institutions request closed meetings without adequate justification. the report also calls for the creation of a european independent authority for the classification of documents and the examination of requests for closed meetings, and recommends that all eu institutions appoint a transparency officer. we voted yes.

madam president, madam vice-president, mr president-in-office, ladies and gentlemen, we are living in a time when the value of data protection as a fundamental right is becoming increasingly evident. it's mind-boggling how much personal data is collected and stored every day: the people we know, the music we like, the books and news we read, the money we spend, and so on. the successive scandals we have seen involving security forces from member states of the union and friendly states have reinforced public awareness of the dangers we face and we know that new technologies make this dangerous task easier. european citizens therefore have reason to demand adequate protection of their privacy and hope that their rights and freedoms can be safeguarded and guaranteed. i congratulate viviane reding on her proposal and on the fact that it largely incorporates the recommendations contained in the european parliament's 2011 resolution. although we would have preferred a single instrument, we have accepted the division between a directive and a regulation. the result achieved with the regulation and the directive is far from perfect and i believe that it can be improved. but we cannot accept that the council should proceed with the regulation alone, which would undermine the great aim of this reform, which is to create a legislative body covering all issues and all areas, providing greater clarity and legal certainty and regaining the confidence of the citizens. i therefore call for both reports to be made viable and i congratulate both rapporteurs. there are no perfect solutions, but they are good negotiating platforms for dialogue with the council.
i think the most important thing that's been said in this debate, since it started eight months ago, was said by edward snowden himself, who said, governments cannot do what they're doing on this scale with access to this level of information and with the means they have, without democracy making its decision, without the representatives of the citizens speaking. the citizens' representatives are here and they are speaking, and we are proud that the european parliament was the only parliament to carry out such an inquiry to the end, but on the other hand we have the feeling that we are not being heard. and why don't they listen to us? because they are listening all the time to what we say on our phone calls, our emails, our skype calls, our facebook messages, less to what we say in the plenaries of our parliaments. i therefore appeal to the european commission: we know when the united states starts listening to us, it's when we turn off the information tap. there is at least one agreement, the swift agreement, which the european commission can terminate at any time, which we know is being used beyond its mandate. madam vice president, i call on you to shut down the swift agreement so that instead of listening to what we say through our bank transfers, the united states finally listens to what we say from inside this room.
the european union's relationship with the united states has been shaken by edward snowden's revelations about the nsa's spying activities. the united states has spied and spies, rightly and wrongly, on the communications of european citizens, heads of state and economic agents, using the imperative of internal security embodied in the patriot act and the anti-terrorism legislation adopted after 11 september, which is largely incompatible with the united states' obligations under international law and human rights in particular. and in fact, they are disqualifying the fight against terrorism. the americans argue, and regrettably rightly, that this data was and is provided by the european intelligence services, which in most countries are still under real democratic control. we hope that this scandal will at least serve to force us to review the procedures and to establish democratic scrutiny of the information services in all the member states. the commission should also be able to provide information on the number of cases of fraud in the union, the number of cases of fraud in the member states and the number of cases of fraud in the union. the snowden revelations and the reactions to them, including the important moraes report (here i pay tribute to our colleague who brought it forward), should lead us to a different kind of cooperation with the united states. the internet certainly opens up new doors but also new risks and therefore there has to be a rethinking of the rules on data importation in order to balance the dilemmas between security and privacy of communications. in the framework of the negotiation of the transatlantic trade and investment agreement, this issue has to be taken into account - the protection of our citizens' data - and it is good that this is done before the model agreement itself. we must ensure that european citizens can have administrative and judicial recourse in the united states of america when their privacy is violated and therefore also claim rights of redress. we must also ensure reciprocity in the passenger name record, ensure that the transfer of data of passengers flying to europe also takes place and it is time to review the safe harbour, which is outdated, and review the swift agreement, ensuring reciprocity and redress for european citizens. it is another aspect, which is vital in this report, which is to ensure the protection of whistleblowers, as is the case with edward snowden. without them, we would be more helpless and more ignorant of what is happening in terms of privacy violations today.

in writing. - the single european sky (ses) initiative was launched in 2000 and air traffic management and navigation services were included in the common transport policy. since its inception, the enlargement policy, coupled with an active neighbourhood policy, has extended the european aviation market to 38 countries, making eu aviation a global player. the recast of the regulation on the implementation of the single european sky aims to accelerate the implementation of the reform of air navigation services while remaining faithful to the original objectives and principles. to achieve this objective, it intends, inter alia, to strengthen the independence of national supervisory authorities, strengthen the role of the network operator, redefine the concept of functional airspace blocks, allowing industry to play a more prominent role, and finally to make support for air navigation services subject to open competition.
in writing. - the single european sky (ses) initiative was launched in 2000 and air traffic management and navigation services were included in the common transport policy. the recast of the regulation on the implementation of the single european sky aims to accelerate the implementation of the reform of air navigation services while remaining faithful to the original objectives and principles. to achieve this objective, it intends, inter alia, to strengthen the independence of national supervisory authorities, strengthen the role of the network operator, redefine the concept of functional airspace blocks, allowing industry to play a more prominent role, and finally to make support for air navigation services subject to open competition. only then will we achieve a better internal aviation market and benefit consumers. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. the single european sky (ses) initiative was launched in 2000 and has now included air traffic management and navigation services in the common transport policy. since the creation of the european economic area, the enlargement policy, combined with an active neighbourhood policy, has extended the european aviation market to 38 countries, thus making eu aviation a global player. however, the ses did not produce the expected results. little progress is being made in the bottom-up approach to fabs (interstate airspace management initiatives) and in the overall efficiency of the design and use of the european route network; therefore, the navigation charges, ticket prices, average flight duration or fuel consumption have not decreased sufficiently due to the ongoing ses reform. consequently, airspace users and passengers pay an unnecessary cost in terms of time, fuel consumed and money for the inefficiencies in the aviation chain. the amended proposal properly addresses the expectations of citizens as it is a balanced approach between the views of industry and social needs. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - the second single european sky+ package contains a set of measures to accelerate the completion of a single airspace. it therefore calls on the member states to take a series of measures to make the european space an efficient and functional bloc. i would like to make it clear that the inclusion of the north atlantic region in the single sky legislation would be a clear violation of the international law of the sea, since this region was ceded to us by icao. so while i agree with the general aims of this proposal, i could not accept this inclusion. on the other hand, i also believe that the separation of air services from support services should not be done without an impact assessment, where each member state can assess the effects of this opening. despite these points, i voted in favour of the report as a whole.

in writing. - i approve this report, welcoming the revision of directive 90/314/eec on package holidays, package tours and package tours, in particular in view of the need to ensure that its provisions apply to the online travel business. it should be borne in mind, however, that the holiday travel market is constantly developing, in particular online, and that new business concepts are being developed all the time. one thing that must be avoided at all costs is the development of business models with the sole purpose of circumventing the directive. on the other hand, it is important that existing business models that are working well and that are beneficial to consumers continue to operate. it is therefore desirable that this should not be done too regularly because this would have a disproportionate impact on businesses and could result in models that would no longer be available to everyone.
in writing. - the travel market is constantly changing but it is essential to maintain existing business models that work well and are useful to consumers. it is important to draw up a clear differentiation between package travel and related travel services and to clarify the distribution of responsibility, in particular as regards pre-contractual information. in the event of a change in the travel contract due to price increases imposed by third parties, the traveller should be able to choose between three options: accepting the increased price, accepting the alternative travel arrangement or terminating the travel contract with the right to immediate reimbursement of the travel price, including related expenses. if the traveller does not respond to the written notification of the changes, the trip shall be deemed to have been accepted at the increased price. the report thus seeks to strike a balance between consumers and commercial interests by creating a comprehensible and well-structured regime that is in line with the developments of our time, ensuring a wide variety of business models and offering sufficient and lasting protection to all stakeholders. i therefore support this report.

in writing. - directive 90/314/eec aims to ensure that consumers receive the essential information before and after they sign a package travel contract. it also provides that operators and/or travel agencies are responsible for the proper execution of the package, even when the services are provided by subcontractors, and regulates what should happen in the event of a change in the package contract. it also ensures that travellers are reimbursed for payments made and repatriated in the event of the insolvency of the organiser and/or the agency. in 1990, however, the structure of the transport market was much simpler than it is today, and the internet did not even exist. despite the contribution of that judgment of the court of justice of the european union, it is still unclear to what extent the new ways of combining travel services are covered by the directive. the modernisation of directive 90/314/eec thus responds to the requests made by the co-legislators, the european economic and social committee and the european consumers' consultative group. a large number of industry professionals and consumer organisations also supported this revision. in view of the favourable opinion of the committee responsible, i voted in favour of this proposal for an amendment to the directive which reflects the views of the commission and parliament.

in writing. - i approve this report on the grounds that the european union has called for a reduction of 80%-95% of greenhouse gas emissions by 2050 compared to 1990 levels. according to the european commission's roadmap to a low carbon economy, achieving this target requires 72%-73% reductions in non-co2 emissions (which includes fluorinated greenhouse gases) by 2030. but while all other greenhouse gases have been reduced, emissions of f-gases in the eu have increased by 60% since 1990. hfc-based products and equipment can have a lifespan of up to 50 years. additional legislation is therefore now needed to prevent emissions from rising for several decades to come. fortunately, there are now sustainable alternatives on the market and in use that have proven to be safe and cost-effective and energy efficient. these sustainable alternatives can replace almost all hfc-based equipment now and in the near future. the phasing out of hfcs will enhance sustainable growth, encourage innovation and compensate european industries for investing in green technologies.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the environment is protected and that it is sustainable. it is our duty to leave an environment equal to or better than the one we live in. so all these measures are indispensable, not only for the preservation of the environment but also for our health. the european union is known as the regional organisation that protects the environment the most, and this is another step towards ensuring that this recognition continues to be a feature of the european union.
in writing. - commonly used in a number of industrial sectors as refrigerants, solvents, insulation gases, foaming agents and aerosol propellants, fluorinated gases are hundreds of times more dangerous than co2 for global warming. with demand for refrigeration and air conditioning increasing, especially in developing countries, these gases will account for about 8% of greenhouse gases by 2050. it is therefore important to limit their use, particularly of hydrofluorocarbons (hfcs). the majority of industrialised countries agreed to the premise when they signed the montreal protocol, but there was no agreement at the last meeting of the parties in october 2013 to put these efforts into practice. the existing eu regulation on these gases aims to prevent the use of fluorinated gases where alternatives exist and to prevent their escape where they are still needed. but it is ineffective and therefore needs to be revised. although it should and could be more ambitious, this text is already an improvement on the previous regulation, in particular when it provides for the prohibition of the use of fluorinated gases, with a higher climate impact, in fixed refrigeration systems from 2022 and fixed air conditioning systems from 2025.
- the reduction of this type of gas is very important if the objectives set for 2050 are to be achieved, as it has a warming potential 23 000 times greater than that of carbon dioxide. if the existing regulations are applied, we will be able to achieve the objectives set.
in writing. - the montreal protocol, considered the most successful of the international environmental agreements, has achieved the global elimination and phasing-out of the substances that deplete the ozone layer the most, including chlorofluorocarbons (cfcs) and hydrochlorinated fluorocarbons (hcfcs). hydrofluorocarbons (hfcs) have recently been functioning as substitutes for cfcs and hcfcs, but they are very climatically active. in addition, fluorinated greenhouse gases (f-gases), including perfluorocarbons (pfcs) and sulphur hexafluoride (sf6), have global warming potentials (gwp) up to 23 000 times greater than carbon dioxide and can remain in the atmosphere for thousands of years. in view of the need for action in this area, i voted in favour of this proposal which sets the targets to be achieved by 2030, namely 72%-73% reductions in non-co2 emissions (which includes fluorinated greenhouse gases).

in writing. - the free movement of workers is one of the four fundamental freedoms inherent in the concept of european citizenship on which the single market is based. every eu citizen has the right to work in a member state other than his own and to be free from discrimination in terms of pay or working conditions. this is a right under the treaties and should be directly applicable by the member states. unfortunately, there are still too many legal and administrative obstacles to the free movement and equal treatment of migrant workers in the union, and it is therefore essential to bridge the gap between the rights of eu migrant workers and their exercise in practice by facilitating the correct application of the legislation in force and providing them with the means to enforce their rights. i therefore support this directive which allows for the creation of a common general framework of appropriate provisions and measures to facilitate a more effective and uniform application of the rights conferred on such workers, in particular by strengthening their protection, creating national support structures, raising awareness and promoting a dialogue with the relevant social partners and organisations.

in writing. - although the free movement of workers is enshrined in the treaty on the functioning of the eu as a fundamental freedom of eu citizens, there are still many problems of discrimination on grounds of nationality and these workers face administrative problems, in terms of access to and working conditions, the right to education, training, social security and access to health. this directive aims to provide a more effective tool to protect mobile workers and their families from such discrimination by advocating respect for the different labour models existing in the member states. we believe that there are positive aspects to this directive. however, we cannot dissociate it from a broader context in which the idea of mobility is embedded: an eu of great asymmetries in which the most competitive economies suck the youngest and most skilled labour from the countries facing the most economic difficulties. the high levels of emigration - now called mobility - thus contribute to the increase in asymmetries between exporting and importing countries.

in writing. - i approve the following report as it aims to support member states in establishing strategies to organise legal migration and to increase their capacity to develop, implement, monitor and, in general, evaluate all immigration and integration strategies, policies and measures for third country nationals, including the legal instruments of the union. i agree that the fund should support the exchange of information, best practice and cooperation between the different administrative departments as well as with other member states. i think it is important to provide for the possibility for member states to draw up national programmes in which the actions they take part in may include the immediate family members of third-country nationals, to the extent that this is necessary for the effective implementation of these actions. i also stress the importance for member states to ensure that their national programmes include actions focused on the specific objectives of this regulation, allowing for the allocation of resources in order to effectively achieve the objective of this report.
in writing. - the stockholm programme stresses that well-managed migration can be beneficial for all stakeholders and recognises both the opportunities and challenges inherent in the increasing mobility of people. in the framework of the development of a common asylum policy, in accordance with the principle of solidarity and responsibility-sharing, it is necessary to establish mechanisms aimed at balancing the efforts of member states with regard to the reception and the responsibility for the reception of persons in need of international protection and of displaced persons. a well-organised legal immigration policy, as well as more effective economic and social integration strategies for legally resident third-country nationals, will help to maximise the benefits of immigration. and a credible policy in this area has to include a component of the fight against irregular immigration, as well as the existence of an effective and sustainable return policy. i therefore support the creation of this asylum and migration fund which will allow financial resources at union level to become more flexible and coherent in terms of scope and applicability in order to support the development of the common policy on asylum and migration.
in the case of the united kingdom, the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european union's asylum system is not disrupted. however, the mediterranean region is the one with the greatest instability on its borders, whether maritime or land, so the application of these funds should be closer.
in writing. - policies relating to the area of freedom, security and justice have evolved steadily in recent years. its importance has been confirmed by the stockholm programme and its action plan, the implementation of which is a strategic priority for the next five years covering areas such as migration (legal migration and integration, asylum, irregular migration and return), security (prevention and fight against terrorism and organised crime, police cooperation) and external border management including visa policy), as well as the external dimension of these policies. better economic and social integration of legally resident third-country nationals remains the key to maximising the benefits of immigration.
in writing. - the area of freedom, security and justice is becoming increasingly important for the union, as demonstrated by the increase in the budget available in this new financial framework 2014-2020. in order to make the management and use of funding more efficient, the three funds for refugees, the integration fund for third-country nationals and the return fund have been merged into one. i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that the merger has brought improvements to the new asylum and migration fund.
in writing. - i approve the following recommendation, given that the adoption of the council decision is intended to allow safer and more environmentally friendly recycling of non-eu vessels. on 15 may 2009, the international maritime organisation adopted the hong kong international convention on the safe and environmentally sound recycling of ships. to enter into force and take effect, it will need to be ratified by the main flag states and recyclers. i believe that the adoption of the new ship recycling regulation applies the explicit right, provided for in article 1 (2) of the hong kong convention, to take more stringent measures to ensure truly safe and environmentally sound ship recycling.
in writing. - the international maritime organization adopted in 2009 the hong kong international convention on the safe and environmentally sound recycling of ships. it will enter into force after ratification by the main flag states and recyclers. the export of hazardous waste from the eu to non-oecd countries has been prohibited since 1998 and, due to the various hazardous materials on board, any ship destined for scrapping is considered hazardous waste. unfortunately, it's hard to tell when ships become waste. the export ban has proved difficult to enforce and has been almost systematically ignored by the shipping community since its adoption. the hong kong convention will be a major improvement globally on the current situation and i think we should endorse the council recommendation allowing member states to ratify or accede to the hong kong convention. it will be a step towards safer and greener recycling of non-eu ships worldwide. i believe, however, that only truly safe and environmentally friendly recycling can be achieved by going beyond the provisions of the hong kong convention, as adopted in the new ship recycling regulation.
in the case of the united kingdom, the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the community's fishing fleet is not dismantled. at the end of their useful life, most large seagoing merchant ships continue to be dismantled in low-quality yards located in asia (india, pakistan and bangladesh), usually by the ship-sanding method, resulting in a considerable environmental and health impact. it is therefore essential that the hong kong international convention for the safe and environmentally sound recycling of ships is applied. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i support this report, given that there is introspective work that needs to be done in the eu on this whole process, on the objectives, core values and consequences of operations in relation to the countries of the troika programme in the euro area. the imf's stated objective in its assistance operations under the troika is internal devaluation, notably through cuts in wages and pensions. these actions have particularly affected the most vulnerable social groups, such as women, young people and the elderly. i would also stress the worrying increase in poverty levels. i believe that there is a weak democratic legitimacy of the troika's negotiations and of the eurogroup's decisions, and that this legitimacy needs to be strengthened, given that the troika is a purely technical body. the european parliament must be more involved, giving the process of economic recovery democratic legitimacy and political and social sensitivity. i believe that macroeconomic adjustment programmes should also be evaluated with a view to improving the legal and institutional arrangements for a more effective system of budgetary control.
in writing. - this parliament's own-initiative report aims to assess the action of the troika (the european commission, the european central bank and the imf) in the member states which have requested financial rescues in the course of the economic and financial crisis. in this context, several members of the european parliament visited the member states concerned (portugal, greece, ireland and cyprus) and carried out questionnaires to the entities involved in the adjustment programmes in order to ascertain the effectiveness, democratic legitimacy and appropriateness of the measures taken. the conclusions indicate that the role of the troika was crucial at the time in preventing an economic collapse and much more complicated social situations. although positive, the work of the troika should be reviewed on a number of points, notably the need for enhanced democratic legitimacy and transparency, greater dialogue with the social partners and greater adequacy and flexibility of programmes to the realities of the member states. the main proposals in this initiative, which aims to put an end to the harmful consequences of nascent crisis management systems, include making the financial assistance process fully european, excluding the imf and creating a european monetary fund with a permanent and robust capacity to act. i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. - having voted in favour of the karas/hoang ngoc report (and also the cercas report) on the activities of the troika in the countries under financial assistance, because i agree with many of the criticisms and recommendations, but i do not share some aspects of these reports. firstly, the troika solution was an emergency solution to deal with exceptional situations for which the union was not prepared; the criticism of the legitimacy of the troika therefore seems to me to be frankly exaggerated. secondly, the social situations described are largely the result of the budgetary, economic and social crisis and not of the action of the troika (not to mention the harmful effects of drug overdose, as happened in portugal). secondly, to blame the painful effects of the social crisis mainly on the adjustment programmes ends up by absolving the governments of the countries concerned of their heavy responsibility and provides them with a convenient excuse at the domestic level. the heavy social costs of budgetary and economic adjustment are undeniable, and are aggravated by the inability or overzealousness of national governments. but the balance of adjustment can only be properly assessed against the alternative of non-adjustment, namely budgetary collapse, exit from the euro and perhaps leaving the eu.
