in writing. - i voted in favour of this legislative resolution of the european parliament of 2 april 2014 on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending the regulation on european environmental economic accounts and in which parliament encourages a wider use of data from environmental accounting by the european commission and national administrations to develop specific policies that contribute to the union's policy priorities on green growth and resource efficiency.
in writing. - i know . the development and availability of accurate indicators and descriptive statistics to monitor the evolution of economic and environmental factors and their possible interactions is undoubtedly a useful tool to support strategic planning, the definition of public policies and sustainable development pathways. according to the european commission, most of the necessary statistical data are already available, but they need to be adjusted to have a scientifically sound approach and to ensure european and international comparability. the new models will allow the extension of the available and integrated databases for applications, analyses and better policies in the field of environment and energy. the data obtained can and should contribute to policy evaluation by allowing the environmental impact of economic activities to be measured. three new accounts were proposed and added. environmental protection expenditure accounts, i.e. the national economic resources devoted per resident unit to environmental protection, the quantity of environmental products and services that are created in industry, are also proposed energy flow accounts, energy inputs, energy products and energy waste during production, consumption and accumulation measured in terajoules per inhabitant
in writing. - i approve this report in the hope that a general mobilisation of all development actors will be part of a broad movement to raise awareness among european public opinion of the european union's external action in developing countries. the committee on development of the european parliament is aware that a debate on the poor in the rest of the world cannot ignore the more than 100 million poor people living in the european union. the aim is not to ignore the poor living in the union or to set them against the disadvantaged people in other regions. on the other hand, the fundamental european values are sufficiently rooted both in the provisions on citizenship and in those governing the union's external action. i am in favour of the idea that living five thousand kilometres from the territory of the european union is no reason to lose the right to respect for human dignity. the year 2015 will be a good opportunity to remind us that this right does not depend on a person's place of residence or his or her heritage, but that human dignity is a right for everyone and a basic principle of any european policy.
in the case of the united kingdom, the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to support the development of the community's economy. the coherence of this question is extremely relevant so that in the end we can look back and see that the mission has been accomplished. however, we must not forget to look at the eu itself. there are poor, underdeveloped regions at risk of population desertification. the aid for territorial cohesion must always be geared to the european area and to the idea of a united europe. there can be no imbalances between regions.
in writing. - this legislative initiative, the subject of this report, is the result of a campaign involving representatives of the economic and social committee, the committee of the regions, concord (the european confederation of emergency and development ngos) and the european parliament. the round table organised for this purpose at the 2012 european development days allowed the idea to be disseminated to a wider audience. the european parliament then voted on an amendment calling on the commission to declare 2015 the european year for development. the present legislative proposal is therefore the result of a major awareness-raising exercise. in this context, i voted in favour of the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council declaring 2015 the european year of development, regretting that a political majority had not been achieved for a european year against food waste.
in writing. - i approve this report as it aims to contribute to the development of an independent european space surveillance and tracking capability to prevent and monitor the increasing risk of collision between infrastructure, vehicles or space debris. the need for such a service is shared at national and international level, both by public authorities and by industry as a whole, which depends on space infrastructures. this service is also particularly relevant to ensure the long-term availability of european space resources, in particular the galileo and copernicus satellites. this is the first attempt of its kind at union level and the commission proposes that it starts by pooling the resources and expertise available at member state level and by providing services to users. i am in favour of taking esa's expertise into account by concluding an agreement between the european space agency and the contributing member states.
in the light of the above, the commission will propose to the council that the council adopt a decision on the conclusion of the agreement on the european space agency. all member states with their own sensors will contribute to this programme, which will be led by the eu and not by the european space agency because of its size and importance. the sst programme will be funded under the copernicus and galileo programmes as well as the horizon 2020 programme until the multiannual financial framework is finally adopted and sst becomes self-funding.
in writing. - in its communication of 4 april 2011 entitled 'towards a space strategy for the european union serving the citizen', the commission underlined that the shared competence in the field of space conferred on the union by the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) is linked to a strengthened partnership with the member states. the commission also stressed that all new actions should be based on existing resources and on the joint identification of needs for new resources. i voted in favour of this legislative resolution on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council establishing a programme to support surveillance and tracking in space which, among other measures, calls for the reduction of risks associated with the launch of european spacecraft, the promotion of the control of uncontrolled re-entries of spacecraft or space debris into the earth's atmosphere, and the creation of more accurate and effective early warnings, with the aim of reducing potential risks to the safety of union citizens and mitigating potential damage to ground infrastructure, while seeking to prevent the proliferation of space debris.
in writing. - over nearly 50 years of space activity, more than 4900 launches have put more than 6500 satellites into orbit, of which about half are still there, but only about 1000 satellites are operational and the rest are considered debris. the support framework for space object surveillance and tracking (sst) is designed with the overall objective of contributing to ensuring the long-term availability of european and national space infrastructures, assets and services that are essential for the protection and security of europe's economies, societies and citizens. the sst aims to assess and reduce collision-related risks for spacecraft operations in orbit, as well as to reduce risks related to the launch of european spacecraft, to monitor their uncontrolled re-entries or space debris into the earth's atmosphere, to enable more accurate and effective early warnings and to prevent the proliferation of space debris. the actions under the sst are intended to build capacity at european level for the establishment and operation of a network of ground and/or space sensors of the member states for the monitoring and tracking of space objects and to constitute a database of such sensors.
in writing. - i approve this report in view of the fact that in the current financial framework the budget lines for food security have followed the same position as that established in the framework of the common agricultural policy. however, the new structure of the multiannual financial framework for 2014-2020 provides for a transfer of appropriations from the food security budget lines. this transfer of appropriations for the 2014-2020 programming period entails a significant risk of a budget deficit in the event of a large-scale animal disease outbreak. if such an epidemic were to occur, the union would need to be able to mobilise additional appropriations in a short space of time to finance emergency veterinary or phytosanitary measures in order to avoid losses and further risks to human health. on the other hand, we must find a way of increasing the budget for food security, for example in the event of large-scale agricultural crises. unfortunately, since the overall allocation for the 2014-2020 european union budget is limited, it is not easy to identify other funds that could be used in such cases.
the food sector is extremely important in european policies. the quality to be preserved, the information on the origin of the product, and the harvesting/slaying processes should remain priorities for a more transparent market. this is what distinguishes european products from those of the rest of the world and here the eu gains a competitive edge in what it produces.
in writing. - i know . this regulation is part of the legislative package entitled 'better regulation for safer food', which consists of four sectoral pieces of legislation on animal health, plant health, plant reproductive material and official controls, and a horizontal regulation, which brings together the financial provisions: the regulation on the management of expenditure. the regulation on expenditure management aims to simplify the legislative framework on food supply chain security. the new regulation will repeal and amend 11 previous acts and, in general terms, take up and consolidate existing provisions in a single text. however, some possible funding in the past is forgotten and it is appropriate to allow new expenditure corresponding to the new food safety policy guidelines to be covered. it therefore appears desirable to include the costs relating, in particular, to the slaughter of animals, losses due to emergency vaccination, the possible reinforcement of the current measures, the processing and disposal of carcasses, the economic loss resulting from the measures ordered in the framework of plant protection and the lost value of the destroyed plants. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal, which is aimed precisely at achieving the objectives set out above.
in writing. - the regulation provides for the targets for expenditure relating to the food chain, animal health and welfare, plant health and plant reproductive material, with a total maximum amount of eur 1891.936 million, broken down by sector. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the definition of the term 'competition' and to extend the scope of the term 'competition' to include the use of the term 'competition' in the definition of the term 'competition'. the result of the trilogue improves the regulation by rejecting the amendments proposed by the ep, some of which were interfering with national legislation, others could provide for the allocation of support to the poorest regions of the richest countries, which would mean taking support from the poorest countries (with limited financial volume). the commission also rejected the idea of performance-based evaluation, which could create greater difficulties in weaker member states, and the idea of support in justified cases, whereby the only ones who could justify themselves would be large producers.
in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account that the proposal adopted by the commission does not seek to amend the essential elements of the flegt licensing scheme, but rather to align the provisions on comitology of council regulation (ec) no 2173/2005 with the new regime of delegated and implementing acts enshrined in the treaty of lisbon. the amending regulation now proposed gives the commission the power to adopt both implementing and delegated acts. in my view, the new article on the exercise of the delegation proposed by the commission requires two amendments reflecting the conclusions of the trilogue negotiations on the omnibus i and ii files, which aim to align a large volume of legislation in the area of the common commercial policy with articles 290 and 291 tfeu. the first amendment aims to ensure that the delegation of power is not conferred for an unlimited period, but is limited to five years, which may be extended by an equal period. in other words, it aims to extend the european parliament's monitoring period from four months (2+2) to six months (2+4). this extension is justified in that three areas covered by the delegation involve political consideration.
in writing. - council regulation no 2173/2005 establishes a licensing scheme for forest law enforcement, governance and trade, known as flegt. this scheme aims to tackle the problem of illegal logging and related trade. it applies to certain wood products from partner countries, i.e. countries that have concluded voluntary partnership agreements (vpas) with the eu. in view of these parameters, it provides that only timber products legally produced in accordance with the national legislation of the said partner countries may be imported into the eu. the import of certain timber products from partner countries without a flegt import certificate is prohibited. six countries are developing the systems agreed under a vpa and six others are currently negotiating agreements of the same nature with the eu. i voted in favour of this proposal which does not seek to change the essential elements of the flegt licensing scheme but rather to align the comitology provisions of council regulation (ec) no 2173/2005 with the new regime of delegated and implementing acts enshrined in the treaty of lisbon. the amending regulation now proposed gives the commission the power to adopt both implementing and delegated acts.
in writing. - i approve this report on the grounds that there is broad agreement among all the parties concerned that the current legislation on clinical trials needs urgent revision. there has been a sharp decline in the number of clinical trials conducted in europe in recent years, which is at least partly due to some measures in the clinical trials directive. in addition to the serious economic consequences, this also impedes the progress of medicine to the detriment of patients. europe must be competitive and an attractive place for pharmaceutical companies to develop research, while fostering academic research and encouraging research into medicines for rare diseases. at the same time, europe must be a world leader in patient safety and transparency, in the interests of public trust and scientific rigor. one of the main problems with the current directive is precisely its legal form, i.e. the fact that it is a directive, and a different approach is needed to allow for better results in overall terms.
in writing. - this directive concerns the rules to be applied to all clinical trials for human use conducted in the european union. there are several principles listed which must always be followed without exception for the approval of a clinical trial. the need for approval by an ethics committee is a sine qua non requirement, and participation by risk groups such as pregnant women will be subject to stricter rules. i would therefore like to congratulate all the work that has been done to define strict european rules and parameters in this area.

in writing. - the directive establishing a community framework for the nuclear safety of nuclear installations has entered into force with the aim of initiating the process of creating a common eu framework for nuclear safety. this directive aims to maintain and promote continuous improvement in nuclear safety and, in this context, member states should establish appropriate provisions at national level. the directive covers aspects ranging from provisions on the establishment of national legislative and regulatory frameworks in the field of nuclear safety of nuclear installations to the organisation, duties and responsibilities of the competent regulatory authorities, licensees, education and training of staff, information to the public, and the requirement for the functional separation of the competent regulatory authorities from any other body or organisation related to the promotion or use of nuclear energy. in this context, i voted in favour of this instrument which also provides for self-evaluations by member states at ten-yearly intervals, accompanied by a peer evaluation of their relevant segments, the results of which are to be communicated to the member states and the european commission.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the safety of nuclear installations is not compromised. in 2009, the directive establishing a community framework for the nuclear safety of nuclear installations entered into force with the aim of initiating the establishment of a common eu framework in this field. this directive covers aspects of the establishment of national legislative and regulatory frameworks in the field of nuclear safety of nuclear installations, including the organisation of the duties and responsibilities of the competent regulatory authorities, of licence holders, of the education and training of personnel, of information to the public, and of the requirement for the functional separation of the competent regulatory authorities from any other body or organisation related to the promotion or use of nuclear energy. in accordance with the guidelines of the euratom treaty, this process has reduced the powers of the member states to those of the european commission, a course which, in the light of legitimate concerns for security, serves only the interests of the multinational companies in the sector, putting at risk the access of the population to safe and affordable energy, as well as the safety of workers and the population itself.
in writing. - i approve of this report by stating first of all that, in addition to amending articles 1 and 4 of the dsma, i am in favour of strengthening the definition of parent company so that a further extension of the deadline and the minimum share capital that a parent company must hold in another member state will prevent multinational companies from unlawfully benefiting and distorting competition. it is extremely important that the european union takes the lead in ensuring that multinational companies start contributing proportionately to tax systems. systems must be put in place to combat aggressive, complicated, unfair and unprincipled tax evasion schemes by multinational companies whose sole purpose is to avoid paying their fair share of taxes at a time of european crisis when taxpayers across europe have been pressured to contribute their fair share.
in writing. - as part of the eu's efforts to close the current fiscal gaps resulting from the exploitation of differences between national tax systems, double taxation, and under-taxation, this legislation is intended to contribute to a tax regime with more significant revenues and which fosters fair competition between companies. for reasons of fairness and transparency, as well as economic efficiency, the eu is making every effort to ensure the greatest possible harmonisation of taxation in the community area. the current proposal aims to tackle disparities in the operation and taxation of hybrid financial instruments and introduces a general anti-abuse rule. the rapporteur also proposes to strengthen the definition of a parent company so that multinational companies do not unlawfully benefit from differences in tax legislation and are not able to distort competition. it also seeks to put an end to fiscal dumping and to promote greater fiscal harmonization in the single market. with the erosion of taxable matter taking centre stage in the eu, it is of the utmost importance to ensure that multinational companies contribute fairly to tax systems at a time when taxpayers across europe are pressured to contribute their fair share.
in the case of the united kingdom, the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the taxation of capital is not distorted. in 2013, the european parliament invited the european commission to address the issue of differences between the different tax systems of the member states and to submit a proposal for a revision of the current directive in order to review the anti-abuse clauses and eliminate the double non-taxation facilitated by hybrid financial instruments in the eu. the rapporteur's work on this subject should therefore be commended.

in writing. - i approve this report in view of the fact that greenhouse gas emissions from aviation are increasing rapidly. the international civil aviation organization (icao) predicts that emissions will accumulate to 1900 mt by 2040. other estimates predict 3,500 to 4,500 mt by 2050. 3.5 gigatons is 20 percent of the amount of global emissions that need to be limited according to the ipcc in 2050 to contain climate change. although the kyoto protocol is not enough on its own to curb the effects of climate change, at least on the part of the european union, it has had some effect in limiting emissions. furthermore, no significant action has been taken on aviation emissions. i believe that the aviation industry needs to be involved in the challenge of minimising climate change. it is important to take account of the particular situation of island and outermost regions, for which air transport is sometimes the only viable means of transport. restricting or penalizing air transport in this case may worsen the economic and social situation of these regions, which are already structurally vulnerable by their nature.
in writing. - the issue of greenhouse gas emissions is damaging to all of us. however, the eu cannot be the only actor in the international system seeking to conclude and enforce agreements to this end. i think it is essential that we try to reach agreements, the eu is known for its environmental policy, so it must play a more active role in this area in order to be able to conclude an agreement that is worthy of being honoured.
in writing. - i could not vote for the liese report on greenhouse gas emission allowances for commercial aviation, because flights originating or destined outside the union are exempt, which will benefit all international flights outside the eu, which are exempt from paying. this is an unenlightening concession to the major air powers (the usa, china, russia, etc.) and an exception that is not consistent with the union's policy on combating climate change.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's air transport sector is not left behind. but the solution will not come from integrating more sectors, notably aviation, into market-based regimes which experience has shown are no longer a solution. the sdr is one example of the unequivocal failure of market instruments. we advocate replacing a market approach with a normative and regulatory approach, in a framework for reducing emissions that does not depend on or feed into financial speculation. the issue of greenhouse gas emission allowances and the trading of pollution allowances only serve the large polluters with the capacity to buy the allowances. in addition, smaller airlines such as tap will be the most affected by the inclusion of aviation emissions in the global market. here it is once again demonstrated that the eu's so-called environmental policies do not include a genuine concern for the environment and the future of the planet, being only a pretext for generating profits.

in writing. - i am very pleased to have voted today for a regulation which fully reflects one of the great european objectives, the creation of an internal market. in this particular case, the creation of an internal market for the telecommunications sector, where it was decided that in 2015 the roaming charges which have existed until now in the mobile communications sector would be abolished. in 2015, we will finally see these tariffs abolished and the means of communication within the european union made easier, with more and more families living and working in different member states.
in writing. - i welcome the adoption of the del castillo report on the single market for electronic communications because the new legislative diploma completes the integration of electronic communications in the eu area by abolishing roaming charges for telephone calls, sms, e-mail and data from 2015. this is an essential step in creating a genuine single market for personal communications, facilitating free movement within the union. the european commission's determination and persistence in this matter are to be commended.
in the light of the above, the commission has decided to extend the scope of the directive to cover the whole of the european union. in order for europe to fully exploit the potential for growth, competitiveness and jobs that the digital single market has to offer, it is necessary to strengthen the role of telecommunications in providing innovation and connectivity to all sectors of the economy. indeed, the economies of scale of a telecoms market of 500 million people would allow the electronic communications sector to be strengthened and to provide high quality and innovative connectivity services to european citizens and all sectors of the economy, making europe a strong competitive player globally. the european parliament considers that the completion of the digital single market is a process which needs to be accelerated and the commission's proposal represents an important step forward in this direction. however, taking into account the views of stakeholders, parliament considers that some of the proposed measures should be subject to a more in-depth and structured public consultation and a thorough ex ante assessment of the expected impact and, consequently, be included in the next review of the framework for electronic communications. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - this report aims to deepen the single market for electronic communications in the eu. according to its advocates, electronic communications companies will be able to operate and provide the service wherever their customers are established. however, this is fundamentally a giant step in the further liberalization of the sector which favours the great powers and sharpens the interest of multinationals in obtaining the monopoly of electronic communications, which will be done by destroying more jobs and to the detriment of the interests of workers who will be subject to greater pressure to reduce wages and other rights. the regulation has positive aspects related to the abolition of roaming charges and net neutrality, providing that all internet traffic is treated equally, without discrimination, restrictions or interference, regardless of the sender, receiver, type, content, device, service or application. it also provides for the improvement of certain consumer rights, in particular the right to compensation, the termination of contracts for non-compliant services and contractual amendments, proposals which have been supported by us. the positive aspects do not, however, cancel out a liberalization trend whose consequences will far outweigh them. we voted against it.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that the digital agenda for europe identifies the existing obstacles to europe's digital development and provides for legislation on trust services such as electronic signatures and mutual recognition of electronic identification and authentication. i think it is important that this initiative aims at establishing a clear legal framework that will put an end to fragmentation and lack of interoperability, improve digital citizenship and prevent cybercrime. the adoption of legislation ensuring the mutual recognition of electronic identification and authentication across the eu is also a key action of the single market act and the stability and growth pact. this proposal follows on from what the european parliament has been stressing in terms of the importance of the security of electronic services. i welcome the commission's proposal as a good starting point and the effort to establish a legal framework at european union level. i believe, however, that both the aims and the content of the proposed regulation could be further clarified and it is important that the legislators consider the proposal in its entirety carefully.
in the case of the united kingdom, the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european parliament is able to exercise its right to vote. this regulation will make it possible to strengthen the confidence of institutions, businesses and citizens in electronic signature and identification means. i would therefore like to congratulate the rapporteur on her work on this matter.
in writing. - the european union does not have any general transnational and cross-sectoral framework for secure, reliable and simple electronic transactions covering electronic identification, authentication and trust services. the existing eu legislation on the subject, in particular the directive on a community framework for electronic signatures, covers only electronic signatures. the digital agenda for europe identifies existing obstacles to europe's digital development and provides for legislation on trust services such as electronic signatures and mutual recognition of electronic identification and authentication, with a view to establishing a clear legal framework that will end fragmentation and lack of interoperability, enhance digital citizenship and prevent cybercrime. i voted in favour of the adoption of this legislation which aims to ensure the mutual recognition of electronic identification and authentication throughout the eu and which is also a key action of the single market act and the stability and growth pact. the european parliament has repeatedly stressed the importance of the security of electronic services.
in writing. - we are not opposed to technological progress making it possible to sign documents electronically in a secure, recognised and legal manner, provided that this system does not call into question, in particular, the principles relating to the protection of personal data. this report states that an electronic signature cannot be denied legal effect because it is in that form or because it does not meet the requirements of a qualified electronic signature. however, the legal effect of electronic signatures in the member states should be defined by national law, except for the requirement laid down in this regulation that a qualified electronic signature should have an equivalent legal effect to a handwritten signature. the framework for developing legislation in this area is of course to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market, a framework with which we do not agree because of all the consequences that the internal market in electronic communications has for the people today, in particular because of the privatisation of the public companies that provide these services and therefore the limitation of access to the poorest sections of the population.

banking crises. and this is perhaps the most important piece of legislation since the 2008 crisis, with the bailout of banks involving over 26% of the union's gdp, spending the equivalent of six eu budgets and dragging countries and companies into a crisis that still persists. it was possible to do things differently, and this is what parliament said back in 2010 in the report that commissioner barnier was kind enough to mention. at that time parliament was pressing the european commission to act with courage and determination, and under the guidance of commissioner michel barnier and his team, the answer came. banks are the lifeblood of the european economy. their health determines the lives of companies and families. at today's sitting we will finally approve the european rules which must manage a crisis in a bank in a predictable and organised way, by enshrining the allocation of losses to shareholders and creditors, the so-called bail-in, and financing the resolution through funds fed by the banks according to their risk profile. we will also confirm by law the national guarantee for deposits of less than eur 100 000. for the euro area and the acceding countries, the ambition is higher. the banking union includes single supervision centred on the european central bank, which is already operational this year. but strong supervision would have to be matched by a strong and unique resolution system, and that is what i hope we will also be adopting today. as rapporteur, i am convinced that here too parliament's contribution has greatly improved the council's text. the scheme we will approve centers on the ecb declaring a bank unviable, frees the resolution process from possible and likely political interference by member states and substantially speeds up the constitution of the common part of the resolution fund almost 70% after 3 years. the regime has become more european, more credible and more efficient. because the negotiations were very difficult, the usual thanks are particularly sincere in this case, first to sharon, corinne, sylvie, sven, vicky, the four women and one man on parliament's negotiating team, for their commitment, determination and resistance, but also to the leaders of the political groups, and let me also highlight the thanks of my own socialist and democratic group, and the president of parliament, who accompanied us and politically strengthened our convictions. together we have made the european parliament a negotiating partner of unwavering strength and determination. the council has understood that position. and i thank the greek presidency and minister iannis stournaras, the president of the eurogroup, minister jeroen dijsselbloem, for the serious effort to bring the two co-legislators closer together, and i also thank the whole team at the european commission for facilitating this rapprochement. of course, without our collaborators none of this would have been possible. but we have to follow up on the implementation. we welcome the commitment of the council expressed here today to ratify the intergovernmental agreement before 1 january 2016 and the commitment to have a credit line operational from the start of the operation of the resolution fund. we trust that the interpretation of instruments such as precautionary capitalisation will be consistent with the principle that taxpayers will no longer finance banks. i'll be right with you, madam president. i would just like to remind you that the third pillar of the banking union is a single deposit guarantee system which has yet to be built. this parliament is laying the foundations for breaking the dependence between banks and the state, for protecting taxpayers and depositors, for putting banking at the service of business and jobs. it will be up to the new parliament to ensure that what we have achieved today is not lost in the implementation and deepening phase which is the next phase. thank you so much again.

in writing. - i approve this report, considering that the proposed regulation is part of the effort to create a banking union in the eu in order to increase financial stability and ensure that the european economy can rely on a properly functioning financial sector. the regulation establishes a single resolution mechanism (srm) one of the measures considered by the european council in march 2013 as essential for the completion of the banking union. the srm will apply to euro area member states and other member states that have opted to participate in it. the proposal is based on article 114 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. in parallel with the proposal for a regulation, the commission is also proposing a directive of the european parliament and of the council establishing a framework for the recovery and resolution of credit institutions and investment firms.
in writing. - today, another important step towards the creation of a true banking union has been taken: the creation of a bank resolution mechanism and a single resolution fund. banking supervision will no longer be the sole responsibility of individual national authorities, but will be the responsibility of the european central bank together with all supervisory authorities, and the decision to recover or liquidate a credit institution will now be the responsibility of the resolution authority, the national competent authorities, the ecb and the european commission, creating a more robust system and less susceptible to failures that could endanger europe as a whole. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the environment and the protection of the health of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. for the first time there will be a european mutual fund. finally, i would like to congratulate my colleague elisa ferreira on her work and remind her that ruinous situations such as the bpn in portugal or the savings banks in spain will be increasingly rare in europe.
in writing. - the adoption of the bank resolution mechanism diploma (e. ferreira report) is not only the second fundamental pillar of the banking union, but also the essential building block of the european union's response to the financial crisis that has engulfed europe since 2009. this term will be marked by two historic events: first, the transformation of the ep into a full-fledged parliament under the lisbon treaty; second, the union's overcoming the most serious test of european integration since its inception. happy are those who have had the privilege of being part of this legislature. when i was elected in 2009, i never imagined i'd have this privilege! in presenting my final statement of vote, it could not have been more auspicious.
in writing. - i abstained from the final vote on the single resolution mechanism to signal my objection to the council's impositions in the final agreement. the council undermined the ordinary legislative procedure by applying a method which split the commission's proposed regulation, turning the srm into an intergovernmental mechanism when it should have been communityised. as i have always argued, banking union is essential to stabilise the euro area and break the vicious circle between banking and sovereign debt. a srm that operates in a predictable and equal manner for all member states is essential. instead, this final agreement - despite the great work of the rapporteur and other representatives of parliament, whose importance i recognize - keeps us hostage to the council's political veto. it will therefore retain the decision-making power of the larger member states. this suggests that bank resolution continues to run the risk of resulting from inferior political agreement or continued blackmail on member states with less power or weak budgetary positions. what the eu must have is a banking union commensurate with the needs of the union as a whole. unfortunately, we are being offered a system that will be abused by the powers that be.

in writing. - i approve this report, considering that, in addition to their direct function of protecting depositors, deposit guarantee schemes are also fundamental to the stability of the financial system, particularly in times of crisis. if bank customers lose confidence in their credit institution and simultaneously attempt to withdraw their deposits, the phenomenon known as a 'bank run' may not only lead to the collapse of the institution that is already in a precarious situation, but also spread to other credit institutions and other countries due to the widespread loss of confidence. indeed, no credit institution can maintain such a high level of liquid assets available as is necessary to secure deposits. i particularly agree with the european commission that, with a view to a common internal market, improvements should be made in relation to excessively long payment periods for reimbursing depositors in the event of insolvency and in view of the wide disparities in the financing of guarantee schemes in the various member states.

in writing. - the directive adopted today will harmonise the rules on the opening of payment accounts for consumers, in particular by removing the residence requirement imposed by the member states when opening an account. from today, european consumers will be able to open bank accounts in any country of the european union and will be able to do so with minimum and reasonable fees based on the principle of maximum transparency and access to information. another important step taken with this directive will be to facilitate the opening of bank accounts for all european consumers without exception and without imposing economic barriers and requirements based on the profile of that consumer, thus enabling all european consumers to be included in the financial system, regardless of what they suffer. i would like to conclude by recalling the importance of access to a bank account in our economy, particularly in that it reduces the existence of shadow economies and tax evasion.

in writing. - from today there will be clear, transparent and mandatory rules for all investment products. this means that all issuers of such products are now bound by the same rules and that european consumers are better informed about the conditions and risks of such products. this directive is primarily aimed at investment products for retail investors. pension funds and products intended for such funds are exempted from this directive. so from today, small investors will be more protected by law, in particular because, in case they incur losses due to misinformation by the issuer, they can resort to the law.

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by congratulating my fellow rapporteur on the result of her consistent work on this important report. recent developments in our society and the economic crisis have shown that labour and occupational mobility in the union can make a positive contribution to reducing unemployment and filling temporary labour gaps in certain professions. the current rules governing this matter of posting are not fair because they leave room for non-compliance with labour law by less scrupulous companies and also allow room for legal skills, as exemplified by the creation of well-known post office box companies in member states with weaker social protection. adoption of the rules advocated in this report will ensure that the rights of posted workers are respected and that employers make the most of the potential of the single market. i warmly welcome the measures which will enable more effective labour inspections with national controls and the existence of lists which clearly identify posted workers. i also welcome the transparency and ease of access to information on labour rights and conditions in host countries, which will be available through a single point of contact and a single national website. in conclusion, i would like to stress that improving free movement in the european union must remain a priority.

the rapporteur. - mr president, three final words. first of all, to thank all the kind comments that have been made on my report, but to stress that it would not have been possible without the help of everyone. we would not be here today if the greek presidency had not been able to overcome the blocking minority in the council. we would not be here today if commissioner malmström had not provided us with solutions when we got stuck between parliament and the council. and we would not be here today if the political groups had not been firm in their positions, had not shown the flexibility to find the consensus that was needed. secondly, as the minister has just said, we need more solidarity. this phenomenon is most acute in the southern countries - greece, italy, spain, malta, cyprus - but it has repercussions throughout the european union. a policy of responsibility-sharing and solidarity is essential in this area. finally, madam president, i think we can say that we have found balanced solutions, that is to say, we have not given in to the simplistic solutions that some people like to use in these matters, such as saying that schengen no longer makes sense or that internal borders must be fixed. we have found balanced solutions and, above all, we have proved once again that it is possible to reconcile greater security with the protection of human rights, and in this way we are honouring the values which are our common values.

in writing. - i approve this report, considering that the commission's proposal is extremely important for public health, since approximately 70% of infectious diseases are as common in animals as in humans. the proposal, however, is not aimed at protecting animals in the context of a health law, but at a law on the control of animal diseases in the sense of human protection. it deals with the prevention and control of animal diseases which are transmissible to animals or humans. it is important to emphasize this point (which should also be reflected in the title of the regulation, so as not to be misleading), just as it is also important to clarify that this is not an animal protection law.
in writing. - the importance of animal health for our food, the quality of our products and for animal welfare is of such importance that i cannot remain indifferent to it. animal health, in my view, involves a great deal of effort on the part of veterinary authorities and livestock producers, who every day try to make quality meat and dairy products available to us. the control and prevention of diseases, particularly those likely to affect humans, must be at the forefront of european concerns in this respect. all measures to improve european response capacity and the union's coordination with the member states are welcome. only by working together will we be able to achieve results that are commensurate with the health and safety ambition underlying these matters.
in writing. - the pests present in certain crops are quite harmful to production. there are ways to combat them: chemicals are used to prevent these pests from breeding or a manual weed is used, in this case only applicable to small crops. however, plant pest control sometimes proves difficult to combat chemically because it prevents some species from coming into existence, namely in vegetable products. the greatest difficulty is indeed in relation to vegetable products, and we must therefore rethink the funding of scientific research in this area so that we can reduce the use of chemicals. the commission proposal aims to update and improve the legal framework in order to protect the union from organisms of external origin which threaten plant health and to put in place control and eradication measures. i hope that the content of the proposal will rise to the challenge and that the union will not let down its guard on such a sensitive issue with potentially grave implications for its citizens, for agriculture, livestock and forestry and all related activities.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering it to be intended to provide a consistent response to this fundamental and ongoing debate. in my view, it is indisputable that the effective functioning of the single market depends on two fundamental aspects: safety for consumers and a level playing field for businesses. i believe that only regulation and requirements can guarantee consumer safety. it is necessary to ensure safe products in order to stimulate consumers to buy more products in the single market. product safety is crucial for the effective functioning of the single market and therefore for the growth of european businesses and economic prosperity in the union.
in writing. - it is important that consumers can buy your products knowing that they are safe, where they come from and, where possible, how they are produced. for example, the pdo, doc or organic labels are important. a seal of this kind is usually a guarantee to the consumer that the product is of quality. the lack of safety of products would inevitably lead to a decline in their consumption and an economic setback with serious consequences for the union. even from an economic or commercial point of view, the focus on quality and safety benefits the seller and not just the consumer. i welcome all measures to improve product safety and the traceability of its components, to avoid unfair competition and misleading advertising and to prevent public health problems.
in the light of the above, i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter. the report introduces the eu tested safety marking, which could help consumers to distinguish between ce marking (in accordance with eu standards) and ce + marking (in accordance with safety requirements). we welcome the maintenance of the article on made in in the regulation. its permanence is useful and necessary to enhance the traceability and safety of consumer products, and the indication of the origin of the product is mandatory. we voted in favour.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that the free movement of goods is one of the four pillars of the single market of the european union. this pillar and the smooth functioning of the single market ultimately depend on consumer confidence: european consumers need to have confidence that - regardless of where the product is made and the member state where they can buy it - the products they use are safe and compliant. efficient and high-quality market surveillance should be the ultimate guarantee of this. it shall ensure that products do not present a risk to the health or safety of consumers or persons at the workplace, and shall also ensure that they comply with applicable union legislation. therefore, it should be ensured that they comply with the rules specifying energy efficiency, noise levels and emission limits. however, it is becoming increasingly clear that market surveillance is not overcoming the challenge posed by the increase in imports into the european union and the increasing number of products circulating in the single market. that is why i think this report is important.
the free movement of goods is one of the pillars of the eu. the monitoring must be in place to benefit both consumers and producers. a more transparent and flexible market for all, from which all will benefit. for example, health checks should be a form of control of products, whether in the pre-processing stage or already processed, so that they are not checked when they are already on the market in order to hinder their sale. the purpose of the surveillance is also to prevent unfair dumping practices between member states. this will reduce asymmetries and make trade in products more equal and consistent within the union. market surveillance rules should be objective, clear and understandable and be complied with by all operators. their harmonization and the increase in measures to reduce risks are welcome.
in writing. - this regulation is included in the legislative package on product safety, focusing on eu market surveillance, with the aim of providing the authorities with more effective control devices. the report makes a clear reference to the precautionary principle, placing great emphasis on the obligation of market surveillance authorities to organise their activities in such a way as to maximise their effectiveness and to carry out sample checks to alert consumers to compliance and the risk thereof. another positive aspect of the report is the inclusion of the guarantee of authenticity or origin. ensuring traceability along the supply chain is important to determine the country of origin of the product and the responsible manufacturer, which in the case of imported products also defends european union industries, particularly the portuguese industry. that is why we voted in favour.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that commodity markets are totally different from purely financial markets. you can go a lifetime without being directly exposed to the price of stocks and bonds, but you can't go a lifetime without being exposed to the price of food or energy. commodity derivatives, in the form of contracts that set a price for future delivery, predate financial markets. i understand that commodity markets have arisen out of the legitimate need of producers and consumers of raw materials, agricultural products and energy to protect themselves from the influence of factors beyond their control on prices. however, the growth of financial markets has led to commodities joining bonds and shares as investment assets over the last decade.
in writing. - as of today, the rules on markets in financial instruments will be made more resilient, transparent and efficient. the european union has decided to review the rules on these markets, as in the aftermath of the recent financial crisis it was found that many of these markets were completely unregulated. in order to create more robust safeguards and avoid potential systemic crises, the category of organised trading facilities (otfs) for bonds, structured finance products, emission allowances and derivatives has been introduced into european law to ensure that they are properly regulated and apply non-discriminatory rules for access to the system.

in writing. - the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) is an important instrument for the conservation of threatened species of flora and fauna, as it aims to ensure that international trade in rare or endangered species of wild animals and plants does not threaten their survival by regulating the export, re-export and import of live and dead animals, plants and derivatives. the species covered by cites are listed in three appendices, with varying levels of protection according to their status. the success of cites depends on the effective implementation of the agreed recommendations. council regulation (ec) no 338/97 lays down provisions on the import, export and re-import, and intra-eu trade, of specimens of the species listed in its four annexes, the implementation of cites being at european level. until now, all the amendments made to the lists have been incorporated by means of commission regulations, but after the treaty of lisbon it was considered more appropriate to re-codify regulation (ec) no 338/97 in order to incorporate the necessary amendments, in particular in accordance with the rules of comitology. we voted in favour.
in writing. - the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites), signed in 1973, aims to ensure that international trade in species of wild fauna and flora does not endanger their survival. the species covered by cites are listed in three appendices, benefiting from various levels of protection. council regulation (ec) no 338/97 addresses the protection of species of wild fauna and flora by controlling their trade and also lays down provisions on the import, export and re-export, as well as on intra-eu trade, of specimens of the species listed in its four annexes. i voted in favour of this proposal from the european parliament which calls for the regulation to be recast because it needs to be updated under the lisbon treaty, replacing the old provisions with new and appropriate provisions (including updating the legal basis, i.e. article 192 (1) tfeu, which corresponds to the former article 175 (1) of the ec treaty), in particular as regards the comitology rules.
in writing. - i approve this report, bearing in mind that the economy of seychelles is based mainly on the fishing and tourism sectors. the economy associated with fishing activity developed in the 1980s, boosted by the signing of fisheries agreements with the european union and japan. over the past decade, fishing activity, mainly tuna fishing, has overtaken the tourism industry as the main source of foreign exchange for the country. in 2012, fisheries and related sectors generated revenues of the order of sek 4 864.6 million, or approximately eur 296.6 million, and contributed to 31,4% of the gross domestic product. direct and indirect employment in fisheries and related sectors (ship repair, maritime supplies, port services, fish processing, export activity) is around 5 000 workers, representing about 10% of formal employment in seychelles. in 2012, there were between 1 300 and 1 400 full-time or part-time seychelles fishermen. the european union is thus making progress in its development cooperation and policy at world level and at the same time enjoying the fishing opportunities offered by this island country.
in writing. - fishing is very important from an economic point of view for the whole eu. it must be done in a conscious way so that fisheries resources are not exhausted. we all know the importance of fish for human nutrition. in addition to opening up new fishing opportunities for european fleets, this agreement could help seychelles to improve its fishing capacity and maximise the sustainability of its fisheries resources.
in writing. - the present report, for which i was rapporteur for the european parliament's committee on fisheries, concerns the fisheries partnership agreement between the eu and seychelles. the protocol, which will be valid for six years, provides fishing opportunities for 40 tuna seiners (22 spanish, 16 french and 2 italian vessels) and 6 surface longliners (2 portuguese, 2 spanish and 2 french vessels). the total eu financial contribution is eur 30.7 million, divided between eur 15.5 million for access to the eez, calculated on the basis of a reference tonnage of 50 000 tonnes per year, and eur 15.2 million for support to the seychelles' fisheries sector policy. this protocol allows the european long-distance fishing fleet to maintain its strategic presence and increase its fishing opportunities, boosting the european economy, contributing to the sustainability of fisheries and preventing other international fleets operating without environmental and social concerns from taking the place of the european fleet in this important region for tuna fishing in the indian ocean. i consider the protocol to be balanced and favourable to both parties, and i therefore recommend its adoption and vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account that since 2005 the routes of tuna vessels have been altered due to somali piracy. the progressive expansion of the territory by pirate operations to the whole northern sector of the indian ocean and the seychelles coast during the austral summer monsoon has forced vessels to change their fishing routes considerably. faced with such difficulties and high risks, several ships abandoned the indian ocean. total european fleet capacity decreased by 25% between 2005 and 2009. in recent months, security has been increased on board fishing vessels and fewer acts of piracy have allowed vessels to move further north to the somali coast. however, fishing conditions have not yet returned to the level of the situation that existed before 2005. although the comoros has a fisheries policy, it has few means to implement it and to manage small-scale fisheries and support the development of fisheries. several development partners, for example from qatar, are currently investing in the comoros to set up fish processing units.
in writing. - it is important for the eu to develop partnership agreements of this kind. sometimes it's a way to help certain poorer regions of the globe that have an abundance of untapped resources. the need arises in order to avoid an overload of catch on the fishery resources of the european maritime area. i see it as an investment in preserving our own resources, protecting them and doing everything we can to increase the number of species. however, we must not forget that fishing is the livelihood of many families and communities throughout the eu, many of them the poorest. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the fisheries agreements are properly implemented.
in writing. - this report concerns the establishment of the protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the comoros. this protocol is valid for three years and provides fishing opportunities for 42 purse seiners and 20 surface longliners. the eu financial contribution is eur 600 000 per year, divided into eur 300 000 per year for access to the comorian exclusive economic zone, calculated on the basis of a reference tonnage of 6 000 tonnes, and eur 300 000 per year for support of the comorian fisheries sector policy. if the catches by the european fleet exceed that reference tonnage, the annual eu financial contribution shall be increased by eur 50 for each additional tonne caught. this protocol allows for the consolidation of the strategic presence of the eu tuna fleet in this important fishing region of the indian ocean, provides significant fishing opportunities for the european fleet and enhances partnership and cooperation for the sustainable exploitation of fishery resources in comorian waters. i have voted in favour of this report because i consider that the protocol to this fisheries agreement is balanced and beneficial to both parties.

in writing. - this report concerns the fisheries partnership agreement between the eu and madagascar. the agreement is part of a set of tuna fisheries agreements with several countries in the indian ocean. it will be in force for two years and will provide fishing opportunities for 96 vessels, including 40 tuna seiners and 56 surface longliners. the overall financial contribution to the protocol is eur 3 050 000 (eur 1 525 000 per year), corresponding to an annual amount of eur 975 000 for access to the eez, calculated on the basis of a reference tonnage of 15 000 tonnes per year, supplemented by an annual allocation of eur 550 000 for the development of madagascar's fisheries sector policy. the increase in the reference tonnage (more than 1 700 tonnes per year) was reflected in an increase in the eu's financial contribution (more than eur 328 000 per year). i believe that this fisheries agreement will help to consolidate the strategic presence of the eu tuna fleet and sustainable fishing in this important fishing area in the indian ocean, that the new protocol is balanced and favourable to both parties, and that the electoral process has contributed to the stabilisation of the political situation in madagascar, so i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account that the aim of the recast is to increase the number of restitutions of cultural property classified as national heritage. to this end, the commission proposes to delete the annex to the 1993 directive and to extend the time limits for bringing actions for restitution and for the limitation of the period of validity of such actions. another valid objective of the recast, in my view, is to approximate the laws of the member states as regards the conditions for compensation of the owner of the property to be returned, by assigning the burden of proof to the owner and not referring the matter to the laws of the member states.
in writing. - council directive 93/7/eec on the return of cultural objects unlawfully removed from the territory of a member state was adopted to ensure the protection of cultural objects, including national heritage, when controls at the internal borders of the eu were abolished as from 1 january 1993. in may 2013, the commission proposed a recast of the directive, based on the evaluation reports of the directive, which indicate that since 1993 only 15 refund actions have been brought and of these only 7 have resulted in refunds. this does not mean, however, that few goods have been taken illegally. in fact, an average of 8000 property crimes were reported per year between 2007 and 2010, with a particular focus on france, germany, poland, italy and the czech republic. it is therefore clear that the directive had a limited effect. the purpose of the recast is therefore to make the directive more effective and to increase the number of restitutions of cultural goods qualified as national heritage.
in writing. - the directive on the return of cultural objects unlawfully removed from the territory of a member state was adopted to ensure the protection of cultural objects, including national heritage, when controls at the internal borders of the eu were abolished as from 1 january 1993. at that time, fearing being overrun by refund requests, member states adopted legislation which was quite restrictive and well-founded. however, according to the commission, trafficking in cultural goods, including national heritage, has increased considerably in recent years. this trafficking is the third largest source of revenue for organized crime. the aim of this recast is to increase the number of restitutions of cultural property qualified as national heritage. to this end, the commission proposes to delete the annex to the 1993 directive and to extend the time limits for bringing actions for restitution and for the limitation of the period of validity of such actions. i have voted in favour of this procedure because i agree with the amendments.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that the excessive consumption of single-use plastic bags is not only extremely inefficient from the point of view of resources, but also has negative consequences for the environment. every year, 8 billion plastic bags end up as waste in the european union, including in the sea. despite the increase in resource prices, the current recycling rate for plastic bags is estimated to be only 6,6% and is unlikely to increase significantly in the coming years. because they are so thin and light, plastic bags have little recycling value. increasing the number of recycled plastic bags is also not a solution to the problem. although 39 percent of plastic bags are incinerated, one in two plastic bags is sent to landfill, where it is blown away by the wind and dispersed into the environment. landfills are usually considered the worst option. prevention is clearly the best solution, limiting the use of plastic bags, presenting greener alternatives.
in writing. - the initial proposal from the european commission is a long way from what the rapporteur wants to see adopted today. the commission proposal was simple and aimed at creating incentives for the gradual reduction of plastic bags under 50 micrometres and in accordance with the use made of them by each member state. the aim was to reduce the consumption of these very thin bags, which are being used less and less in favour of stronger and more durable bags, and which tend to increase the levels of waste. the european commission's objective was not, and never was, to eliminate the use of plastic bags altogether, let alone to extend the scope of the directive to the point of legislating on which products may or may not be found in food transport packaging. i therefore condemn the rapporteur's distortion of the commission's proposal, using unsubstantiated information to support her actions and thereby putting at risk various sectors of our economy.
in writing. - the need to reduce the use of plastic bags excessive and resulting from poor economic choices is evident. this can be achieved by campaigns to raise awareness and environmental awareness, by encouraging the repackaging or re-transport of goods marketed by the various sectors and by calling on member states to promote the use of alternatives. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. this report advocates the application of the polluter pays principle, understood here as the reservation of the right to pollute to those who can pay for it. pollution is no less harmful if someone pays more or less. further research and development of solutions to avoid the harm associated with plastic bags by replacing them in their various uses should be pursued. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the quality of life of the citizens of the community, and has recently launched a new initiative to combat the pollution of the environment.
in the european union, the consumption of plastic bags is excessive. nearly 100 billion plastic bags are consumed each year, a number that is expected to increase to 111 billion by 2020 if no action is taken to reduce them by then. this means that on average, each european uses 200 plastic bags in the course of a year. inefficient use of resources and cross-border environmental pollution are common challenges to all eu member states and require a common approach. a consultation carried out by the european commission in 2011 revealed that european citizens would strongly support an intervention at union level to tackle the problem of single-use plastic bags. this is not yet the case in the present proposal from the european commission, which does not call for any action at european level. in any case, this is an important milestone in the development of significant legislative action against the unnecessary use of plastic bags and it deserves my vote in favour.

in writing. - the central organising principle of this regulation is that the financial responsibility arising from investor-state dispute settlement proceedings should be assigned to the agent who granted the disputed treatment. this means that in cases where the treatment in question is granted by the union institutions, the financial responsibility should lie with the union institutions; in cases where the treatment in question is granted by a member state of the european union, the financial responsibility shall lie with that member state. only where the actions of the member state are required by union law should the financial responsibility be borne by the union. in this context, i voted in favour of the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a framework for the management of financial liability in relation to investor-state dispute settlement bodies set up by international agreements to which the european union is a party.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that the commission's proposal to modernise anti-dumping and anti-subsidy regulations involves four key changes: (1) the elimination of the lesser duty rule in anti-dumping cases where there are structural distortions at the level of raw materials and in all anti-subsidy cases; (2) the obligation for union producers to cooperate in ex officio investigations; (3) the reimbursement of duties collected during expiry reviews; (4) and the two-week advance notification in relation to the introduction of provisional duties, commonly referred to as the transport clause. the commission's justification is based on three objectives: (1) to increase the effectiveness of the instruments; (3) to reduce the threat of retaliation by third countries; (3) and to increase transparency and predictability. i welcome these three objectives and believe that they should be combined to maintain public confidence in the instruments.

in writing. - i approve this report, considering that the shipping sector plays a key role in the european economy. the sector is responsible for a large part of the international transport of goods between the european union and the rest of the world, and contributes significantly to the intra-community transport of goods. according to the publication eu transport in figures 2012, in 2010, maritime freight transport in the eu-27 accounted for approximately 1.4 billion tonne-kilometres, second only to road transport. the union-wide maritime passenger transport is less relevant in terms of the number of passengers carried, but it remains an important mode of transport in regions whose geographical characteristics limit the use of other means of transport, such as islands.
in writing. - the eu's targets to reduce greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions by 20% below 1990 levels by 2020 (and ideally by 30%), and the 2011 transport white paper which includes a 40% reduction in co2 emissions from shipping from 2005 levels by 2050, require policies to be implemented in this direction. given the sector's dependence on the combustion of fossil fuels, its emissions contribute to air pollution and climate change. the quantities of co2 and other ghg related to maritime transport are still unknown today, mainly due to the lack of monitoring and reporting of these data. this report presents a monitoring, reporting and verification system which serves the purpose of providing better information, not only on the amount of ghg emissions that are produced by this type of transport, but which will allow concrete data to be obtained and policies to be developed to reduce emissions. this proposal for a regulation goes beyond the monitoring of co2 and adds to the list other ghgs and gases emitted which are also harmful to port cities and the population. this regulation will apply only to vessels between 400 gt and 5 000 gt (gt gross tonnage), covering more vessels. we voted in favour.
in writing. - this report is of the utmost importance for shipping as it is the first step towards the creation of a market-based regime for co2 emissions. i voted in favour of the amendment tabled by a group of meps which aims to exclude island cabotage, i.e. the transport of passengers and persons by sea between ports on the mainland and one or more islands in the same member state, and between ports on islands in the same member state. i do so in the belief that simply applying the proposed scheme would be discriminatory and would impose excessive costs on island regions, which already have only sea and air transport as their gateway. since this amendment did not pass, i voted against this legislative resolution of the european parliament on the monitoring, reporting and verification of carbon dioxide emissions from maritime transport and amending regulation (eu) no 525/2013.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that exotic species are transported out of their natural range through ecological barriers by direct or indirect human action. some of these species can't adapt to their new environment and die quickly, but others can survive, reproduce and spread. only 11% of the more than 12 000 exotic species recorded in europe have an impact on biodiversity and ecosystems, while 13% have some kind of economic impact. however, their effects on biodiversity are significant and invasive alien species are considered the second most important factor in biodiversity loss, second only to habitat loss. given that invasive alien species are recognised as one of the main causes of species extinction, measures should be taken to prevent and manage such situations by avoiding harmful consequences for biodiversity and ecosystems.
in writing. - the release of exotic species into the environment can lead to their proliferation and constitute a threat to indigenous species, with a negative impact on biodiversity and the balance of ecosystems. invasive species are a serious problem in virtually all regions of the world, a process associated with anthropogenic action that has become so acute that it has assumed the dimension of a global crisis, generating extensive negative repercussions on the ecological balance, the economy, agriculture, society, in particular through health problems, and culture. in the eu alone, losses due to invasive alien species are estimated at at least €12 billion per year, which is why the european commission is presenting a proposal for a regulation establishing a list of invasive alien species and the framework for action to tackle this problem. the proposal voted on today has some positive aspects. the commission proposal limited the list of species to 50 and prohibited all trade and marketing of species from this list. this proposal does not limit the number of species and, moreover, takes into account that a species native to one member state may be invasive in another. the importance of emerging species and those with the potential to cause significantly greater damage is highlighted. we voted in favour. we will continue to monitor this matter.
- exotic species are transported out of their natural range through ecological barriers by direct or indirect human action. some of these species fail to adapt to their new environment and die quickly, but others survive, reproduce and spread and even become pests, eliminating endogenous biodiversity. i voted in favour of this proposal, which is based on three key principles: prevention, prioritisation and coordination. prevention aims to reduce the number of new invasive alien species entering the eu, thereby avoiding increased threats to biodiversity and negative impacts on society and the economy. priority setting allows for effective action by focusing resources on the worst invasive alien species, i.e. where the greatest benefits for biodiversity and for society and the economy can be achieved. acting in a coherent and coordinated way across the eu will increase the effectiveness of actions at eu level, i.e. preventing actions in one member state from being undermined by lack of action in another member state.
in writing. - i approve this report in view of the fact that the doha amendment establishes a second commitment period under the kyoto protocol, starting on 1 january 2013 and ending on 31 december 2020. this protocol includes legally binding emission reduction commitments whereby the european union, its member states and iceland commit to limit their average annual greenhouse gas emissions in the years 2013 to 2020 to 80% of their emissions in the base year. in addition, the doha amendment introduced the following changes to the kyoto protocol: first, the inclusion of a new gas; second, an ambition mechanism that provides for a simplified procedure to allow a party to adjust its commitment by increasing its ambition over a commitment period; third, a provision that automatically adjusts a party's objective to avoid an increase in its emissions in the period from 2013 to 2020 beyond its average emissions for the years 2008 to 2010.
