in writing. - i approve this report, recalling that since its inception it has been clear that changes are needed to meet the expectations of the countries and regions affected by disasters that are requesting assistance from the european union. while the instrument generally meets its objectives, its responsiveness is not considered to be as effective as it should be, reflected, for example, in the fact that certain criteria for its activation are too complicated or not sufficiently clear. the process of granting aid is too long and the payment of the grant is late, usually about a year after the disaster. for this reason, i believe that the solidarity fund should improve and simplify the procedures, introduce advance payments and clarify certain provisions so that aid can be paid out more quickly and effectively than it is at present.
in the case of the european union, the european union solidarity fund is the existing mechanism for disaster situations arising from natural disasters such as drought or floods, fires or earthquakes. i welcome the measures to increase its operational capacity and, while respecting its strict budgetary limits and constraints, i hope it can effectively assist victims of disasters which, unfortunately, seem to be occurring more frequently in the european union. in the case of my country, i would like to recall the important aid which the european union has given it through the fund during a wave of fires which particularly struck it. i hope that its greater operability and responsiveness will not be tested too often.
in writing. - the european union solidarity fund was set up to respond to natural disasters and to show european solidarity with the regions affected in europe following the various floods in central europe in the summer of 2002. this fund provides grants to member states and candidate countries affected by a natural disaster. the new legislative proposal simplifies the existing rules so that aid is paid out more quickly. the plans also introduce the possibility of early payments for the first time. these plans give greater clarity on who and what will be eligible, particularly in the case of regional disasters. in addition, the reform encourages member states to develop risk management and disaster prevention strategies on their agenda. the fund's principles remain unchanged, as does its financing, which is not included in the eu budget. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. - i approve this report, given that the commission proposal concerns an amendment to the recovery plan which was initially adopted for bluefin tuna in 2006. in that year, it was clearly recognised that the species was overexploited and depleted, but the contracting parties to the international convention for the conservation of atlantic tunas were reluctant to reduce catches and revenues. however, after several years of policy debate and numerous changes to the recovery plan, the latest scientific analysis on bluefin tuna (2012) suggested that several indicators have recently shown trends indicating that the stock may be recovering. however, it should be noted that scientists are still extremely cautious and state that in 2012 the committee had very limited information on the composition of catches, effort and geographical distribution of the main fisheries in the mediterranean to be able to make a conclusive statement on the issue. i believe that we should proceed with caution on this matter and use more experts and studies to support sound and reliable conclusions.
in writing. - i've always been a conservationist, and i've long been concerned about the illegal capture of tuna. i would stress again that it is important that we exploit existing resources in a responsible way so that they can be maintained in a sustainable way. in the recovery process of this species we should always take into account the impact that its extinction would have on fishing communities and fisheries and fish processing enterprises. i believe that research into the breeding of this species in aquaculture should be considered and, if possible, supported.
in writing. - this report aims to amend certain provisions of the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean, following the adoption of iccat recommendation 12-03, supplemented by iccat recommendation 13-08 on the fishing season for bluefin tuna by vessels using rods and lines (jump-and-line). this report is extremely important for the tuna fleet in the outermost regions of the atlantic, as the previously established fishing calendar for bluefin tuna by this fishing method (1 july to 31 october) did not correspond to the time when this species is most abundant in the azores, madeira and the canary islands. i have therefore been very involved and very active in this document and in the establishment of the necessary political consensus to meet the industry's longstanding demands in this area. after the completion of this work at european level, which culminated in a regulatory amendment allowing member states to freely define the fishing seasons most suitable for the capture of bluefin tuna by the tuna fleets of these outermost regions, it is now up to the competent bodies of the regional and national governments to define the fishing schedule most appropriate to their reality, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i approve this report because according to figures from the european central bank, 184 000 counterfeit euro coins were withdrawn from circulation in 2012, and 531 000 counterfeit banknotes were also withdrawn. olaf estimates that counterfeiting the euro has cost european businesses and consumers approximately €500 million since the introduction of the euro in 2002. i believe that consumers and businesses bear the direct costs, as they are not reimbursed for counterfeits. i am convinced that a harmonised approach to the establishment of criminal sanctions would be a useful deterrent. however, there are a significant number of member states who think that these sanctions are overly ambitious and contrary to the principle of subsidiarity. moreover, given the economic disparities between member states, the introduction of harmonised minimum penalties is likely to have inconsistent effects across the union and thus to be counterproductive.
in writing. - as the single currency shared by the 17 member states that make up the euro area, the euro has become an important factor in the union's economy and in the daily lives of its citizens, and has also become the second most important international currency in the world. the euro thus plays an important role in terms of economic and financial integration in the eu, and the confidence of eu citizens and businesses in the currency is key to ensuring financial stability. however, counterfeiting of the euro remains a matter of concern throughout the eu. since its introduction in 2002, the financial losses caused by counterfeiting have amounted to some eur 500 million, directly affecting citizens and businesses, who are not reimbursed when they receive counterfeit currency, even in good faith, so it is essential to ensure a high level of confidence in the authenticity of the euro. it is therefore essential to ensure that the euro, as a common european 'good', is protected in a consistent manner throughout the union by adopting the measures necessary for the adequate and uniform protection of the euro, in particular by establishing a common definition of offences relating to counterfeiting of currency and by adopting effective, proportionate and dissuasive penalties.
in writing. - this report focuses on recommendations to encourage member states to tackle the criminal offence of counterfeiting in the way they see fit. in particular, the amendment to article 8 is intended to ensure the primacy of territoriality in determining jurisdiction, since it is neither practical nor fair to ask member states to assume responsibility for offences occurring outside their territory, committed by one of their nationals. the european commission is convinced that a harmonised approach to the establishment of criminal sanctions would be a useful deterrent. however, there are a significant number of member states who think that these sanctions are overly ambitious and contrary to the principle of subsidiarity. moreover, given the economic disparities between member states, the introduction of harmonised minimum penalties is likely to have inconsistent deterrent effects across the union and thus to be counter-productive. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that the commission justifies its proposal for reform of the cfp by stating that the european fishing fleet is overcapacity. i would point out that this is a questionable statement, since the commission has not yet defined overcapacity, and it is therefore difficult to prove it. even if certain regions may have a fishing capacity that is too high in relation to the available resource, this situation is specific and localized and cannot in any way be extended to all fishing areas of the union, nor can it be considered a postulate. the commission has also proposed that the fishing fleet be reduced by a further 10% in order to reduce the number of vessels that are caught. i would therefore point out that the commission is proposing to catch the same amount of fish with fewer vessels, thus endangering many small-scale or coastal fishing enterprises and, consequently, many jobs.
in writing. - honey and all bee products are of vital importance to the livelihoods of some eu communities. i understand that honey should be certified because its composition varies from place to place. to give you an idea of how variable its composition is within a country, honey in the central alentejo region is almost entirely made of rosemary pollen and in the northern alentejo region it is almost entirely made of urze or steva. these differences make the issue of their certification somewhat complex, but it should not be abandoned.
in writing. - we have tabled several amendments to this report, always with a view to defending the consumer's right to be informed about the presence of genetically modified organism (gmo) pollen in honey. we are in favour of the obligation to mention the country (or countries) of origin of the honey. in defence of small beekeepers, given the need to carry out product analysis before labelling and the added cost this measure could entail, we proposed that the cost of these analyses should not be charged to the beekeeper and that the eu should compensate affected beekeepers for loss of income due to the contamination of honey with gmos. as a background measure, we proposed that gmos be banned from traditional honey production areas, and that a minimum safe perimeter be set up to prevent contamination. the outcome of the negotiations does not address any of these concerns, with consumers still not being properly informed and small producers subject to contamination of their honey with gm pollen. reasons for our vote against. we recognise the difficulty of dealing with this issue in a framework where the release and large-scale cultivation of gmos in the wild is permitted, as is the case in the eu - a situation which needs to be changed.
in writing. - i voted against this report in the past because i felt that the protection of european beekeepers producing honey without the presence of pollen from genetically modified plants and flowers and the potential value of their production were not guaranteed. the text to be voted on does not allow for a distinction to be made between honey produced from pollen derived from gmos and honey produced from pollen free of gmos, nor does it allow consumers to be adequately informed about the true composition of the honey they buy and consume; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the directive is implemented in a uniform manner. the points i have mentioned remain, and my vote is therefore also negative.

in writing. - this report concerns the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff) which will be operational in the eu for the period 2014-2020. the emff is of great importance due to the reform of the cfp and should reflect the requirements imposed on fisheries operators and promote the environmental, social and economic sustainability of the sector. this report contains measures which are essential for the sector, in particular for its rejuvenation through the integration of young people into fishing, support for the acquisition of a small-scale fishing vessel by young fishermen, incentives for the use of more selective fishing gear, support for the temporary cessation of fishing during periods of biological standstill, support for the improvement of safety and working conditions on board, support for the improvement of infrastructure and conditions in fishing ports, landing sites, shelters and lots, increased funding for data collection, monitoring and surveillance of fisheries. although it does not fully meet expectations, the present report is much more favourable to the fisheries sector than the commission's initial proposal. i voted in favour of this report because i consider that it contains a set of fundamental measures to strengthen the sustainability and competitiveness of the sector and to improve the income of fishermen.

in writing. - i approve this report, stressing that after almost a decade of deliberation, i welcome the commission's proposal for a directive. consumers, as well as small and medium-sized enterprises, are prevented from exercising their rights to compensation for damage suffered as a result of infringements of competition law at eu level. the report also calls for the establishment of a european union-wide network of national authorities responsible for the protection of the environment. however, in my view, horizontal measures which are binding on collective action are not yet a reality. class actions would allow real and qualified entities, such as consumer associations and professional organisations, to bring actions on behalf of the individual plaintiff. however, i urge that only a clearly identified group of persons can act as a representative and participate in the action for compensation. the identification shall be complete when the action for damages is brought and the rapporteur suggests a participation model. i believe that, given that only 25% of cartel cases lead to compensation actions in the european union, more efforts must be made to encourage consumers to exercise their rights.

in writing. - many european citizens claim compensation for infringements in the private application of eu competition law which harm them as consumers or market operators. any individual may claim compensation for damage suffered where there is a causal link between his damage and a breach of eu competition rules. however, there are some obstacles to effective compensation, given the divergence between different national rules on antitrust and compensation actions in the european union. the european commission acted in this field in 2008 by launching a white paper and putting forward concrete policy proposals in this area. in the resulting public consultation, civil society and institutional actors, as well as the european parliament, actively contributed to the preparation of our legislation. parliament therefore broadly supports the creation of a directive in this area which will bring clear benefits in the application of fair and secure competition laws. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. - according to the european environment agency (eea), in 2009 eu member states produced more than 74 million tonnes (mt) of hazardous waste (28% more than in 2000). according to eurostat, in 2010 eu member states produced 101 mt of hazardous waste and 927 mt of waste in total, excluding major mineral wastes. i agree with the objectives of the commission proposal, namely the proposal for firm action against illegal transfers, and therefore i voted in favour of this report. indeed, firm action against illegal transfers is a win-win solution for the environment and health, as well as for industry and the economy.
in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account that new psychoactive substances are substances with the same effects as controlled substances but which are not covered by the united nations conventions on the control of drugs. many of them can have commercial and industrial uses as well as be exploited for scientific and development purposes. when consumed by humans, they may pose health, social and safety risks. in recent decades, there has been a rapid increase in the sales and consumption of these substances in many member states. there is evidence that new psychoactive substances are particularly popular among younger age groups. according to the 2011 eurobarometer youth attitudes to drugs, 5% of young people in the eu have used these substances at least once in their lives; the highest percentage of 16% was recorded in ireland, with poland, latvia and the united kingdom recording values close to 10%. there are more than 300 new psychoactive substances in use today throughout europe. at present, new notifications by member states occur at a rate of approximately one per week.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal to approve the temporary restriction of the marketing of new psychoactive substances. this is an important new feature of the new mechanism which, once adopted by the commission, should remain in force until member states apply the permanent measures. in view of the dynamics of the phenomena and in the interests of efficiency, parliament amended the provisions of article 9 to avoid possible discontinuities between the temporary restriction of marketing and the application of the permanent measures.
in writing. - i approve this report, starting by welcoming the commission's proposal to include new psychoactive substances in the same criminal law provisions as other controlled substances under the united nations conventions. it is therefore vital to amend the scope of the framework decision to include these new psychoactive substances. psychoactive substances, like many other drugs, are a threat to society, as they affect the rational behaviour and common sense of its citizens. these substances affect the functioning of the brain, which in turn causes symptoms such as alterations in consciousness, behaviour and cognition.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive amending the framework decision adopting minimum rules on the constituent elements of criminal offences and penalties applicable in the field of illicit drug trafficking, as regards the definition of drugs. i would stress that the directive laying down minimum rules on the constituent elements of criminal offences and penalties applicable in the field of illicit drug trafficking, as regards the definition of a drug, does not apply to users of psychoactive substances, although some member states may provide for the criminalisation of possession of drugs for personal use at national level.

social democracy has regained government positions in some eu countries, most notably in france and italy. in the first case, the time that has elapsed since hollande became president is very revealing as to the options and the paths followed. the man who promised to change europe and the world has taken over the policies of the right, enshrined in instruments such as the budget treaty, the euro plus pact, economic governance legislation and the european semester. these policies have been the subject of an impressive popular judgment, with the ps/hollande party suffering a resounding defeat in the recent european parliament elections. that is the way, that is the policy of european social democracy. this is also the path, these are also the policies of the italian presidency. the rhetoric of growth and change, with social flourishes and so on, does not hide, in substance, the identity of positions with the european right and the co-responsibility for the neoliberal policies that have brought us to the situation of economic and social disaster that we are facing today in many countries, of which portugal is a painful example. the commitment to free and unregulated trade, evident in the intention to conclude the negotiations on the eu-us transatlantic treaty, is just one example among many others...
the real objectives and results of the troika's intervention in portugal are now clearer. the aim of this intervention was to: (1) increase growth potential, create jobs and improve competitiveness; (2) reduce the ratio of public debt and budget deficit; and (3) safeguard the stability of the financial system. three years on, the results are telling on all fronts: the biggest accumulated recession since the second world war, structural unemployment unseen in a democracy, the bankruptcy of tens of thousands of companies, uncontrolled debt exceeding 130% of gdp and a deficit well above the targets set. a financial system that has channeled millions of public resources to speculative activities contrary to the general collective interest and that is highly vulnerable, as demonstrated by the situation in banco espírito santo, which may lead to developments that are not yet entirely predictable. despair, emigration, desertification, poverty, misery and hunger on the one hand, and the growing accumulation and concentration of wealth on the other. breaking with this path is an undeniable imperative facing the peoples of europe.

i am very honoured to be among the promoters of the resolution which the european parliament is due to adopt on this subject tomorrow. the entry into force of the jurisdiction of the international criminal court on the crime of aggression, defined and approved by the states parties in kampala, will enable the establishment of a system that effectively penalizes the unlawful use of armed force and opens up the possibility of criminal prosecution of perpetrators of violence against the territorial integrity and independence of states parties. the introduction of the definition of the crime of aggression into international criminal law is a necessary civilizational advance to strengthen the jurisdiction of the international criminal court, but also vital to update the united nations charter and strengthen the binding nature of un security council decisions. the crime of assault ushered in a new era in the court's jurisdiction. while the court's jurisdiction has so far focused on crimes of genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes, crimes against individuals and peoples, the criminal jurisdiction over crimes of aggression allows states to be held criminally responsible for the use of military force which is illegal and not sanctioned by the principles of the united nations charter, in particular with implications for the right to self-defence. this is a fundamental civilizational step towards the establishment of a true collective security order. but for that to happen, we need a deterrent, we need to invest ourselves, the european union to invest itself politically in the ratification of the rome statute of the icc and the amendments adopted in kampala by all the states which have not yet accepted the jurisdiction of the court, and in particular those which are our partners in various cooperation agreements. it is also necessary that the mechanisms for activating jurisdiction provided for in the kampala amendments to the statute of the court be used and that the security council commit itself to responsible action in accordance with the charter of the united nations. given the enhanced powers in the matter that give the security council the right to determine whether or not a given event constitutes an act of aggression punishable in the light of international criminal law, which will inevitably raise the bar on whether or not the prosecutor of the court can investigate a case of aggression, then it is vital that the five permanent members do not embark on a strategy of deliberately delaying the prosecutor's work in order to secure immunity for themselves and their allies. a position of the security council is essential in this matter, in accordance with the objectives set out in kampala. the european union, which has built itself up from the rubble left in europe, and not just by nazi germany, must adopt a common position on this matter, as we have called for in this european parliament resolution, without reluctance to act as a bulwark of the icc and the recognition of the crime of aggression.

madam president, the european union must take advantage of the full potential of young people, and young people are a solution, not a problem. it is recognised that the european union has several youth support programmes and has, for example, set aside eur 6 billion to be used this year and next for the youth employment initiative. in this connection, with regard to the youth employment initiative, i would ask the commission: what amounts have been used this year? how much do you plan to use next year? and i ask the council: you're not gonna cut back on payments for this initiative like you've done on other initiatives? and i ask you again: and after 2015, from 2016 to 2020, are you going to end this youth employment initiative program or are you going to provide it with money, with funding, with funding so that this program continues? programmes that support youth employment are an investment, not a cost. the european union must contribute to these programmes which are a valuable addition, as is the case with the youth guarantee. at the same time, it is necessary to create a favourable environment for small and medium-sized enterprises. there is a need to avoid cuts in programmes for growth and jobs cuts in cosme, horizon 2020, erasmus +. these cuts must not be made if jobs and growth are to be a reality in the european union.
in writing. - the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up to provide additional support to workers affected by the effects of major structural changes in world trade patterns and to assist their reintegration into the labour market. regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 provides that 0,5% of the annual ceiling of the egf may be made available each year for technical assistance at the initiative of the european commission (ec). i agree with the european commission's proposal to mobilise eur 330 000 to cover technical assistance costs to the commission, with the aim of following up applications received and financed and proposed and implemented measures, expanding the website and translating new elements into all the languages of the union, increasing the visibility of the egf, producing publications and audiovisual media, providing administrative and technical support to the member states. this funding will contribute to the simplification of the application processes which will allow better access to relevant data, knowledge sharing and information via the website, leading to a more efficient future implementation of this fund.
in the case of the european globalisation adjustment fund, the express objective is the reintegration of workers made redundant as a result of the liberalization and deregulation of world trade. these are unacceptable costs, determined and exploited by those who have brought us into the deep economic crisis we are in and who use it as an argument for the deepening of precariousness and the exploitation of workers. in december 2013, the negotiations to amend the egf regulation gave negative results, with the annual ceiling being reduced from eur 500 million to eur 150 million, while the scope of the egf was broadened. the report agrees with the measures proposed by the european commission to finance technical assistance, in particular the mobilisation of eur 330 000 for monitoring, information, the creation of a knowledge base/interface and advice to member states on the use and evaluation of the egf, although the regulation targets up to 0,5% of the annual maximum amount of the egf (eur 750 000). the report considers that the fund would be more effective and have a much greater impact if the allocation criterion was increased from 500 to 200 workers, and also insists on increasing the total resources to at least eur 500 million. we support it.
in writing. - the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the increasing number of companies relocating to take advantage of low labour costs in a number of countries, including china, india and pakistan, has had a detrimental effect on countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. in this case, the commission requested the mobilisation of the egf to cover expenditure on technical assistance to follow-up on applications received and funded and measures proposed and implemented, to expand the website and translate new elements into all union languages, to increase the visibility of the egf, to produce publications and audiovisual media, to create a knowledge base, to provide administrative and technical support to member states and regional authorities and not to require funds for evaluations in 2014.
in writing. - we regret that in december 2013 the negotiations for the egf produced negative results, with the annual ceiling being reduced from eur 500 million to eur 150 million, while at the same time increasing the scope of the fund. this report agrees with the measures proposed by the commission for the financing of technical assistance, in particular the mobilisation of eur 330 000 for monitoring, information, the creation of a knowledge base/interface and advice to member states on the use and evaluation of the egf. the regulation, however, points to up to 0.5% of the maximum annual amount of the egf (eur 750 000), also stressing the need to strengthen the link between all those working on egf applications, including in particular the social partners and stakeholders at regional/local level, and considers that the fund would be more effective and have a much higher impact if the award criterion was increased from 500 to 200 workers, also insisting on increasing the fund to at least eur 500 million.
in the case of the european globalisation adjustment fund, the official stated objective is the reintegration of workers made redundant who have suffered the unacceptable socioeconomic costs of the liberalization of world trade, which is exploited by those who use the economic, financial and social crisis as the unassailable argument for the deepening of workers' precariousness and insecurity. in december 2013, the negotiations for the egf produced negative results, with the annual ceiling being reduced from eur 500 million to eur 150 million, while the scope of the egf was increased. the report agrees with the measures proposed by the european commission to finance technical assistance, in particular the mobilisation of eur 330 000 for monitoring, information, the creation of a knowledge base/interface and advice to member states on the use and evaluation of the egf, although the regulation targets up to 0,5% of the annual maximum amount of the egf (eur 750 000). the report considers that the fund would be more effective and have a much greater impact if the allocation criterion was increased from 500 to 200 workers, and also insists on increasing the total resources to at least eur 500 million. we support it.
- the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the european globalisation adjustment fund was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic, financial and social crisis. at a time when europe is facing a financial, economic and social crisis, with unemployment as one of the main consequences, the european union should use all the means at its disposal to react, particularly with regard to the support to be given to people who have lost their jobs. i have therefore supported this report on the mobilisation of eur 6096 000 for greece to support the 508 workers, potential beneficiaries, who were made redundant following the layoffs at nutriart sa.
in writing. - the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support to workers made redundant following major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation or the financial crisis and to help them find new jobs. the annual ceiling of the fund for the period 2014-2020 shall be eur 150 million. dismissed workers are offered measures such as support for business creation, job search assistance, vocational guidance and various types of training. in most cases, national authorities have already started to take steps to have their costs reimbursed by the eu when their applications are approved. this mobilisation of the egf in favour of greece is intended to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant by nutriart, its suppliers/producers and the cessation of activity of 24 self-employed workers, totalling 508 persons, and is for a total amount of eur 6 096 000 of the egf. i voted in favour.
in writing. - following redundancies at nutriart sa, the greek authorities submitted an application for a financial contribution from the european globalisation adjustment fund on 5 february 2014. these are redundancies in 25 suppliers and downstream producers and the cessation of activity of 24 self-employed workers whose activity depended on the main company in greece, 508 of the potential workers being beneficiaries of the measures co-financed by the egf. the vast majority of the targeted workers are aged between 30 and 54, in a country where the unemployment rate remains at an all-time high of around 27% of the active population, with the affected regions of attica and central macedonia already at 28% and 30% respectively. this is one of the most bitter and painful aspects of the policy of the european union and of the governments which are submissively applying it. once again, we have agreed to the rapid mobilisation of this aid because it is important to support these workers. however, we reiterate our fundamental criticism of this instrument, since it would be necessary to ensure measures to prevent unemployment, in particular the reversal of the neoliberal course of eu policies leading to such outcomes.

member of the commission. - mr president, i would like to thank everybody who has spoken today. let me first start with the question of whether europe acted quickly. from the humanitarian side, it did. we were the first to bring financial support and to send our own staff – our own doctors are there risking their lives – to mobilise attention to this epidemic. since march when it started, we have been repeatedly giving a very straightforward message from the humanitarian side. this is serious. we have to act in a coordinated manner. already in august, together with the world health organisation, we approached our member states by activating the civil protection mechanism asking for support in kind for the affected communities. very often we in the humanitarian community are like the canary in the mine. we feel trouble and we sense danger before the rest of the world understands the magnitude of this danger. but it is also true that the international community as a whole has not been quick enough to respond to calls, from the doctors in the field and especially from médecins sans frontières, the organisation that has been right there from day one. it has taken some time for the world to recognise – even the world health organisation if i am to be very honest – that this is very serious and requires a massive response. i want to praise our member states because in the last weeks we have seen a surge in reaction from them: just to give you some examples, austria with protective equipment, italy with a field hospital, the united kingdom and france with new centres to be opened and more beds to be provided, hungary with assistance in kind, spain with an emergency unit in the kenema province in sierra leone, etc. our military staff are also looking into how they can contribute – today and tomorrow – to the critical evacuation capability of which many of you have spoken as a crucial need for the medical professions in the field but also, broadly speaking, for evacuation capacity. so we are now finally seeing mobilisation on a global scale. but we also have to stay focused, because in today’s world we are facing crises competing with each other for attention and for resources. not including ebola, we have four level 3 emergencies – this is the highest possible level in humanitarian terms in the world – iraq, syria, the central african republic and south sudan. i would like to respond immediately to those of you have said that we have to create more flexibility in the budget in order to direct funds very quickly to where early action will save lives, but also to reduce the cost, the human suffering and the financial cost of response in the future. i hope that we will work sooner rather than later on this flexibility of response in a more fragile world. i was asked how this virus is spreading. well, it is through the handling of infected chimpanzees, gorillas, monkeys, porcupines, but at the moment we are not seeing it as a danger for the rest of the world because we are not seeing that kind of movement of products. also the virus dies, so from the time between a problem arising and its possible arrival in europe, we do not have a danger. this is what the medical profession is telling us. and also a very direct question: is the opening up of travel a risk for europe? let me first state something you may or may not know: that msf do not have a single case of their international staff being infected by ebola, and they are there, they are in the middle of it. in other words, ebola is controllable. it means washing your hands, making sure that you sanitise before you get on the plane, and of course our airlines are doing that, so i think that we are very strong in our precautionary measures, and therefore we should not worry that keeping this line of communication open is going to be a danger. on the contrary, if we stop this ability to send more medical doctors to these countries and to bring out our nurses and doctors from the most dangerous zones, then the epidemic is going to explode and then the danger to us may – may – become real, because the longer we do not fight, the bigger the risk of this virus mutating. we have been asked about vaccines and using research. at the moment, there is very aggressive deployment of all that has been developed in terms of vaccines and treatment so that we can provide help to people who are infected. but let us be very fair and straight on that: quantities are limited. so can we help everybody who needs help today? the answer is no, and this is why we have to make every effort possible to fight ebola at origin, now, and do it in the most aggressive way we can. my last point is on coordination. i could not agree more that coordination saves lives. we finally have a very strong coordination mechanism from the united nations, with dr nabarro, who is an exceptional professional, and the deployment of the best who staff. but we must also coordinate our own contribution, because if all of us, 28 member states plus the commission, try to help individually, we are putting unnecessary pressure on those who are taking life-saving action today. i am proud to say that last year with your support we created an emergency response coordination centre which is providing a platform for europe to act as one when the need comes, and this is the moment of such need.
president of the council. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to assure you that the council will continue to treat ebola as one of the highest priorities of its forthcoming work and i would like to thank the commission and commissioner georgieva for their work and also for the clarity with which, also in the reply, they reiterated their commitment and the points for concrete action. at the operational level, the needs on the ground remain substantial and include medical and humanitarian personnel, as well as laboratories, hospitals, etc. other health needs are becoming an even bigger problem due to the collapse of health systems in liberia and sierra leone. there are also shortcomings in food and nutrition, agriculture, governance and security. all of these factors can create instability that in turn can contribute to the spread of ebola. further preparedness initiatives should cover all african countries, starting with those most at risk. next week, on 24 september, on the sidelines of the un general assembly, the eu foreign ministers together with international partners and the un will discuss and coordinate the further response to the crisis. we now have a functioning eu response framework to protect eu citizens against cross-border health threats. health services in eu member states are fully aware of the possibility of ebola virus patients arriving in europe and are doing everything possible to prepare for this eventuality, although at present the risk of contracting the disease for eu residents and those travelling to affected countries is considered low. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.
the ebola epidemic affecting west africa is taking on increasingly alarming proportions. the relative passivity with which the more developed countries and the european union have dealt with this problem has contributed to a staggering loss of human life. this is unacceptable and our duty to help is a moral imperative! affected african countries lack health systems that can respond to this disease without it taking on catastrophic proportions! the absence of more vigorous action increases the risk of the spread of the disease and makes it more difficult to control, requiring ever-increasing operational means and scarce containment infrastructure. moreover, the closure of borders and the restrictions on transit to and from the countries concerned threaten the stability of the whole region, which is based on an already fragile economic structure. i therefore call for the immediate deployment of technical and human resources on the ground and for coordination with our international partners for a closely coordinated intervention.

in writing. - the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the european globalisation adjustment fund was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic, financial and social crisis. at a time when europe is facing a financial, economic and social crisis, with unemployment as one of the main consequences, the european union should use all the means at its disposal to react, particularly with regard to the support to be given to people who have lost their jobs. i therefore supported this report on the mobilisation of eur 1 019 184 for spain to support the 633 workers made redundant in 142 factories in the comunidad valenciana region.
in writing. - the egf was set up to provide additional support for workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation or the financial crisis and to help them find new jobs. the annual ceiling of the fund for the period 2014-2020 shall be eur 150 million. dismissed workers are offered measures such as support for business creation, job search assistance, vocational guidance and various types of training. spain submitted an application for the egf, following 633 redundancies in 142 enterprises in the metal products manufacturing sector during the reference period from 1 april 2013 to 31 december 2013, linked to the global financial and economic crisis, which resulted in a reduced demand for and production of metal and metal products by 23,3% in 2009 compared to the previous year and by 36,6% between 2008 and 2013. the turnover decreased by 38,5% during the period 2008 to 2012 and redundancies represent 43% of total employment in the metallurgical sector. in this mobilisation of the egf in favour of the spanish region of comunidad valenciana, eur 1.019 million was granted. i voted in favour.

- the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the european globalisation adjustment fund was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic, financial and social crisis. at a time when europe is facing a financial, economic and social crisis, with unemployment as one of the main consequences, the european union should use all the means at its disposal to react, particularly with regard to the support to be given to people who have lost their jobs. i therefore supported this report on the mobilisation of eur 570 945 for belgium to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant at the assembly plant of ford-werke gmbh (ford genk) and at ten of its supplier companies, resulting from major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation.
in writing. - the egf was set up to provide additional support for workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation or the financial crisis and to help them find new jobs. the annual ceiling of the fund for the period 2014-2020 shall be eur 150 million. dismissed workers are offered measures such as support for business creation, job search assistance, vocational guidance and various types of training. belgium submitted an application to the egf following the dismissal of 512 workers at ford east belgium in genk and ten of its suppliers in belgium during the reference period from 1 july 2013 to 1 november 2013. the redundancies at the assembly plant of ford-werke gmbh and in ten supplier companies of ford genk are related to major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation, with an accelerated decline in the eu market share in the passenger car production sector worldwide and a progressive decline in sales of new cars in the union. in this mobilisation of the egf in favour of genk in belgium, eur 911.934 was granted. i voted in favour.

in writing. - the egf was set up to provide additional support for workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation or the financial crisis and to help them find new jobs. between 2014 and 2020, the annual ceiling of the fund is eur 150 million. dismissed workers are offered measures such as support for business creation, job search assistance, vocational guidance and various types of training. france submitted this application following the 6 120 redundancies at peugeot citroën automobiles, mainly in the île-de-france (aulnay plant) and brittany (rennes plant) regions, during the reference period from 1.10.2013 to 31.01.2014. the commission notes that the psa group's sales volume in the union is estimated at around eur [0-5] million, which is a significant increase compared to the total sales volume of the union industry. in this mobilisation of the egf in favour of the region of brittany and the île-de-france, eur 12 704 605 was granted. i voted in favour.
in the case of the french government, the commission has not yet submitted a proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens. the justification for this further attack on the right to work is repeated: major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation. it is noted that between 2000 and 2012, world production of vehicles increased by 44%, while in the same period production in western europe decreased by 25% and at the same time production in third countries (south korea, china, turkey, indonesia, iran, malaysia, thailand and south america) increased significantly, representing now 47% of world production of vehicles (compared to 15% in 2000). the shift of the automobile industry to countries with lower wages, thus ensuring higher and easier profits, is evident. we are approving palliative measures which, as this case demonstrates, do not apply to all workers made redundant: of the 6120 redundancies, only 2357 are covered by this fund. we must face this wave of mass redundancies head on and attribute to it the real reason: it's the quickest and easiest profit that's talking the loudest. and it is always the workers who pay for the crises that capitalism creates and will never be able to solve.

in writing. - as a portuguese socialist member of parliament, in accordance with the voting orientation of the socialist and democratic group, i have decided to vote in favour of the investiture of the juncker commission, giving it the benefit of the doubt in the face of the political commitments to change made to the european parliament. the vote, despite the reservations expressed, takes account of the serious inconveniences that would result from a political impasse in the european union and is articulated with an attitude of demand towards the new commission, which will continue in its political oversight. in the course of this process, which has strengthened the democratic functioning of the european union, the demanding attitude of the socialists has led to improvements in the proposed commission, such as the allocation of the sustainable development and energy coordination portfolios to socialist commissioners, as well as new commitments on the economic agenda. the appointments of commissioners with the profile of navracsics and katainen warrant reservations. and the lack of clarity in terms of powers, budgetary flexibility and the investment plan calls for a vigilant attitude. the portuguese socialists will continue to demand that the new commission fully comply with the programme of change announced by juncker, notably the €300 billion investment plan promised for the beginning of 2015.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the second amending budget for the financial year 2014. i do, however, share the criticisms made by mr josé manuel fernandes. the council is systematically violating the treaty on european union, which clearly states that there can be no deficit in the union's budgetary year. if commitments made with the authorization of the budgetary authority (and therefore also of the council) are not paid for, this only proves that parliament was right when it complained about the difference between the commitment appropriations and the payment appropriations. they also prove that the council lied when it promised to provide the missing funds if they were to be needed.
in writing. - it is urgent and of the utmost importance for the credibility of the european union to ensure that budgetary imbalances are corrected, as there are insufficient appropriations to pay commitments. these imbalances are caused by the council's repeated policy of increasing cuts in budgets, especially in payment appropriations. the council's position in this and other amending budgets will serve to demonstrate whether or not it is in good faith in this process, whether it is reliable and takes its institutional loyalty. these amending budgets are intended to pay for investments, programmes and projects already carried out and duly authorized, often by the council itself, in favour of smes, young people, scientists, local authorities and ngos. it is unacceptable that the council should refuse to pay what it has asked and authorised. it should also be noted that the council has signed declarations each year, in the context of conciliation with parliament, in which it assumes that it approves the necessary amending budgets for payments which are confirmed. commitments are to be honoured and i hope that the commitments between the institutions and with the citizens will be respected.
in writing. - draft amending budget no 2/2014 aims to enter in the 2014 budget a surplus for the financial year 2013 of eur 1005 million, which is mainly the result of a surplus of eur 771 million of positive differences resulting from the implementation of revenue, eur 276 million from under-implementation of expenditure and eur 42 million from negative exchange rate changes. we agree with the principle of transferring the surpluses of a given year to the budget of the following year, provided that this corresponds to additional revenue! we regret that this budget surplus serves to reduce the proportion of the gni-based contribution of the member states to the eu budget, instead of constituting a much-needed extraordinary revenue to make up for the shortfall of a budget determined by a multiannual financial framework for poverty. even more so in the current situation, marked by the accumulation of debts resulting from expenditure authorised by the eu and the non-payment by some of the member states that contribute the most (and should contribute the most, given the need to implement the redistributive function of the budget...) to the eu budget. that is why we abstained.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the draft general budget of the european union for the financial year 2015, although i criticise the meagreness of the financial resources allocated to the european union. at a time when we are calling for more investment, economic recovery and job creation, we need more europe, not less europe. a budget of less than 1% of gnp is an insufficient budget. especially when we take into account that 94% of the union budget (excluding administrative expenditure) is money that returns to the member states to help public and private investment. the basic accounting and interest-bearing of the so-called net contributors calls for urgent rethinking of the eu's own resources system, which is not largely dependent on payments from the member states.

in writing. - the signing of the additional protocol to the free trade agreement by all member states and the republic of korea has established a set of important principles for the sustained economic development of the european union, further opening a channel for the distribution of its products. as the republic of croatia has been a full member state since july 2013 and is already covered, albeit provisionally, by this protocol, it makes sense for it to continue to participate fully in this free trade agreement, which is still in force.
in writing. - our position on free trade is well known. remembering lacordaire: between rich and poor, between strong and weak, it is the law that liberates and freedom that oppresses. trade deregulation is a way for the stronger economies to tap into new markets at the expense of the progressive dismantling of weaker production systems. asymmetries between countries are growing. and in all of them a race to the bottom is forced in terms of workers' rights and wages. by putting the workforce of different geographical origins in competition, it forces its general devaluation. since the european parliament's approval is a mandatory component of the completion of the ratification process of the additional protocol to croatia's accession to the eu, this report is essentially technical in nature, since we are not deciding on the creation of a free trade area or on croatia's accession, but on adapting existing legislation to take account of the consequences of accession. our position on accession is well known: the european union is a political union, a political union of the peoples of europe, a political union of the peoples of europe, a political union of the peoples of europe. that is why we abstained.
in writing. - the accession of croatia as an eu member on 1 july 2013 entails the need to approve an amendment to the protocol to the free trade agreement between the european union and the republic of korea. it is a pro forma measure to preserve the integrity of the internal market of the european union.
written. - the council of the european union concluded on 6 march 2014 the additional protocol to the free trade agreement (fta) signed on 15 october 2009 between the eu and its member states, of the one part, and the republic of korea, of the other part, which already provided for the accession of croatia to the european union, which took place on 1 july 2013. since that date the additional protocol to the eu-south korea fta has been applied on a provisional basis. the council decision thus ensures that croatia, following its accession to the eu, can continue to participate fully in the eu-korea fta, which remains in force. in this respect, and because it is a mandatory component of the completion of the ratification process of the additional protocol, i voted in favour of this recommendation, which contributes to maintaining and preserving the integrity of the european internal market.
in writing. - since the approval by the european parliament is a mandatory component of the completion of the ratification process of the additional protocol of croatia's accession to the european union, it is no less true that this moment should serve for a deep reflection on what eu enlargement has been over the past decades. this enlargement has not contributed to the development of these countries. in fact, despite the initial aid, they do not conceal the weakening of the productive apparatus, with very serious social consequences. even the infrastructure subsidized by european funds is now serving the large industry of central europe, thus proving that enlargement is mainly based on a strategy of expanding markets and attracting cheap labour.
in writing. - the european semester is now an essential tool in coordinating the economic and budgetary policies of the member states. despite the encouraging signs of the past two years, in a context of overall unemployment, particularly youth unemployment, persistently high public debt levels, low nominal gdp growth, banking crisis and fragmentation of the labour market, this coordination becomes vital to support the eu's economic recovery in order to deliver more growth and jobs. i believe it is important and necessary to adopt an ambitious initiative to stimulate investment across the eu and to revive the economy, boosting european investment by eur 300 billion as proposed by president juncker. i also believe that it is a matter of priority to focus our efforts on strengthening competitiveness, supporting job creation, combating unemployment and monitoring reforms to improve the financing of the economy and labour markets, objectives which the european council had already set in march.
in writing. - in this global world, the eu must be competitive, uphold its values and social status, and ensure that all resources are able to promote sustainable growth, job creation and territorial cohesion. the economic environment in europe is further characterised by a sluggish gdp (increased by 0.2% in the eu28 in the second quarter of 2014), markedly low inflation (reduced by 0.3% in august 2014) and an excessively high unemployment rate (11.5% in the euro area and 10.2% in the eu28 in july 2014). the economic recovery in the eu has shown encouraging signs over the past two years, but it is still fragile and uneven, and an ambitious initiative to stimulate investment across the eu is urgently needed to re-launch and support economic dynamism. these are the expected completion of the banking union and urgent reforms for all member states where the difficulties of setting up businesses are a barrier, as well as moving forward with a €300 billion european investment programme, as proposed by jean-claude juncker, to help europe recover in the short term from growth.
in writing. - this report comments on the implementation of the european semester in the last semester and makes recommendations for the next, which will start with the publication of the annual growth survey by the commission at the end of november. the report is full of the rhetoric of socially balanced and sustainable growth, the call for job creation and the fight against youth unemployment, and everything that is intended to make us believe that we are entering a new cycle. the enthusiasm is marked by the promise to increase investment by 300 billion euros - the solution to all ills! the truth is that the european semester is an attack on the interests and aspirations of workers and peoples, an anti-democratic process, an attack on the rights of sovereignty. more recessionary policies that destroy thousands of jobs every day is the meaning of this process. the paper is the best: development of smes, with the aim of promoting sustainable, smart and inclusive economic growth and quality employment; combating youth unemployment; and so on... this report calls not only for the continuation of this unacceptable process but for the deepening of its basic features. we obviously voted against it.
in writing. - after six years of economic crisis and negative growth rates, the economic recovery is slowly gaining ground and is expected to spread to all member states by 2015. the commission's forecasts for economic recovery are still weak and reforms must continue to meet citizens' employment and social needs and to restore productivity and competitiveness. in many areas of the eu, social conditions are poor and unemployment has reached unprecedented levels. measures to address this social and unemployment situation are needed, which would improve the prospects for competitiveness and growth. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - we are equally in solidarity with the ukrainian people. that is why we condemned the illegal coup d'état supported by the eu and the us. we also know that the eu is helping the people of ukraine in portugal. in exchange for financial aid, the eu will impose economic liberalisation. it will dismantle the productive apparatus of that country, which is not in a position to compete with the big european companies. the eu is not trying to help. it only wants to expand its market to new consumers and gain access to raw materials from ukraine. if the eu wants to help, it must demand that the current coup government in ukraine respect human rights. that you stop supporting the fascist militias that persecute trade unionists and other social activists. condemn the attempt to outlaw the communist party of ukraine and investigate all the crimes committed, with particular reference to the crime in odessa. this is the help that the eu should be giving.

in writing. - the agreement on specific aspects of the organization of working time in the inland waterway transport sector lays down minimum requirements for safety and health at work which have positive aspects. such as the right to at least four weeks of paid annual leave and to benefit from free annual health checks. however, many of the principles laid down run counter to the demands of workers in the sector, particularly in portugal. the agreement provides for an average working time of 48 hours, whereas portuguese legislation provides for 40 hours. it also provides for a maximum reference period of 12 months, which allows for working hours of more than 8 hours. in addition to other provisions which may lead to greater flexibility and deregulation of working time. although the directive states as its objectives the protection of the health and safety of workers in a sector with predominantly cross-border characteristics, it is necessary to ensure that the most favourable national legislation is not prejudiced by the application of the directive.

i would like to begin by expressing once again, on behalf of my party, our solidarity with the cypriot people, who have been living under turkish occupation since 1973, when turkey invaded the northern part of the island and killed thousands of people. this crime continues, to this day, with impunity. this occupation has never been recognized by any state, except turkey itself. this invasion of the exclusive economic zone of cyprus is an unspeakable provocation which must be condemned in the strongest terms. we have once again noted the double standard of the european union: a european union that is quick and ready when it comes to following nato and the united states' directives, but that is nothing more than pious declarations when it comes to the sovereignty of one of its states. i hope that the european union will go further this time by imposing sanctions on turkey and thus help to continue the peace negotiations with a view to reunification.
the conflict in south sudan, which has dragged on for almost a year, lacks an urgent political solution. the united nations representative on sexual violence in armed conflict told the security council just a few days ago that in her thirty years of experience she had never seen such human suffering, particularly of women and children who are victims of rape with weapons of war and on ethnic grounds. and this is also the framework in which humanitarian ngos are being prevented, including by the sudanese government itself, from intervening. it is time to question the very capacity of igad to mediate the peace process when igad member countries are accomplices, supporters and also responsible for dragging the conflict along. the european union has a lot to do with the existence of south sudan. you can't wash your hands! we must urge the un security council to intervene - now - to impose an arms embargo on south sudan that should have been in place by now. and to impose targeted sanctions at the highest level so that they actually understand that this cannot continue. the inclusion of civil society in the peace process must also be urgently called for, because otherwise we are in fact contributing to the systematic breach of ceasefires. a peace agreement cannot guarantee impunity for those responsible for the violence in southern sudan. we must include a hybrid special court - with international involvement - or determine the jurisdiction of the international criminal court to investigate and punish war crimes and crimes against humanity committed in southern sudan. only in this way can we one day build peace in this country so tormented.
i shall only speak of the application of these agreements on swiss territory. this is a matter of very serious concern because there are some 120 000 portuguese workers in switzerland. these workers are present in many sectors, from construction, to the hotel industry, to metalworking, to watchmaking... obviously, a large number of these workers suffer the scourge of unemployment. the portuguese social security system does not automatically recognise social benefits granted by switzerland. that is, it covers pensions, disability and the unemployment benefit itself. we therefore support these measures which aim to harmonize social security rules and thus facilitate the mobility of workers.
the european union needs an intelligent policy for coordinating migration within its territory and between it and third countries. a wise policy must first of all be fair and humane, but it must also take account of the creation of the best economic and social conditions for the permanent or temporary integration of migrants. we need to attract talented and creative people to the european union. we cannot close the door to the despair of those who try to cross our borders in the name of survival, but it is bolder and more courageous if we are able to put into practice an active policy of openness and exchange. the more migrants who arrive in the union - not in a desperate flight, but as part of a common project they want to share - and the more europeans who leave our territory not in disillusionment, but with a universalist sense and a global vision, the more humane and sustainable the migration policy of the eu can be. that is the sense of the proposed amendments, although they are clearly insufficient, and they deserve my support.
the approval of this agreement means the surrender of moldova and its sovereignty to the interests of the major economic groups and the major powers of the european union. as we know with regret, this agreement will severely restrict the taking of measures in portugal to protect its national production. it will put workers under pressure to cut wages and benefits even further. the removal of customs barriers will open up the public sector to competition from foreign firms. the agreement will subject workers, small and mediumsized enterprises and small and mediumsized farmers to a process of fierce competition, requiring them to sell the products of their labour at a discount. as a corollary, it will increase the pressure on external and internal balances, increasing deficits and debts. a common story in many countries in europe.
