in writing. the request for waiver of immunity was triggered in the context of statements made by ms ana gomes during a televised debate, with a view to allowing criminal proceedings to be brought against her and her to be questioned in the same proceedings. in the television programme in question, ana gomes, a member of the european parliament, spoke about the portuguese government's decision to privatise the viana do castelo shipyards. as a result of the sub-concession to private owners of the land and facilities of the viana do castelo shipyard, the company was dismantled and the overwhelming majority of its workers were laid off. the pcp has denounced and fought against this crime against the country from the very beginning, including in the european parliament, and the psd, cds and ps share responsibility for it. the principle underlying parliamentary immunity provided for in article 8 of the protocol is that members are free to take part in debates and to represent their constituents on matters of public interest. this principle is not a personal privilege of members but a guarantee of the independence of the whole parliament and its members in the performance of their duties. we therefore support the rapporteur's vote not to waive ana gomes' immunity.
in the case of the european parliament, the commission has the power to adopt decisions which are binding on the member states. in accordance with article 8 of the protocol on the privileges and immunities of the european union, members of the european parliament may not be subject to any form of search, detention or prosecution for opinions or votes they express in the performance of their duties. this request for withdrawal is made by a prosecutor of the lisbon criminal investigation and prosecution department in the context of allegedly defamatory statements made by ana gomes during a televised debate, in order to allow a criminal case to be brought against ana gomes and for her to be questioned in the same case. the ep considered that in the television programme in question, ana gomes had appeared as a member of the european parliament to discuss matters of interest to her at european level, as was shown in particular by the questions for written answer which she had submitted to the commission. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the application of the principle of proportionality. i am therefore in favour of defending the parliamentary immunity of mrs ana gomes.
in writing. - without calling into question the legal correctness of the decision of the committee on legal affairs, i decided to abstain on the grounds that the statements in question deserve a judgment of political censure.
in writing. - in the television programme which gave rise to the request for waiver of immunity, ana gomes spoke as a member of the european parliament, drawing attention to the decision of the portuguese government on the privatisation of the viana do castelo shipyard a decision which also gave rise to an investigation by the european commission into the violation of eu state aid provisions. as a result of the sub-concession of the private use of the viana do castelo shipyard, the company was dismantled and the overwhelming majority of its workers were laid off. the principle underlying parliamentary immunity provided for in article 8 of the protocol is that members are free to participate constructively in the debate and to represent their constituents on matters of public interest. this principle is not a personal privilege of members but a guarantee of the independence of the whole parliament and its members in the performance of their duties. we therefore support the rapporteur's vote not to waive ana gomes' immunity.
- the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the european globalisation adjustment fund was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic, financial and social crisis. at a time when europe is facing a financial, economic and social crisis, with unemployment as one of the main consequences, the european union should use all the means at its disposal to react, particularly with regard to the support to be given to people who have lost their jobs. i therefore supported this report on the mobilisation of eur 1 501 200 for ireland to support the 171 workers made redundant at andersen irland limited.
in writing. - the egf was set up to provide additional support for workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation or the financial crisis and to help them find new jobs. the annual ceiling of the fund for the period 2014-2020 shall be eur 150 million. dismissed workers are offered measures such as support for business creation, job search assistance, vocational guidance and various types of training. in most cases, national authorities have already started to take steps to have their costs reimbursed by the eu when their applications are approved. ireland submitted an application for a financial contribution from the egf, following the redundancies of 171 workers in the jewellery manufacturing company andersen ireland limited, operating in nace rev. 2 division 32, which are linked to major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation, as imports, 95% of which are from asia, have increased by four times the eu production over four years (2008 to 2012). in this mobilisation of the egf in favour of greece, eur 1,5 million was granted. i voted in favour.
in writing. - following the redundancies of 171 workers at andersen ireland, the irish authorities submitted an application to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund. given that these redundancies have a serious impact on regional employment and the local and regional economy and that unemployment levels in this rural region are already more than twice the national average, the irish authorities have included in the application the request for funding for up to 138 unemployed young people under 25 years of age who are not in education or training, which will bring the number of targeted beneficiaries to 276. the application was submitted under the criterion that at least 500 employees were made redundant or self-employed persons ceased their activity. however, due to the exceptional circumstances presented, a derogation from the 500-redundancy threshold is justified in order to accept the application. it is regrettable that governments and the eu insist on policies that lead to economic degradation, business closures and mass layoffs. more than the recurrent mobilisation of this fund, what is required is an end to the neoliberal policies which are at the root of these problems and the defence of the preservation of jobs.
in writing. - the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the number of companies relocating is increasing, taking advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, with harmful effects for countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has already been used in the past by other eu countries and this aid should now be granted to ireland, which submitted an application egf/2014/007 ie/andersen ireland in order to obtain a financial contribution from the egf, following 171 redundancies in the company andersen ireland limited, operating in the nace rev. 2 division 32 (manufacture of jewellery, ornamental articles and similar articles) during the reference period from 21 october 2013 to 21 february 2014.
in writing. - ireland has submitted an application to receive a financial contribution from the egf, following 171 redundancies in andersen ireland limited, which operated in the nace revision 2 division 32 (manufacture of jewellery, goldsmithing, jewellery and similar articles) during the period from 21 october 2013 to 21 february 2014. under that application, ireland also proposes to provide personalised services co-financed by the egf to a maximum of 138 young people under 25 years of age who are not in employment, education or training. the commission considers that the application meets the eligibility criteria laid down in the egf regulation, as the redundancies in question have a serious impact on the economy of this region, where the unemployment rate (39,3%) was already more than double the national average (19%), and as the redundancies are linked to major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation, as imports in this sector, 95% of which come from asia, have become four times the eu production. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, which approves the decision to mobilise the egf for ireland.
in writing. - financial assistance to workers affected by redundancies as a result of globalisation should be provided on an individual basis and aimed at their reintegration into the labour market. on this basis, ireland submitted an application to the egf in respect of redundancies in 171 workers at andersen ireland limited, which was active in the economic sector of manufacturing of jewellery, goldsmith's items, jewellery and similar articles. although we are dealing with less than 500 redundancies in a four-month reference period, i believe that the exceptional circumstances surrounding the admissibility of the application deserve to be taken into account, given the serious impact on employment and the local, regional and national economy in ireland. i therefore voted in favour of this report on the mobilisation of eur 1 501 200 for ireland.
in writing. - the irish authorities have submitted an application to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund following the dismissal of 171 workers by andersen ireland. these redundancies have a serious impact on regional employment and the local and regional economy, and unemployment levels in this rural region are already more than double the national average. the application was submitted under the criterion that at least 500 employees were made redundant or self-employed persons ceased their activity. however, due to the exceptional circumstances presented, a derogation from the 500-redundancy threshold is justified in order to accept the application. it is absolutely regrettable that governments and the eu insist on policies that lead to economic degradation, the closure of businesses and mass layoffs, as has been the case whenever this fund is requested. what is required is an end to the policies of liberalization and profit maximization which are at the root of these problems and the defence of the preservation of jobs.
- the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the european globalisation adjustment fund was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic, financial and social crisis. at a time when europe is facing a financial, economic and social crisis, with unemployment as one of its main consequences, the european union should use all the means at its disposal to respond, particularly with regard to the support to be given to people who have lost their jobs. i have therefore supported this report on the mobilisation of eur 7 290 900 for greece to support workers made redundant by sprider stores s.a.
in writing. - the egf was set up to provide additional support for workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation or the financial crisis and to help them find new jobs. between 2014 and 2020, the annual ceiling of the fund is eur 150 million. dismissed workers are offered measures such as support for business creation, job search assistance, vocational guidance and various types of training. in most cases, national authorities have already started to take steps to have their costs reimbursed by the eu when their applications are approved. greece submitted an application for a financial contribution from the egf, following the redundancies caused by the global financial and economic crisis, in 761 workers at sprider stores s.a., a company active in the economic sector classified under nace rev. 47 division. in this mobilisation of the egf in favour of greece, eur 7.29 was granted. i voted in favour.
in writing. - the greek authorities have submitted an application to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund for the company sprider stores sa following the dismissal of 761 workers under the economic crisis criterion. this company is active in the retail trade. the number of workers made redundant includes self-employed workers whose activity has ceased in the supplying undertakings or in the downstream producing undertakings of the supplying undertaking. two circumstances are identified as giving rise to the redundancies: 1) reduction of household disposable income due to the increase in the tax burden, the decline in wages (both in the private sector and in the public service) and the increase in unemployment which resulted in a huge fall in purchasing power; 2) drastic reduction of loans to companies and individuals due to the lack of liquidity of greek banks, linked to the economic crisis. in the face of this situation, we reaffirm that the solution is not to give a subsidy in exchange for the loss of jobs, which, moreover, has no price, but to reverse the neoliberal policies that have been responsible for these situations, carried out by the governments of the member states and encouraged by the eu, which the report itself describes as causing this social problem.
in the case of the european union, the european union is a space of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the increasing number of companies relocating to take advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, has had a detrimental effect on countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has already been used in the past by other eu countries and this aid should now be granted to greece, which submitted the application egf/2014/009, el/sprider stores on 6 june 2014, following the redundancies of 761 workers in sprider stores s.a., an enterprise operating in the economic sector classified under nace rev. 2 division 47 (retail trade other than motor vehicles and motorcycles).
in writing. - greece has submitted an application to receive a financial contribution from the egf, following the redundancies of 761 workers at sprider stores s.a., which were engaged in nace rev. 2 division 37 (retail trade other than motor vehicles and motorcycles) during the period from 17 november 2013 to 17 march 2014. under the terms of that application, greece also proposes to provide personalised services co-financed by the egf to a maximum of 550 young people under 30 years of age who are not in employment, education or training. according to the commission, this application fulfils the eligibility criteria laid down in the egf regulation, as the redundancies in question are linked to the economic and financial crisis, which, as is well known, has led to a huge fall in purchasing power and consumption, a drastic reduction in lending to businesses and individuals due to the lack of liquidity of banks, as well as a significant increase in the unemployment rate and a sharp decrease in greek gdp. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, which approves the decision to mobilise the egf for greece.
in writing. - in the face of structural changes in international trade, it is important that the european economy is able to effectively implement the union's instruments to support workers affected by unemployment, such as the european globalisation adjustment fund, and thus to (re) train them for (re) integration into the labour market. i voted in favour of this report, as it will allow the mobilisation of eur 7 290 900 for greece, with the aim of supporting not only the workers made redundant by sprider stores s.a., but also providing personalised services co-financed by the egf to a maximum of 550 young people under the age of 30 who are currently not working, not studying or even in training.

in writing. - by approving the conclusion of this agreement, the majority of the european parliament supports the capitulation of moldova and its sovereignty to the interests of the major economic groups of the eu powers, severely limiting or even preventing the taking of measures to defend its national production and exposing workers there and here to pressure to further reduce wages and rights. the measures envisaged, in particular the creation of the comprehensive and deep free trade area - the essence of this association agreement - will lead to the abolition of customs and tariff barriers, the opening of public procurement to private and non-moldovan companies, and the prevention of the establishment of limits on the establishment of foreign companies in moldova. the agreement will put workers, smes, small and medium-sized farmers - most moldovans - in one of the poorest countries in europe in a process of fierce competition to force them to sell the cheapest product of their labour and their labour force. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.

in writing. - on 12 june 2013, the commission published a proposal for a council decision on the approval, on behalf of the european union, of the luxembourg protocol on specific matters relating to railway rolling stock annexed to the convention on international guarantees for mobile equipment materials, adopted in luxembourg on 23 february 2007. on 20 november 2013, the council adopted a decision on the approval, on behalf of the european union, of the protocol and on 14 april 2014 it requested the approval of the european parliament. i supported this recommendation which creates a register of international guarantees for railway rolling stock and is complementary to the european vehicle identification number system adopted under the railway interoperability directive. it also promotes not only capital investment in the railway sector, but also benefits the creation of a genuine market for mobile railway equipment in europe and also encourages innovation and investment in the eu railways.
in writing. - the aim of the proposal is the eu's approval of the protocol on specific issues relating to railway rolling stock. the cape town convention establishes a uniform regime for the establishment and effects of an international guarantee. the convention applies when the debtor is located in a contracting state and strengthens the rights of creditors if the debtor fails to meet its obligations by creating an international creditor system that allows creditors to register collateral in relation to various categories of movable property and to benefit from rules on the priority and enforceability of collateral. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union's institutions. we shall follow our group's position in voting against.
in writing. i voted in favour of the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the draft council decision on the adoption, on behalf of the european union, of the protocol on specific questions relating to railway rolling stock. several provisions of the railway protocol allow the contracting parties to make declarations as to the applicability or scope of its provisions, or even as to how they will be applied. the railway protocol advocates the transition to greener and more sustainable modes of transport, such as rail, an objective that was highlighted in the 2011 transport white paper.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which gives its agreement to the protocol on specific questions relating to railway rolling stock annexed to the convention on international guarantees in respect of materials of mobile equipment, adopted in luxembourg on 23 february 2007, on the understanding that the said protocol, by establishing an international system of registration of guarantees, will contribute to promoting capital investment in the sector and enhancing the functioning of a genuine market for mobile railway equipment in europe, and is compatible with union law and the objectives set out in the 4th railway package and the 2011 white paper on transport.
in writing. this proposal concerns the approval by the european union of the luxembourg protocol on specific matters relating to railway rolling stock and is an annex to the convention on international guarantees for mobile equipment materials, adopted in luxembourg on 23 february 2007, hereinafter referred to as the railway protocol. it was signed by the eu, by prior council decision, on 10 december 2009. the rapporteur notes that the proposal under discussion is intrinsically linked to the implementation of the fourth railway package, which includes the objective of advancing innovation and investment in this sector at european level by using greener and more sustainable modes of transport. i therefore believe that the essential conditions for the european parliament to have given its favourable approval to this proposal, which i consider to be beneficial in creating a genuine and sustainable market for railway equipment in europe, are fulfilled.
in writing. - the cape town convention establishes a uniform system for the formation and effects of an international guarantee, namely: contract for the formation of the guarantee, contract for the reservation of the right of ownership and lease agreement for certain mobile equipment. it includes legal provisions that apply to all categories of mobile equipment and a set of specific protocols providing for specific rules for certain equipment. the proposal under discussion is closely linked to the implementation of the fourth railway package, which includes the objective of encouraging innovation and investment in the eu railway, with the general trend towards privatisation in the railway sector.
in writing. the objective of the proposal is the eu's approval of the protocol on specific questions relating to railway rolling stock annexed to the convention on international guarantees in respect of mobile equipment materials. the eu decided to sign the rail protocol and did so in december 2010. the convention applies when the debtor is located in a contracting state and strengthens the rights of creditors if the debtor fails to meet its obligations by creating an international creditor system which allows creditors to register collateral in relation to various categories of movable property and to benefit from rules on the priority and enforceability of collateral. according to the proposal, the objective of the rail protocol is to facilitate the financing of high value railway rolling stock by creating a strong international guarantee for creditors, whether they are credit sellers or institutions providing credit for such sales. as the proposal under discussion is closely linked to the implementation of the fourth railway package, with the general trend towards privatisation in the railway sector, we voted against it.
- the hague convention essentially gives the international dimension to the revised brussels i regulation as regards agreements on jurisdiction in commercial and civil matters. this is intended to increase legal certainty for both businesses and consumers. and these in particular find their position especially safeguarded, since insurance contracts are excluded. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. - the aim of the hague convention is to promote international trade and investment by strengthening judicial cooperation, which involves the introduction of uniform rules. the convention seeks to strike a balance between: (i) the need to ensure that parties are assured that only the courts they have chosen will hear the case and that the judgment given will be recognised and enforced abroad, and (ii) the need to enable states to implement certain aspects of their public policy, relating in particular to the protection of the weaker parties, protection against serious forms of injustice in certain situations and respect for certain criteria of exclusive competence of states. it thus creates a worldwide alternative resolution mechanism to the existing arbitration system. this report is a recommendation for the adoption of the convention. the european commission has declared that it has competence in respect of all matters governed by the convention. the member states are therefore bound by the eu's conclusion of the agreement, which gives rise to some reservations. we recognize, however, the essentially technical nature of this recommendation.
in writing. i have tabled my vote in favour of the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the approval, on behalf of the european union, of the hague convention of 30 june 2005 on the forum election agreements. the choice of court agreements are agreements in which two parties agree that any matter in dispute between them shall be decided by the courts of the designated state. i believe that the european union should participate in this convention, which the union signed in 2009. widespread accession to this convention would ensure greater legal certainty with regard to exclusive choice of court agreements, promoting trade between the participating states.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which gives its consent to the adoption of the hague convention of 30 june 2005 on agreements on the election of jurisdiction in civil and commercial matters, as it is of great relevance in the context of international trade, ensuring respect for private autonomy and the necessary legal certainty in cross-border transactions.
in writing. one of the objectives of the european union is to create a common legal area based on the principles of judicial cooperation and mutual recognition of judicial decisions. in that regard, the hague convention of 30 june 2005 established an international legal framework for exclusive choice of court agreements in civil and commercial matters, in which the parties stipulate that any matter in dispute between them is to be decided by the courts of the designated state. i therefore considered it important to vote in favour of this recommendation approving, on behalf of the european union, this convention, not only because of the valuable contribution it makes to the autonomy of the parties in international commercial transactions, giving them predictability and legal certainty, but also because of the guarantee given to the parties that their choice of judicial settlement will be respected and that the decision given by the chosen court will be capable of recognition and enforcement in international cases. the eu's approval of this convention will thus reduce legal uncertainty for european companies operating outside the union, while maintaining those that meet its objectives of extending its competence and legal harmonisation in international trade.
in writing. - the aim of the convention is to promote international trade and investment by strengthening judicial cooperation, including the introduction of uniform rules on jurisdiction, based on exclusive choice of court agreements, and on the recognition and enforcement of judgments given by courts chosen by the contracting parties. the council proposal states that the eu's approval of the convention will reduce legal uncertainty for european companies operating outside the eu by ensuring that the choice of court settlements included in their contracts is respected and that judgments given by the courts designated in those settlements will be eligible for recognition and enforcement by the other contracting parties to the convention. overall, the eu's approval of the convention will complement the achievement of the objectives underlying the eu rules on the extension of jurisdiction by creating a harmonised set of rules in the eu in relation to third countries that will become contracting parties to the convention. it is part of the creation of a common judicial area based on the principle of mutual recognition of judicial decisions.
the express objective of the convention is to promote international trade and investment by strengthening judicial cooperation through the introduction of uniform rules of jurisdiction based on exclusive choice of court agreements and on the recognition and enforcement of judgments given by courts chosen by the contracting parties. the council proposal states that the eu's approval of the convention will reduce legal uncertainty for european companies operating outside the eu by ensuring that the choice of court settlements included in their contracts are respected and that judgments given by the courts designated in those settlements will be eligible for recognition and enforcement by the other contracting parties to the convention. article 6 of the convention imposes some limits on article 5 by stating that the court of a contracting state other than the court chosen shall suspend or declare itself to be incompetent to hear a case to which an exclusive choice of court agreement applies. this report is a recommendation for the adoption of the hague convention of 30 june 2005. the convention was signed by the eu in 2009. the current step is the ratification process and we have not objected.
in writing. - the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the european globalisation adjustment fund was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic, financial and social crisis. at a time when europe is facing a financial, economic and social crisis, with unemployment as one of the main consequences, the european union should use all the means at its disposal to react, particularly with regard to the support to be given to people who have lost their jobs. i therefore supported this report on the mobilisation of eur 1 426 800 for finland to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant at stx finland oy.
in writing. - the egf was set up to provide additional support for workers made redundant following major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation or the financial crisis and to help them find new jobs. in 2014-2020, the annual ceiling of the fund shall be eur 150 million. measures such as support for business creation, job search assistance, vocational guidance and various types of training are offered to dismissed workers. in most cases, national authorities have already started to take steps to have their costs reimbursed by the eu when their applications are approved. in this egf mobilisation, the finnish authorities submitted on 27/05/2014 an application egf/2014/008 fi/stx rauma for a financial contribution from the egf, following the redundancies of 577 workers in stx finland oy, an enterprise operating in the economic sector classified under nace rev. 2 division 30 manufacture of other transport equipment, on the grounds that the global maritime industry has undergone dramatic changes in recent years and that in this overall context the eu market share in the shipbuilding sector has decreased from 13% in 2007 to 5% in the first 3 quarters of 2013, while the equivalent share of the whole china, south korea and japan increased from 77% in 2007 to 86% in the same period. i voted in favour.
in writing. - i know . following the dismissal of 577 workers at stx finland oy, a manufacturer of transport equipment, the finnish authorities submitted an application to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) for a total of eur 1 426 800. the application is justified on the basis of the dramatic changes that the global maritime industry has undergone in recent years, affecting the company's market share in the shipbuilding sector, which fell from 13% (2007) to 5% (in the first 3 quarters of 2013), an expansion of the asian shipbuilding market, and the decline in orders resulting from the economic crisis led to a weakening of the sector. we understand the need to help immediately to improve the situation of these workers, in particular by mobilising the proposed amounts. however, as we have said on several occasions, the mobilisation of this fund cannot be used to make redundancy policies viable by promoting the worsening exploitation of cheap and unfair labour. in this case, the deregulation and liberalisation of the shipbuilding and ship repair sector worldwide, which the eu has been vigorously promoting, must be denounced as having inseparable consequences.

in writing. finland applied for a financial contribution from the egf, following 634 redundancies in stx finland oy, which operated in the nace rev. 2 division 30 (manufacture of other transport equipment), during the period from 7 october 2013 to 7 march 2014. according to the commission, this application fulfils the eligibility criteria set out in the egf regulation, as, on the one hand, the redundancies in question are linked to major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation, as the eu market share in the shipbuilding sector decreased from 13% in 2007 to 5% in the first three quarters of 2013 due to the expansion of the asian shipbuilding market and the decline in orders resulting from the economic and financial crisis, and, on the other hand, such redundancies will further aggravate the unemployment situation in the rauma region, with a high risk of prolonged unemployment given the low level of education and the advanced age of the workers affected. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, which approves the decision to mobilise the egf for finland.

in writing. - these amendments are intended to allow the ecb to use confidential statistical data information in the performance of its new banking supervisory tasks. in addition, amendments are proposed to ensure that the same statistical information as that collected by the ecb in the context of its new tasks is transmitted within the escb, and that only the ecb can collect it. the authorities or bodies of the member states and the eu responsible for the supervision of financial institutions, markets and infrastructures or for the stability of the financial system may only have access to this information when it is transmitted to them by the escb. this report only adds to the concern about the physical and electronic protection of information, which must be ensured by technical, administrative and regulatory measures. the amendments tabled once again aim to empty the supervisory powers of the national institutions, and to ensure that confidential and important information passes through the ecb's screening first after the escb and only then through the national institutions, all in order to protect information that is important for the markets. this proposal comes as the ecb's role is being deepened and the sovereignty of the states is being lost in this strategic sector, in areas such as supervision and control. we voted against it.

in writing. - this regulation is a further step towards the implementation of the banking union, in particular the single supervisory mechanism (ssm). this ssm gives the ecb new supervisory powers in relation to euro area banks, such as the authorisation of all banks in the eu, the application of the single rulebook in the euro area, direct supervision of large banks (130) and monitoring of the supervision of less significant banks by national supervisors. under this regulation, the ecb may at any time decide to carry out direct supervision of one or more credit institutions, and national competent authorities may only impose sanctions on credit institutions directly supervised by the ecb when the ecb requests them to initiate a procedure to that end. in addition to usurping supervisory powers from national institutions, since this regulation gives the ecb supervisory functions that were previously performed by national institutions, such as banco de portugal, this regulation gives the ecb a significant administrative sanctioning capacity and states will lose control, regulation and intervention powers over banking, thus further limiting the possibility of this strategic sector being placed at the service of economic development. we voted against it.
this report follows the establishment and implementation of a single mechanism for banking supervision in the euro area, the single supervisory mechanism (ssm). the regulation gives the ecb new supervisory powers in relation to euro area banks, such as the authorisation of all banks in the eu, the application of the single rulebook in the euro area, the direct supervision of all significant banks, including those with assets of more than eur 30 billion or representing at least 20% of their home country's gdp (about 130 banks), and the monitoring of the supervision of less significant banks by national supervisors. this also means that this regulation gives the ecb the ability to impose administrative sanctions and thus reinforces its position as the most powerful non-democratic entity and apparently holder of an endless mandate. the member states are thus weaker in the area of regulation and intervention than they were in the case of banking. for these reasons i voted against.
the financial crisis has revealed the need for better regulation and supervision of the eu's financial sector. new rules have been adopted to ensure that all financial players, products and markets are properly regulated and effectively supervised. these standards create a basic framework for all 28 eu member states and form the basis for the smooth functioning of the single market for financial services. for regulation to be fully effective, it must be accompanied by strict supervision and enforcement. the objective is therefore to improve supervision of the financial sector at eu level, on the one hand, by improving coordination between national supervisors and, on the other hand, by strengthening supervision at eu level, under the ecb's top management, in order to address risks and issues with cross-border implications. the two levels of supervision are complementary and fundamental to preserving financial stability in europe. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a council regulation amending regulation (ec) no 2532/98 on the power of the european central bank to impose sanctions, considering that, in view of the new tasks of the european central bank (ecb) in the field of the prudential supervision of banking institutions, these amendments are justified, which are essentially aimed at defining the specific rules concerning the maximum limit of sanctions imposed by the ecb in the exercise of its supervisory tasks (new article 4a), the specific procedural rules for the imposition of such sanctions, including the review procedure (new article 4b) and the specific time limits applicable to administrative sanctions imposed by the ecb in the exercise of its supervisory tasks (new article 4c). the credibility of the single supervisory mechanism is enhanced if the ecb has clear and unequivocal authority to impose sanctions on banks that are in breach of the law.
in writing. since 4 november this year, the single mechanism for banking supervision in the euro area (single supervisory mechanism - ssm) has been fully operational. in this respect, the amendment to regulation (ec) no 2532/98 - on the power of the european central bank (ecb) to impose sanctions, which preceded the creation of the ssm, constitutes an important step in the effective implementation of a more coherent and effective regulatory framework. the ssm confers new supervisory powers on the ecb in respect of euro area credit institutions, including the authorisation of all banks in the eu and the consistent and coherent application of a single set of rules in the euro area, the direct supervision of significant credit institutions (about 130) and, finally, the monitoring of the supervision of less significant credit institutions by national supervisory authorities. in addition to the obvious need for updating, the enhancement of the credibility of the ssm requires that the ecb has a clear and unequivocal authority to impose sanctions, and this report proposes a number of amendments to that effect, which i support and voted in favour of. i would like to conclude by recalling that the ssm is a fundamental step towards the achievement of genuine economic and monetary union in europe.

in writing. climate change poses a potentially irreversible threat to human societies, biodiversity and the planet, and therefore requires an urgent and determined international response. the measures to be taken include, inter alia, the conclusion of an agreement at the paris climate conference in december 2015 (cop 21) establishing an ambitious, legally binding international agreement for climate action beyond 2020; the urgent strengthening and broadening of existing measures to limit greenhouse gas emissions by 2020; and the increase of financing by developed countries for reduction, adaptation, technology transfer and development and capacity building in developing countries, as well as the simultaneous increase of official development assistance to meet the long-promised target of 0,7% of gross national income. in this regard, it is appropriate to underline the importance of the next united nations climate change conference (cop 20), to be held in lima, peru, from 1 to 12 december 2014, and to call on the eu and its member states to play a constructive and leading role in it.

in writing. as in previous resolutions, we agree on greenhouse gas emission reduction targets; greater concern with meeting the targets set and the need for other, more ambitious targets (in line with the ipcc recommendations). we agree with the principle of sharing responsibility and helping developing countries to cope with the consequences of climate change. since the main polluters, the causes of such changes, are the richest and most industrialized countries, the truth is that the most serious consequences for the populations are felt in the countries with the least capacity to respond, where the socioeconomic circumstances are most unfavourable to their populations. the objectives of the kyoto protocol, with these mechanisms, which were to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, with co2 as an index, have been replaced by the desire to see another functioning, free market generating millions of euros, becoming a business opportunity, as we have always said. this parliament is simply proposing green solutions, such as a part of the revenue from this market being allocated to financing the fight against climate change.

in writing. article 42 of the srm regulation provides for the establishment of a single resolution board, which should be fully operational as of 1 january 2015. in accordance with the powers conferred on it in article 65 (5) of the srm regulation, the commission adopted on 8 october 2014 a delegated regulation on the provisional system of advance payments of contributions to cover the administrative expenses of the single resolution board during the transitional period. taking into account that the regular functioning of the council as from 1 january 2015 requires that it establishes its financing arrangements as soon as possible and in any event before 1 january 2015 so that it can cover its first administrative expenditure (staff remuneration, infrastructure, administrative and operational expenditure) from its own resources, and considering furthermore that the council will have an autonomous budget, which is not part of the union budget, but is financed by contributions from the banking sector, i voted in favour of this decision to raise no objections to the said commission delegated regulation of 8 october 2014.
in writing. - we understand the need to make operational the policy decisions taken by the commission and the council. we understand that the single resolution board needs the means now to be able to start functioning as early as january 2015. however, we reject these policies of regulation, devised in the wake of the financial crisis, which centralize control mechanisms to the detriment of the sovereignty of countries. we therefore think that this crisis should lead to a rethinking of the whole architecture of the financial system, focusing the discussion on the need for public control of banking and financial institutions as the only way to ensure the proper functioning of the economy. as such, we refuse to be associated with this single resolution mechanism, and therefore opt for abstention.

in writing. we agree with the aim of improving the rigour and credibility of the impact assessment (ia) process, ensuring that economic, social and environmental aspects are assessed in equal depth and that the approach is carried out in all initiatives legislative proposals; commission legislative and work programme; non-legislative initiatives that define future policies; and commission delegated or implementing acts that may have significant identifiable impacts. but it is not this concern that is at the heart of the proposals put forward by the commission and its president. we have the strongest reservations about the advisory body called better lawmaking, which is mentioned in the resolution. the commission's proposal is based on the principle of subsidiarity and proportionality, and the representatives of the interested parties are convinced that the lobbyists will have a greater say in the whole legislative process, from the source. moreover, under the pretext of avoiding that smes are disproportionately affected or harmed by the commission's initiatives compared to larger companies, what is actually intended is to further weaken the ai instrument. in view of these contradictions, we could not vote in favour.
in writing. ai, as an instrument at an early stage in the development of the legislative framework, plays a crucial role in the commission's smart regulation agenda, with the aim of providing transparent, comprehensive and balanced data on the economic, social and environmental consequences, the added value of eu action, the expected administrative and regulatory burdens, and the costs and benefits of alternative lines of action for all stakeholders. the commission's commitment to regularly review the ia guidelines with a view to improving the ia procedures is therefore to be welcomed.
in writing. impact assessments are an important tool to support decision-making in the legislative process, as they allow data to be collected on the economic, social and environmental consequences of legislative proposals, the added value of eu action, the expected administrative and regulatory burdens, and the costs and benefits of alternative lines of action. it therefore seems to welcome the commission's initiative to revise the guidelines on impact assessments with a view to improving the procedures for impact assessments. the draft revision presented does, however, have some shortcomings which need to be addressed, in particular as regards the clarification of the role of the jrc and the strengthening of its independence, the introduction of the reference to the sme test, the approach to the exclusion of micro-enterprises from the scope of legislative proposals and the updating of impact assessments following the changes introduced during the legislative process. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, which rightly calls on the commission to present a new draft guideline on impact assessments which takes due account of the above aspects.
in writing. impact assessments play a key role as a pre-legislative tool to provide transparent, comprehensive and balanced data on the economic, social and environmental consequences of eu action. for this reason, i welcome and approve the commitment made by the commission to the draft revision of the legislative guidelines, particularly as regards impact assessments. this will promote an improvement in legislative procedures and ensure a careful assessment of the economic, social and environmental aspects associated with them. i voted in favour of this proposal because it calls for rigorous, comprehensive impact assessments with full, accurate and objective information, based on a balanced analysis and focused on the scope of the proposal, so as to enable informed policy decisions to be taken. in addition, they should be updated to ensure continuity between the elements contained therein and any other proposal that is finally adopted by the commission. if these requirements are met, impact assessments are an important means of supporting decision-making in all the eu institutions and an essential element of the better lawmaking process.
in writing. - we agree on the objective of improving the impact assessment (ia) process, covering economic, social and environmental aspects. the approach should be applied to all initiatives: legislative proposals and the commission's legislative and work programme, legislative proposals not included in that programme with clearly identifiable economic, administrative, social and environmental impacts, non-legislative initiatives defining future policies and delegated or implementing acts of the commission which may have significant impacts identifiable in the same terms. however, we regret that this resolution seeks to establish an advisory body called better lawmaking. the eu, as always, is giving one hand to take the other, and that is why the resolution supports the maintenance of the sme tests, to avoid that smes are disproportionately affected or harmed by the commission's initiatives compared to larger companies, naturally accepting that smes are harmed, as long as this damage is not disproportionate. in view of these contradictions, we could not vote in favour.
in writing. we agree with the aim of improving the impact assessment (ia) process, ensuring that economic, social and environmental aspects are assessed in equal depth and that the approach is carried out in all initiatives: legislative proposals in the commission's legislative and work programme, legislative proposals not included in the said programme that have clearly identifiable economic, administrative, social and environmental impacts, non-legislative initiatives that define future policies and commission delegated or implementing acts that may have significant identifiable impacts in the same terms. however, we regret that this resolution seeks to establish an advisory body called better lawmaking, composed of stakeholder representatives and national experts, to complement the commission's work on ai, particularly with regard to subsidiarity and proportionality. the eu, as always, is playing catch-up, and that is why the resolution supports the maintenance of the sme tests, to avoid that smes are disproportionately affected or harmed by the commission's initiatives compared to larger companies', naturally accepting that smes are harmed, provided that this harm is not disproportionate. in view of these contradictions, we could not vote in favour.
in writing. in 2012, some 6.6 million children under the age of 5 died, mostly from preventable causes; 168 million children aged 5-17 are involved in some form of child labour; 11% of girls are married before they turn 15; more than 59 million children were directly affected by crises, mostly linked to conflict, and there are some 250,000 child soldiers in the world. in 2012 alone, nearly 95,000 children and adolescents under the age of 20 were murdered, nearly one billion children aged 2 to 14 were subjected to physical punishment, one in three adolescents aged 13 to 15 were harassed, about 70 million young people aged 15 to 19 were subjected to some form of physical violence, and 120 million girls worldwide were forced into sexual intercourse at some point in their lives. these figures deserve reflection on the 25th anniversary of the un convention on the rights of the child, and are also an opportunity to ensure its full implementation in programme and practice and to take additional measures to ensure respect for the rights of children, especially the most vulnerable.
in writing. 25 years after the adoption of the convention on the rights of the child, it is necessary to reflect on the path taken to promote a future with better conditions of well-being and dignity for children. the convention, despite the accession it has granted, is not being applied in many countries of the world. in several member states, children's rights are being put at risk by the eu's austerity policies. policies that lead to the deprivation of various rights, such as the right to education, health, housing and healthy food adequate for their physical and mental growth. only an urgent break with these policies will prevent the worsening of the living conditions of children and the attack on their rights. we welcome the adoption of our amendments which advocate the extension of the public network of kindergartens, day nurseries and public services providing play activities for children; which call on the member states to protect or increase the rights of motherhood and fatherhood and to ensure compulsory secondary education free of charge for all. it is significant and regrettable that the psd and cds voted against several of these proposals. and that the ps also voted against references to the effects of austerity policies.
the united nations convention on the rights of the child and its optional protocols constitute the standard in the promotion and protection of children's rights, encompassing a wide range of international legal standards relating to the protection and well-being of children. children's rights are at the heart of eu policies and the 25th anniversary of the un convention on the rights of the child is an opportunity to ensure its full implementation in programme and practice and to take further steps to ensure that children's rights, especially the most vulnerable ones, are respected everywhere. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. while significant progress has been made in defending children's rights since the adoption of the united nations convention on the rights of the child, the truth is that these rights continue to be violated in many parts of the world as a result of violence, abuse, exploitation, poverty, social exclusion and discrimination, with 2.6 million children living below the poverty line since 2008, even in rich countries, bringing the total number of children living in poverty in the developed world to around 76.5 million. however, given that the promotion of children's rights is an explicit objective of eu policies, this resolution proposes a set of additional measures to be taken by the eu and its member states (such as the ratification of all optional protocols to the un convention by the member states and the full implementation of the common european asylum system package) to effectively promote and safeguard children's rights, thereby ensuring the full implementation of the convention and the eu's commitment in the stockholm programme.
in writing. the 25th anniversary of the united nations convention on the rights of the child is being celebrated. this is the perfect opportunity to put them at the centre of the european union's policies and to ensure their full implementation, not only at the programme level but above all in practice, by adopting measures to ensure that the rights and interests of the most vulnerable people in particular are respected. it is a fact that all the member states of the european union have already ratified the un convention. however, we must strive to ensure that the united states, somalia and south sudan also do so, so that its ratification becomes universal. but it's not enough! we must also ensure that what is ratified in theory is implemented in practice. there are still several scourges to be tackled: cyberbullying, child abuse, child pornography, genital mutilation, among others. some 170 million children are subjected to child labor and a quarter of a million are child soldiers. nothing justifies or can justify these inhuman and horrible atrocities. this resolution makes an important contribution to the guarantee, safeguard and protection of the rights of the child by formulating a set of priority recommendations for the eradication of these terrible scourges, with a view to the development of future generations.
in writing. - we agree that the united nations convention on the rights of the child and its optional protocols constitute the standard in the promotion and protection of children's rights, encompassing a wide range of international legal standards relating to the protection and welfare of children. the resolution recognises that although progress has been made since the adoption of the un convention on the rights of the child 25 years ago, these same rights continue to be violated in many parts of the world, including eu member states. however, the resolution does not go into the depth of the underlying factors that are at the root of all these violations. there's no mention of austerity. there is no mention of reducing social spending by the states. there is no mention of the devastating effects of the policies of economic liberalization, of the deregulation of industrial relations. without this diagnosis, there can be no effective remedies.
in writing. the convention on the rights of the child was adopted in november 1989 and ratified by portugal a year later. we know that the convention, like the other human rights instruments, is not being applied in many countries of the world. in several eu countries, children's rights are being undermined by the austerity policies imposed by the european union, which leads to the deprivation of various rights, such as the right to education, health, housing and healthy food, adequate for their physical and mental growth. only an urgent break with these policies will prevent a worsening of the living conditions of children and their rights. we welcome the adoption of our amendments which advocate the extension of the public network of kindergartens, day nurseries and public services providing recreational activities for children, the increase of maternity and paternity rights, the guarantee of compulsory secondary education free of charge for all as a basic condition for the exercise of the right to equal opportunities. the psd and cds meps, contrary to statements about the need to reverse the current demographic problems in portugal, voted against amendments aimed at supporting children and their families.

the digital single market is one of the evolving areas which, while posing challenges, offers opportunities for significant efficiency gains, which could amount to €260 billion per year, and can therefore help europe to emerge from the crisis. it is one of the most innovative sectors of the economy and therefore plays an important role in the competitiveness of the european economy, but not only offers economic advantages, but also has a profound impact on the daily cultural, social and political lives of eu consumers and citizens. however, this market cannot be competitive without high-speed broadband and telecommunications networks in all regions of the eu, including peripheral regions, and it is essential that member states make sustained efforts to apply and implement the existing regulation as part of an overall strategy. it is recalled that e-commerce alone could save consumers more than €11.7 billion a year if they could choose from the full range of eu goods and services whenever they shop online.
the aim of this resolution is to remove all obstacles to the development of the digital single market, i.e. the liberalisation of the digital market, based on a comprehensive strategy which the eu believes is the panacea for the ills of the crisis of capitalism, and thus create economic growth, jobs, and strengthen competitiveness and resilience in the world economy. more than theoretical considerations about the harmful effects of market liberalisation, reality shows that such liberalisation strategies lead to the closure of firms, concentration of wealth in countries and monopolies in liberalised sectors, weakening of national productions in member states with weaker economies, and consequently increased redundancies, increased exploitation of workers, who in the face of such levels of unemployment are forced to work for less pay and in worse working conditions. this is the result of the deepening of capitalist integration in its various aspects. we voted against the principle advocated in this resolution, against the ambition to liberalise the services market, against the current deregulation of the protection of personal data and individual freedoms. although the resolution lists as eu concerns issues such as net neutrality and would improve consumer protection, nothing is effectively guaranteed in this area.

in writing. the creation of a european digital single market offers the possibility of significant economic efficiency gains of up to eur 260 billion per year, and is a powerful engine for growth in the european economy, which could lead to a 4% increase in european gdp by 2020 and the creation of 3 million quality and sustainable jobs between 2013 and 2018. in addition, the development of cloud computing, in the context of bridging the digital divide and connectivity on the continent, must be accompanied by the defence of digital entrepreneurship, copyright and intellectual property, as well as the protection of consumer rights (the protection of personal data, the protection of children, access to information and the right to privacy). for these reasons, i voted in favour of this resolution, which calls for the completion of the european digital single market and the removal of the obstacles that prevent its full realisation (such as the restriction of service providers to certain countries or territories, refusal to sell, automatic re-routing and unjustified diversification of sales conditions), as well as the protection of consumers' interests.
in writing. the digital single market (dsm) is a major bet for europe to grow faster economically and its completion would, according to some projections, allow europe's gdp to grow by a potential 4% by 2020. the market for computer applications alone is expected to triple revenues between 2013 and 2018, creating 3 million jobs over that period, and enabling the inclusion of all citizens in the digital age society, regardless of their income, social status and geographical location. however, as the european parliament stresses in its resolution, it is absolutely necessary to take account of the protection of consumer rights in this market. therefore, the protection of personal data and privacy, cybersecurity, security of electronic communications and networks must be a reality in the mud. as this report states, any legislative proposal on mud is expected to take into account the charter of fundamental rights of the european union so that the rights enshrined therein are fully protected in the digital domain. for these reasons i voted in favour of this resolution.
