‒ under the refit programme for regulatory adequacy and effectiveness, the european commission is planning measures to simplify european legislation and reduce regulatory costs, thus contributing to a clear, stable, predictable regulatory framework conducive to growth and jobs. in this connection, it seems to me that it is appropriate to repeal directive 93/5/eec, which ensured the effective functioning of the scientific committee for food by promoting scientific support from the member states and organising cooperation with the national bodies responsible for food safety, since, by subsequent legislation, the european food safety authority is the body responsible in these fields.
in writing. under the regulatory fitness and performance programme (refit), the commission has committed itself to ensuring a simple, clear, stable and predictable regulatory framework for businesses, workers and citizens. the establishment of the authority has made it competent for the promotion of scientific cooperation with member states and national competent bodies operating in the areas of the authority's tasks and gives it powers to act in close cooperation with the competent bodies of the member states, and member states should cooperate with the authority in the pursuit of its tasks. the repeal of the previous directive therefore makes perfect sense.
‒ this report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council repealing council directive 93/5/eec on the assistance of the member states to the commission and their cooperation in the scientific examination of questions relating to foodstuffs, is part of the ongoing european commission programme for regulatory fitness and effectiveness (refit), launched in 2012, where the commission commits itself to repealing outdated and redundant legislation. the purpose of that directive was to promote scientific support by member states and to organise cooperation with the competent national bodies on scientific matters relating to food safety, in order to ensure the effective functioning of the scientific committee for food, which in 2002 was replaced in its scientific tasks by the european food safety authority (efsa). furthermore, pursuant to regulation (ec) no 178/2002, the efsa has also become the competent body for the promotion of scientific cooperation with the member states and the competent national bodies operating in the areas of competence of the authority, rendering directive 93/5/eec obsolete. this is an eminently technical report, to which the simplified procedure (article 50 (1)) has been applied and which we voted in favour of.
in writing. ‒ in december 2012, the commission launched the regulatory fitness and performance programme (refit) to ensure a simple, clear, stable and predictable regulatory framework for businesses, workers and citizens. in this context, the commission has undertaken to repeal rules which have become superfluous or obsolete. this is the case of council directive 93/5/eec of 25 february 1993, which is now repealed. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ council directive 93/5/eec of 25 february 1993 aimed to ensure the effective functioning of the scientific committee for food by promoting scientific support from the member states and by organising cooperation with the competent national bodies on scientific matters relating to food safety. however, pursuant to regulation (ec) no 178/2002 of the european parliament and of the council of 28 january 2002, the tasks of the scientific committee for food were transferred to the european food safety authority and, consequently, commission decision 97/579/ec of 23 july 1997 setting up that committee was repealed. directive 93/5/eec has thus become obsolete and should therefore be repealed, as proposed by the commission. i voted in favour.
‒ the scientific committee for food was initially set up in 1974 (later amended by decision 97/579/ec, which created scientific committees in the field of consumer health and food safety). in 1993, council directive 93/5/eec was adopted to make the committee more effective by promoting scientific support from the member states and by organising cooperation with the competent national bodies on scientific questions relating to food safety. with the adoption of regulation (ec) no 178/2002, the functions of the scientific committee for food were transferred to the european food safety authority (efsa) and decision 97/579/ec was subsequently repealed. directive 93/5/eec has thus become obsolete, leading to the presentation of the proposal from the european parliament and the council which gave rise to the report voted on today. given that this proposal for a directive was taken up by parliament in this report and drafted under the regulatory fitness and performance programme (refit) - where the commission has committed itself to clear and predictable regulation for businesses, workers and citizens by repealing rules which have become superfluous and obsolete - i voted in favour of it.
‒ this report is part of the european commission's ongoing regulatory fitness and performance (refit) programme, launched in 2012, where the commission commits to repeal outdated and redundant legislation. the purpose of that directive was to promote scientific support by member states and to organise cooperation with the competent national bodies on scientific matters relating to food safety, in order to ensure the effective functioning of the scientific committee for food, which in 2002 was replaced in its scientific tasks by the european food safety authority (efsa). the authority, in accordance with regulation (ec) no 178/2002, became the competent body for the promotion of scientific cooperation with the member states and the competent national bodies operating in the areas of competence of the authority, rendering directive 93/5/eec obsolete.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council repealing council directive 93/5/eec of 25 february 1993 on the assistance of the member states to the commission and their cooperation in the scientific examination of questions relating to foodstuffs, because it fulfils the objective of ensuring the effective functioning of the scientific committee for food by promoting scientific support from the member states and by organising cooperation with the competent national bodies on scientific questions relating to food safety.
‒ this report is part of the ongoing european commission's regulatory fitness and performance (refit) programme, launched in 2012, where the commission commits to repeal outdated and redundant legislation. the purpose of the directive was to promote scientific support from member states and to organise cooperation with the competent national bodies on scientific matters relating to food safety, in order to ensure the effective functioning of the scientific committee for food, which was replaced in its scientific tasks by the european food safety authority (efsa) in 2002. furthermore, pursuant to regulation (ec) no 178/2002, the efsa has also become the competent body for the promotion of scientific cooperation with the member states and the competent national bodies operating in the areas of competence of the authority, rendering directive 93/5/eec obsolete.
‒ the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites), in force since 1975, is an important international instrument for the protection of endangered species of fauna and flora by controlling international trade in specimens of these species. the original text of the convention limited participation in cites to states, with the european union as an observer only. the gaborone amendment, adopted on 30 april 1983, enabled membership of economic and regional integration organisations consisting of sovereign states and empowered to negotiate, conclude and implement international agreements in matters covered by the convention, and entered into force on 29 november 2013. i support the eu's accession to cites, which will make the eu's legal status more transparent vis-à-vis the other parties to the convention. the eu will also be adequately represented at cites meetings and will participate fully in the work of the convention, in accordance with the treaties. accession is therefore a logical and necessary step to ensure that the european union is in a position to pursue the objectives of environmental policy.
the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) is an important international instrument for the protection of endangered species of fauna and flora by controlling international trade in specimens of these species. it currently has 178 parties (including all eu member states), covers some 35 000 species and ensures that international trade in specimens of these species does not endanger their survival. the european union's accession becomes important for the work that the convention has been doing, recommending that the current practice be adopted when someone becomes an effective party: the annual contribution corresponding to 2.5% of the total amount allocated to the cites trust fund (about 115 000 euros in 2015) reducing accordingly the share of the member states in these contributions, a situation that deserved my vote in favour.
‒ the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) is an international agreement whose objective is to ensure that international trade in species of wild fauna and flora does not threaten their survival, and thus constitutes an important instrument for the conservation of endangered species, particularly those of commercial interest, which as such should be defended and enhanced. the success of cites depends on the effective implementation of the agreed recommendations. the european union had observer status in cites. at the second extraordinary meeting of cites cop (1983), the gaborone amendment to the convention was agreed, allowing regional economic integration organisations made up of sovereign states to become parties to the cites convention. the aim of this recommendation is to approve the accession of the european union to cites in order to enable it to participate fully in the work of the convention and to legally bind the eu and the member states to the implementation and enforcement provided for in the convention. it should be noted that the rights and obligations of the member states under cites will not be affected by the accession of the eu, which will pay a quota to the organisation.
‒ i agree with the eu's accession to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites). cites is an important international instrument for the protection of endangered species of fauna and flora by controlling international trade in specimens of these species. cites entered into force in 1975 and currently has 178 parties (including all eu member states). it covers some 35 000 species, which are listed in the three appendices according to the degree of protection they require, and ensures that international trade in specimens of these species does not endanger their survival. this convention is very important in the fight against illegal trade in protected and endangered species, which is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) entered into force in 1975 with the aim of protecting certain endangered species of wild fauna and flora against overexploitation due to international trade. it currently has 178 parties, including all eu member states. since the initial text of cites limited states to participation in cites, the eu has hitherto had the status of a mere observer. with the entry into force of the gaborone amendment on 29 november 2003, it became possible for regional economic integration organisations made up of sovereign states with competence to negotiate, conclude and implement international agreements in matters covered by the convention to accede to cites. however, since the matters covered by cites (environmental protection and trade) fall within the eu's competence and its accession to cites will enable it to participate fully in the work of the convention, ensuring the conditions for the pursuit of its environmental policy objectives, i voted in favour of this resolution, which approves the eu's accession to cites.
‒ the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) is an international convention that brings together 178 countries, including all eu member states, and covers some 35 000 species, which are under a system of prior licensing for their trade. cites is therefore a highly relevant instrument for the protection, control and monitoring of trade in these species. initially, participation in cites was limited to states, with the european union having observer status. however, a recent amendment to article 21 of the convention allows membership of regional economic integration organisations made up of sovereign states and endowed with the powers to negotiate, conclude and implement international agreements on cites matters which their member states have transferred to them. since the convention's fields of action concern the protection of the environment and international trade, the former being a competence shared with the member states and the latter an exclusive competence of the union, i consider the eu's accession to the cites convention to be a logical and very welcome step, and i therefore voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ we broadly agree with this decision to accede to the convention. as has been said, the preservation of some 3000 animal species and 40 000 plant species is at stake. my concern is with the means which the eu will put to the service of this important mission. without the means, without effective intervention on the ground, this accession to cites will not make much sense. in the eu, public veterinary control services which played a decisive role in the eradication of several zoonotic diseases such as tuberculosis and swine fever in portugal have been dismantled in some countries. the need to strengthen the means to combat illegal trade in these species is therefore emphasized. in particular, it is necessary to strengthen border inspection posts by providing them with human and technical resources; to improve the training of veterinary staff within the food and veterinary office, possibly with the european veterinary federation; it is also necessary to give the member states the means to monitor their eezs, which has not been possible in portugal, given the austerity measures, despite having the largest eez in the eu.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european union's accession to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites). the eu's accession to cites was a consistent and necessary step forward in ensuring that the european union is fully equipped to pursue its environmental policy objectives. accession will not only allow the commission to express, on behalf of the european union, a coherent eu position on cites matters, but also to participate effectively in the negotiations of the conferences of the parties. this accession will enable the commission to negotiate on behalf of the european union and to work actively towards a compromise solution balanced between the positions of the 28 member states. in addition, by becoming a party to cites, the european union will have formal responsibilities, having to be accountable to the other parties for the implementation and enforcement of the convention.
‒ the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) is an international agreement whose objective is to ensure that international trade in species of wild fauna and flora does not threaten their survival, thus constituting an important instrument for the conservation of endangered species, particularly those of commercial interest, which as such should be defended and enhanced. the aim of this recommendation is to approve the accession of the european union to cites in order to enable it to participate fully in the work of the convention and to legally bind the eu and the member states to the implementation and enforcement provided for in the convention. it should be noted that the rights and obligations of the member states under cites will not be affected by eu accession, and we therefore agree with the recommendation.
‒ europe is building its own global navigation satellite system (gnss) with the most advanced technology, designed to enable accurate and guaranteed positioning for all types of civil applications, including car navigation, mobile phones, maritime, road, rail and air transport. this system provides free satellite radio navigation signals with ten times the accuracy of the gps system. this agreement shall promote, facilitate and enhance cooperation between the parties in the framework of the eu and morocco's contributions to a global satellite navigation system for civil use. i therefore support this agreement which brings mutual benefits, reciprocal opportunities for participation in cooperation activities, timely exchange of information, adequate protection of intellectual property rights and free trade of gnss equipment in the territories of the parties.
the galileo programme is the european radio navigation and satellite positioning programme, which aims to provide the european union with a navigation technology independent of the us gps and the russian glonass, in a sector which has become central to economic development. therefore, the purpose of this cooperation agreement is to facilitate and promote cooperation between the union and the kingdom of morocco in order to collect contributions from both parties to a global navigation satellite system (gnss). i therefore voted in favour of the above recommendation, taking into account the leverage role that a european gnss can play in the european economy and taking into account the advantages of greater precision and security that this system offers over others.
‒ the council proposal for a cooperation agreement on the global navigation satellite system (gnss) for civil use between the european union and the kingdom of morocco is at issue. the gnss system has undeniable utility and potential. the strong dependence on the american gps system is undesirable and limiting, and it carries obvious dangers. we have some reservations, however, about the fact that the system's exclusively civilian use is not fully guaranteed and about the possibility of its use for military purposes - a situation which has been warned about by various peace organizations in various countries. we have already made this point on several occasions. in this case, a cooperation agreement is proposed with morocco, which is responsible for the illegal occupation of the territory of western sahara, which oppresses the people of this territory and refuses to accept un resolutions on their right to self-determination. we therefore voted against this report, taking into account that this agreement may cover occupied territories over which morocco has no sovereignty under international law.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this agreement is to promote, facilitate and enhance cooperation between the parties in the framework of the contributions of the european union and morocco to a global navigation satellite system (gnss) for civil use. the sectors open to cooperation activities in the field of satellite navigation and timekeeping covered by the agreement are the following: scientific research, industrial production, training, application, service and market development, trade, radio spectrum issues, integrity, standardisation and homologation. this is a very important agreement for the development of industrial and research relations between the two countries, and i therefore vote in favour.
‒ contacts on a participation of morocco in the galileo programme started on 24 march 2004. following a round of bilateral talks, on 13 october the moroccan minister for equipment and transport sent a letter to the director-general for energy and transport of the european commission confirming morocco's intention to conclude a cooperation agreement with the eu on the satellite radio navigation system for civil use. the european commission, on the basis of a negotiating mandate conferred by the council on 21 april 2005, then entered into negotiations and the agreement was signed on 12 december 2006, in accordance with the council decision of 27 november 2006 authorising the signature. whereas the said cooperation agreement on a global navigation satellite system (gnss) between the european community and the kingdom of morocco will allow for the strengthening of joint activities in important sectors such as scientific research, industrial production and training, to the benefit of the citizens, industry and scientific communities of both parties; i voted in favour of this resolution, which approves the celebration of the european year.
‒ morocco has been participating in the european union's galileo programme since december 2006. it also has a scientific and technical cooperation agreement with the eu and is part of the european neighbourhood policy, so it can, if it is interested, join the new framework programme for research and innovation - horizon 2020. it also has expertise in space technologies and applications and aims to develop the use of satellite radio navigation in its territory, the western mediterranean and west africa. it also adds that there are close cooperation relations between several european and moroccan companies in the space sector, which enhances the possibility of extension to other sectors of activity. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of the conclusion of this agreement.

in writing. ‒ the agreement on scientific and technological cooperation between the european community and ukraine was signed in copenhagen on 4 july 2007 for an initial period ending on 31 december 2012. in march 2011, the council decided to renew the agreement for a further period of five years until november 2014. i support this initiative which recommends the renewal of this agreement for a further period of five years, which will allow the continuity of scientific and technological relations between the european union and ukraine to be maintained. the renewal of this agreement will enable both parties to improve and intensify their cooperation in scientific and technological areas of common interest and will contribute to the exchange of knowledge and the transfer of know-how for the benefit of the scientific communities and citizens. the agreement is based on the principles of mutual benefit, reciprocity of access to each party's programmes and activities, non-discrimination, effective protection of intellectual property, equitable sharing of intellectual property rights and the exploitation of results.
in writing. approves the renewal of the cooperation agreement and the sharing of specific knowledge and know-how in the fields of science and technology, areas which are clearly beneficial for scientific progress. the commission notes that the agreement between the parties to the agreement on the transfer of the rights of use of the ip and the rights of use of the ip is not a new agreement, but rather a new agreement, which is not a new agreement, and that the new agreement is not a new agreement. the interests of the european union are safeguarded through the review carried out for this new agreement, which allows the commission to regularly monitor all actions under this agreement, in particular through the collection of data and analysis of performance indicators. i therefore voted in favour of the recommendation to renew the said agreement.
the first agreement on scientific and technological cooperation between the eu and ukraine was signed in july 2002, approved by the council on 6 february 2003. it was an agreement whose content was based on areas of cooperation in environmental and climate research, biomedical, health, research in the field of agriculture, forestry and fisheries, industrial technologies, raw materials and production, as well as research in the field of transport, social sciences and training, including exchange of scientists. the content of the renewed agreement is identical to the agreement which expired in november 2014. it will enable both parties to improve and intensify their cooperation in science and technology in areas of common interest and will allow for a greater exchange of specific knowledge and the transfer of know-how. we are in principle in favour of establishing cooperation relations in this field. however, the situation in ukraine cannot be ignored. the illegitimate and undemocratic character of the ukrainian government and the coup that brought it to power, as well as the campaigns of hatred, persecution and violence it has promoted, with the systematic and brutal trampling on of fundamental rights and freedoms, would justify not renewing this agreement at this time.
in writing. ‒ this agreement is identical to the one currently in force and to the one in force on 7 november 2014. the agreement is based on the principles of mutual benefit, reciprocity of access to each party's programmes and activities in relation to the subject matter of the agreement, non-discrimination, effective protection of intellectual property and fair sharing of intellectual property rights, and effective exploitation of results. the renewal of the agreement will allow the generation of scientific knowledge leading to market access opportunities. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ taking into account that the agreement on scientific and technological cooperation between the european community and ukraine expired on 7 november 2014, i voted in favour of this resolution, which approves the renewal of the agreement, in order to ensure that the parties can continue to exchange scientific knowledge and transfer know-how for the benefit of their scientific communities, industry and citizens.
‒ the eu-ukraine agreement on scientific and technological cooperation focuses on the principles of mutual benefit, reciprocal access to each party's programmes and activities, non-discrimination, effective protection of intellectual property (and fair sharing thereof), and effective exploitation of results, principles pursued by the european union. the renewal of this agreement, which is of the same content as the previous one, will allow for intensified and improved cooperation in scientific and technological areas of common interest, as well as the continuation of the exchange of specific knowledge and the transfer of know-how for the benefit of the scientific communities, industry and citizens, leading to market access opportunities. it will also allow regular monitoring by the commission services. i therefore voted in favour of the recommendation.
in the light of the recent events in the ukraine, the european union has decided to support the coup d'état in ukraine, in defiance of international law, in a move that is entirely in line with the united states and nato. as a result of this intervention, the eu had to provide financial support to the illegal government of ukraine, despite the numerous crimes committed against civilian populations, both by the government and by the forces supporting it. we have had to sign a trade agreement with ukraine (recently extended for another year), which opens our borders to products produced in that country, particularly those exported to russia, without reciprocity for european production. it has had to endure a russian embargo on european exports of various agri-food products, with enormous losses for producers. finally, it is paying ukraine's accumulated debts from the purchase of natural gas from russian companies, under the threat of jeopardizing gas supplies to the countries of central europe. for our part, we do not recognize any legitimacy to the group of people who have seized power in this country in defiance of international law. in this sense, we will not sign this agreement, or any other, until institutional legality has been restored.
‒ the agreement on the european economic area (eea agreement) was signed on 2 may 1992 and entered into force on 1 january 1994. the agreement provides for the introduction of eu legislation on the four freedoms - the free movement of goods, services, persons and capital - in all countries that make up the eea. the agreement includes cooperation in other important areas such as research and development, education, social policy, the environment, consumer protection, tourism and culture. the agreement guarantees citizens and economic operators in the eea equal rights and obligations in the internal market. this proposal constitutes the legal instrument for the conclusion of the agreement on the participation of the republic of croatia in the eea and the additional protocol thereto to the agreement with the kingdom of norway and the european union on the norwegian financial mechanism for the period 2014 to 2019, following the participation of croatia in the eea. croatia's participation in the eea is therefore a natural consequence of its accession to the eu on 1 july 2013. it is therefore natural that, more than a year after its accession to the eu, the commission and the council should take the necessary legal measures to make croatia's participation in the eea possible.
croatia's accession to the european union, which took place about a year ago, should have as a natural consequence its participation in the european economic area, which calls for the free movement of goods, services, persons and capital. in addition, the agreement includes cooperation in other important areas such as research and development, education, social policy, the environment, consumer protection, tourism and culture, collectively referred to as horizontal and framework policies. it is therefore quite normal that, more than a year after accession, the commission and the council have taken the necessary legal measures to make it possible for croatia to participate in this european area, assuming its full status as a member state.
‒ this report recommends approving the conclusion of the agreement on the participation of croatia in the european economic area (eea). in view of croatia's accession to the european union, the conclusion of various agreements and protocols is necessary to bring about the country's participation in the eea, i.e. this is one of the consequences of accession, which naturally follows from it. this is therefore a highly technical report. since our general position on the accession of new countries to the european union is well known, without ignoring the nature and meaning of integration and the enlargement processes, it is up to each people to decide freely and sovereignly whether or not to join the eu, which led to an abstention in the accession process of croatia, it is natural that the same sense of vote should follow in relation to the decisions or procedures that fell within the framework of the normal consequences of such accession. that is why we abstained in this report too.
‒ the eea agreement provides for the introduction of eu legislation on the four freedoms the free movement of goods, services, persons and capital in all countries within the eea. in addition, the agreement includes cooperation in other important areas such as research and development, education, social policy, the environment, consumer protection, tourism and culture, collectively referred to as horizontal and framework policies. the agreement guarantees citizens and economic operators of the eea equal rights and obligations in the internal market. croatia's participation in the european economic area is a natural consequence of its accession to the eu. it is therefore quite normal that, more than a year after accession, the commission and the council have taken the necessary legal measures to make this participation possible. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ the agreement on the european economic area, which has been in force since 1 january 1994, brings together the eu member states, iceland, liechtenstein and norway in a single market, providing for the extension of eu legislation on the four freedoms (the free movement of goods, services, persons and capital) to the above mentioned european free trade association member countries, as well as cooperation between the parties in areas such as research and development, education, social policy, the environment, consumer protection, tourism and culture. as croatia has acceded to the eu with effect from 1 july 2013, it is now necessary, in accordance with its act of accession, to ensure its participation in the european economic area. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, which approves the conclusion of the agreement on the participation of the republic of croatia in the european economic area and the three related agreements (additional protocols between the kingdom of norway and the european union on a norwegian financial mechanism for the period 2009-2014; between the european economic community and the republic of iceland; and between the european economic community and the kingdom of norway).
‒ the agreement on the european economic area allowed the three efta countries that were not part of the single market (iceland, norway and liechtenstein) to join. it entered into force on 1 january 1994 and comprises the 27 member states (except croatia) plus the three abovementioned countries. the eea agreement clearly states in article 128 that when a country accedes to the european union, it automatically applies for eea membership, leading to its enlargement. croatia thus undertakes to fulfil the conditions laid down in the act of accession to the eea. the commission and the council have also already adopted the necessary legal measures to make this participation of croatia possible. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that this participation is a natural consequence of croatia's accession to the eu and i am in favour of this new member state also being covered by the european rules governing the four freedoms of the single market - the free movement of goods, services, persons and capital - and its integration into the so-called horizontal and framework policies, thus ensuring full equality of rights and obligations in the internal market.
in writing. ‒ the eea agreement brings together the eu member states and the three members of the european free trade association iceland, liechtenstein and norway into a single market. the agreement includes cooperation in important areas such as research and development, education, social policy, the environment, consumer protection, tourism and culture. the agreement guarantees citizens and economic operators of the eea equal rights and obligations in the internal market. croatia's participation in the european economic area is a natural consequence of its accession to the eu. we consider it normal that this question should be raised and we have nothing to object to, provided that the will of the croatian people is respected.

the authorization given to france to exempt or reduce excise duties on certain products manufactured in the french outermost regions (with the exception of saint martin) to compensate for the disadvantages of the outermost regions concerned and to support their competitiveness and socioeconomic development makes perfect sense. therefore, the creation of a new legal framework for the excise duty for the period from 1 january 2015 to 31 december 2020, allowing to identify the products to which the exemptions or reductions of the duty may apply, was necessary. my vote in favour is based on the fact that this measure is justified and aims to continue to stimulate economic activity and competitiveness in the outermost regions, without undermining the coherence of the internal market and the eu legal order.
in writing. other on 10 february 2004, the council adopted a decision authorising france to apply, until 1 july 2014, exemptions or reductions from the excise duty on certain products manufactured in the french outermost regions, in order to compensate for the constraints to which they are subject, such as remoteness, dependence on raw materials and energy, small market size and poorly developed export activity affecting the outermost regions. france has now requested that a differentiated taxation system identical to the one mentioned above be maintained until 31 december 2020. however, the commission intends to examine the list of products to which the new system will apply, which will make the procedure time-consuming and incompatible with the expiry date of the decision. in order to allow the commission to finalise its assessment, the council decision extends the previous decision for a further six months. when the commission concludes the evaluation, the establishment of the new legal framework for the maritime tax for the period from 1 january 2015 to 31 december 2020 shall be followed up. we voted in favour, taking into account our position in principle of defending the specific features of the outermost regions and the consequent need for positive discrimination.
‒ the octroi de mer is an indirect tax applicable to the supply and import of goods to the french outermost regions. in principle, it applies equally to products which are produced locally and those which are not (products from metropolitan france, from other member states or from third countries). the aim of this proposal is to establish the legal framework applicable to the tax on the granting of a licence from 1 january 2015 to 31 december 2020. it further extends the validity of decision 2004/162/ec for a further period of six months in order to allow france time to transpose the provisions of the new council decision into national law and establishes the new legal framework applicable from 1 july 2015 to 31 december 2020. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ council decision 2004/162/ec of 10 february 2004 (as amended by council decisions 2008/439/ec of 9 june 2008, 448/2011/eu of 19 july 2011 and 2014/378/eu of 12 june) authorises france to apply, until 31 december 2014, exemptions or reductions from the charging of the maritime toll on certain products manufactured in the french outermost regions (with the exception of saint-martin) in order to compensate for the disadvantages they suffer and to support their competitiveness and socioeconomic development. following the request by france to continue to apply such a taxation system, the commission has submitted a proposal for a new legal framework for the charging of excise duty for the period from 1 january 2015 to 31 december 2020, which identifies the products to which the exemptions or reductions of tax will apply and provides for a six-month extension of the validity of decision 2004/162/ec so that france can transpose the new decision into national law. i think that this proposal is entirely justified in the light of the objectives of supporting and stimulating the outermost regions, and i therefore voted in favour.
‒ the promotion of the socioeconomic development and competitiveness of the member states is one of the objectives of the european union. it is particularly important in the case of the outermost regions, which are exposed to a greater number of disadvantages at that level. in this respect, i voted in favour of the report on the european parliament's draft legislative resolution which, on the basis of the current article 349 of the tfeu, authorises france to apply, until 1 july 2014 (with a possible extension of six months), exemptions or reductions from excise duty to certain products manufactured in the french outermost regions. the desirable stimulus to economic activity and competitiveness in these regions justifies the adoption of this measure, which is intended to combat isolation and distance, dependence on raw materials and energy, the small size of the market and the stimulation of export activity (which is not very developed in these regions). for all these reasons, it seems to me clear that this measure will not jeopardise the coherence of the internal market or the eu legal order, which fully justifies the adoption of the commission proposal without amendments, as proposed by the rapporteur.
‒ we agree with the principle that france may apply exemptions or reductions from excise duty to certain products manufactured in the french outermost regions (with the exception of saint martin) in order to compensate for the disadvantages of the outermost regions concerned (remoteness, dependence on raw materials and energy, small market size and underdeveloped export activity) and to support their competitiveness and socioeconomic development. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a regulation on the establishment of a european agency for the evaluation of medicinal products for human use.
‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the european globalisation adjustment fund was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic, financial and social crisis. at a time when europe is facing a financial, economic and social crisis, with unemployment as one of the main consequences, the european union should use all the means at its disposal to react, particularly with regard to the support to be given to people who have lost their jobs. i therefore supported this report on the mobilisation of eur 1 890 000 for italy to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant at whirlpool europe s.r.l.
in writing. the egf was established to provide additional support for workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation or the financial crisis and to help them find new jobs. the annual ceiling of the fund for the period 2014-2020 shall be eur 150 million. dismissed workers are offered measures such as support for business creation, job search assistance, vocational guidance and various types of training. in most cases, national authorities have already started to take steps to have their costs reimbursed by the eu when their applications are approved. the italian authorities submitted the application egf/2014/010 it/whirlpool on 18 june 2014, following the redundancies of 608 workers in whirlpool europe s.r.l., an enterprise operating in the economic activity sector classified in nace rev. 2 division 27 (manufacture of electrical equipment), and in five downstream supplier and producer enterprises, as a consequence of the significant decrease in household consumption, the italian market for large appliances increased from eur 3174 billion in 2010 to eur 2649 billion in 2013, representing a decrease of 16,5%; in this mobilisation of the egf in favour of the region of trento in italy, eur 1.89 million was granted. i voted in favour.
‒ the application under examination concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 1 890 000 for italy. it results in 608 layoffs at whirlpool and five downstream suppliers and producers. this is the fourth application from the electrical equipment manufacturing sector in italy to be examined since 2010. the proposal, which in addition to actions to be carried out directly with the workers made redundant, such as information sessions, counselling and guidance, skills assessment, general training and retraining, vocational training, among others, advocates recruitment subsidies, under fixed-term or permanent contracts, ranging from eur 3000 to eur 2000 per worker respectively. we believe that this measure should make the subsidy to enterprises conditional on the maintenance of rights and the creation of a permanent job, which is not the case. the justification for the closure of these companies and the consequent dismissal of their workers lies, once again, in the structural changes in world trade patterns and the world economic and financial crisis. we're approving palliative measures, but we have to attack the root of the problem: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.

‒ the greek application under examination concerns odyssefs fokas s.a., a company active in the retail trade sector, which has declared bankruptcy, leaving 600 workers, of whom 87% are women, unemployed. the justification for this dismissal has been seen before: reduction in households' disposable income due to increased tax burden, falling wages (both in the private sector and in the public service) and rising unemployment resulting in a huge fall in purchasing power. the commission also notes that the greek authorities have not provided any evidence that the bank of greece has been able to restore its long-term viability. it should be noted that 90% of redundancies are concentrated in the regions of attica (28.2% unemployment) and central macedonia (30.3% unemployment), and that greece is the fifth country in the world with the highest unemployment rate. moreover, the attica region contributes to 43% of greek gdp and, for this reason, the impact of the closure of this company affects the entire greek economy. the report proposes to support the 600 workers made redundant and up to 600 young people who are not working, studying or in training. we voted in favour, despite our well-known reservations about this instrument.

mr president, the first work programme is certainly very important because it is important to set a new direction for europe and to set a new level of ambition. if we want to focus on a strong idea for this new direction for europe, then it is certainly to restart the job creation machine in europe. this machine is not working and we need to restart job creation in order to overcome the stagnation trend we are in, in order to overcome economic and social divergences between member states, and in order to pave the way for new activities: a green transition, a smart and innovative economy. but for that we really need to change direction and we are waiting for a commission that pushes for a new policy mix; where we have fiscal consolidation but where the top priority is certainly growth; where we have reforms but reforms to enhance growth potential and not just to cut public spending; where, most of all, investment is a top priority, and this means having an investment plan which is able to support strategic projects, which are missing in europe. this also means having a fiscal rule with more room for investments and this, we know very well, means having a credible agenda to tackle tax avoidance and to exclude harmful tax competition. this is the level and ambition we are waiting for. let me just underline that you also hold a historic task in your hands which is to complete the economic and monetary union. (the speaker agreed to take a blue card question under rule 162(8))
blue-card answer.– i do not think the problem is with the euro, the euro can become a strength for european union member states; the problem is that our economic and monetary union is deeply imbalanced. we need to complete the banking union, we need to have proper coordination to support demand with supply in deficit countries and most of all we need to build up a real fiscal capacity. with these conditions i think we can again deliver high job creation and better standards in the euro area.
looking at this programme, we see what the much-vaunted new juncker commission cycle means. an investment plan that consists of giving public guarantees to a giant public-private partnership program. infrastructures of public interest which are operated on the basis of private profit-making logic. condemning young people to precariousness and forced emigration. attacks on the welfare system. more liberalization, deregulation of trade, selective immigration. this is the way to go. it is symbolic that files are dropped which could still represent some sort of social advance, even if only slight, such as the maternity directive. and the backsliding is obvious, the backsliding is blatant on environmental issues. the commission is now revealing its true face as the business committee of large transnational capital. this programme is nothing more or less than the specifications of the major confederations of the large european employers' organizations. no matter who sits in that chair, they're the ones pulling the strings. none of this is future. it's all in the past. a dark past that will sooner or later be irrevocably defeated.

in writing. - the eu and moldova have intensified their political and economic relations, notably through the conclusion of an association agreement in which moldova will further enhance its access to the eu market, in particular through approximation to relevant eu legislation and standards. this rapprochement led to russia banning the entry of moldovan products into its territory. agriculture accounts for 40% of the country's economy and employs 250,000 people. seeking assistance and support at this critical time, the moldovan authorities have turned to the eu for urgent assistance to reduce the economic impact of the russian ban, in particular on the most important products for moldovan fruit growers: apples, plums and table grapes which are now exempted from duties by 40 000 tonnes for fresh apples and 10 000 tonnes for fresh table grapes and fresh plums. as this is a matter of social and institutional solidarity, it deserves my vote in favour.
in writing. in 2008, the eu introduced autonomous trade preferences (atps). this grant was foreseen in the 2005 european neighbourhood policy action plan. the cfp regulation abolished all trade rights for moldovan industrial products and granted free access to the eu market to moldovan agricultural products, with the exception of some meat, dairy products, maize, barley and sugar. the signing of the eu-moldova association agreement includes the creation of a deep and comprehensive free trade area (dcfta). the european commission states that in order to support the efforts of the republic of moldova, in line with the objectives set out in the european neighbourhood policy, the eastern partnership and the association agreement, and to reduce the economic impact of the ban imposed by russia on agricultural products due to moldova's political rapprochement with the eu, it proposes to amend the cfp regulation by introducing three new duty-free tariff quotas for apples, table grapes and plums. we are in favour of a policy of cooperation and solidarity with all the countries and peoples of the world. of course, it is also with moldova. but that is not the aim of free trade, nor of the eu's neighbourhood policy, nor of the vision that this report frames.
in writing. the autonomous trade preferences (atp) for the republic of moldova (hereinafter referred to as moldova) were initially introduced by the eu through council regulation (ec) no 55/2008 of 21 january 2008. the granting of these preferences was envisaged in the 2005 european neighbourhood policy action plan, provided that moldova substantially improved its system of controls and certification of goods. moldova has fulfilled its commitments by reforming its customs legislation and by transposing it satisfactorily into administrative practice by 2007. the aim of this report is to help moldova to counter the russian embargo on its agricultural products, in particular on the following products: fresh apples, fresh table grapes and fresh plums. the duty-free tariff quotas for the 3 products concerned are very low in volume compared to eu production (0.4% for apples, 0.7% for plums and 0.6% for table grapes), thus not affecting european producers. that is why i am voting in favour.
the republic of moldova has been subject to a russian embargo on its agricultural production since 21 july 2014, implemented as a result of the intensification of economic and political relations between moldova and the european union (eu). whereas the agricultural sector represents 40% of the moldovan economy, employing 250 000 people, and the total imports from moldova to the eu represented 0,1% of the total eu imports in 2013; whereas imports of fresh apples, fresh plums and fresh grapes would account for a total of 0,01 % of total eu imports, the corresponding loss of tariff revenue would have a disproportionate impact on the eu budget if these three products were to benefit from duty-free tariff quotas; and finally, taking into account that the autonomous trade preferences scheme will expire at the end of 2015, and with it the applicable tariff quotas proposed in this resolution, i voted in favour of the liberalisation of the market between the eu and moldova as designed by the commission.

in writing. ecuador should lose its gsp+ status as of 1 january 2015. this regulation has the effect of prolonging the trade preferences granted to ecuador under the gsp+ regulation. however, this extension is subject to strict conditions imposed by the eu on ecuador. by accepting this agreement to extend gsp+ status, ecuador will, among other conditions, have to refrain from imposing new duties or restrictions on imports from the eu and continue negotiations with a view to signing and ratifying the free trade agreement. should the commission consider that ecuador does not fulfil any of the conditions, it may suspend this tariff treatment. in the context of growing pressure for the liberalisation of international trade, it is clear that the eu is using the end of the gsp+ as a form of blackmail for the acceptance of the so-called free trade agreements, through unacceptable diplomatic and economic pressure on several countries. the gsp+ would need to be extended and renegotiated alongside other development support policies to become a development aid instrument, shaping effective solidarity and combating economic dependence and exploitation of people and their natural resources by eu economic groups.
in writing. on 17 july 2014, negotiations with ecuador for its accession to the trade agreement concluded between the eu and colombia and peru were concluded and a protocol was subsequently signed. in order to avoid unnecessary disruption of trade, pending the completion of the procedures for the approval and application of the protocol of accession, it is necessary to ensure that the customs duties applied on the date of entry into force of the protocol of accession are not increased and that no new customs duties are applied to products originating in ecuador. the proposal for a regulation therefore provides for the maintenance of the level of the duty rates applicable to ecuador at the date of entry into force of the accession protocol.
in writing. the instrument that allows developing countries to benefit from differentiated and more favourable trade treatment by developed countries, the generalised system of preferences (gsp), currently in force for ecuador, would expire in january 2015. the trade preferences granted under the regulation would thereby expire. however, ecuador has since moved up its previous wto ranking, with the list of vulnerable and developing countries eligible for the facility updated for the last three consecutive years, but always excluding ecuador. the eu thus entered into parallel negotiations with ecuador for accession to the trade agreement also concluded between the eu and colombia and peru. in the interim period during which the internal procedures necessary for the application of the accession protocol are being carried out, another transitional application of tariff preferences until the end of 2016, which this resolution approves, with my vote, seems necessary in order to avoid trade diversion due to the increase in customs duties on products originating in ecuador.
in writing. ecuador will lose its gsp+ status as of 1 january 2015. negotiations have been launched for the accession of this country to the trade agreement concluded between the eu and colombia and peru on 17 july. it is noted that the accession of ecuador to the eu trade agreement with the andean community (initially planned but later suspended due to ecuador's withdrawal from the negotiations in 2007) will allow it to restore the competitiveness that its export products have lost compared to similar products imported from colombia and peru, and also give it a new legal framework for bilateral relations with the eu. the proposal thus seeks to ensure, in a harmonious and equitable manner, that the customs duties applied on the date of entry into force of the protocol of accession of ecuador to the free trade agreement between the eu and the andean community are not increased, even if no customs duties are applied transitionally to products originating in ecuador. i therefore agree to the transitional extension of the trade preferences granted under the gsp+ regulation to ecuador until the entry into force of the eu-ecuador free trade agreement.

in writing. this 4th amending budget is intended to cover a revision of the traditional own resources (or) forecasts, such as customs duties and sugar levies, vat and gni bases, the budgeting of the corrections for the united kingdom, and the revision of revenue from fines. this results in a change in the level and distribution among member states of contributions to the general budget of the eu under these resources. while traditional prs decreased by eur 646.1 million and vat-based prs by eur 192.4 million, fines and default interest increased by eur 2.433 million. thereafter, the national contributions based on gni are reduced by eur 1,594,5 million. we disagree with that. we are not in favour of reducing national contributions, which benefits the large countries and impoverishes the redistributive function of the budget. what was needed was an extra boost from a very meagre budget to meet the cohesion objectives which are increasingly merely the dead letter of the treaties. in this case, it is proposed to reduce the appropriations of the european data protection supervisor and channel them to humanitarian aid.

in writing. the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was set up to respond to major natural disasters and to express european solidarity to disaster-stricken regions in europe. the fund may provide financial assistance to member states and candidate countries negotiating their accession. italy, greece, slovenia and croatia were affected by different types of natural disasters floods, earthquakes and snow and ice storms which caused considerable damage in those member states. support the mobilisation of eur 46 998 528 for the member states concerned, which will help the eu to demonstrate its solidarity and support for the affected countries by contributing to the financing of urgent measures such as the immediate restoration of the functioning of infrastructure and equipment in the fields of energy production, drinking water supply, waste water treatment, telecommunications, transport, health and education; the implementation of interim accommodation measures and the provision of relief services to meet the immediate needs of the affected population; the immediate reinforcement of preventive infrastructure and the protection of cultural heritage sites; the immediate clean-up of disaster areas, including natural areas.

in writing. i agree to the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund for a total amount of eur 46 998 528 to minimise the effects of the severe natural disasters described in this report which occurred in croatia, slovenia, greece and italy this year and last year. the activation of this fund was based on the criteria for extraordinary regional disasters, as provided for in the last paragraph of article 2 of regulation (ec) no 2012/2002 laying down the conditions for the mobilisation of the solidarity fund in exceptional circumstances arising from situations which do not qualify as major natural disasters within the meaning of the regulation on the european union solidarity fund. i believe that the european union has once again fulfilled one of its noblest principles: that of solidarity and mutual assistance between different nations that share the same values, the same continent and share part of their sovereignty in a voluntary and committed way.
in writing. the text approves the mobilisation of the solidarity fund for italy, greece, slovenia and croatia. in the case of italy, the call for mobilisation follows heavy rains in november 2013 which caused many rivers to overflow and major floods. greece was struck by a violent earthquake, followed by dozens of severe aftershocks, between january and february last year, leaving 3,000 people homeless and several others injured. as the total losses are below the threshold for large-scale disasters for mobilising the solidarity fund, the application was examined on the basis of the criteria for regional disasters of an extraordinary nature. slovenia and croatia were also affected by winter snowfall which hit several parts of europe and several countries between january and february this year. in croatia, melting ice and snow resulted in floods that caused additional damage. as the estimated total direct damage in both countries exceeds the normal threshold for mobilising the solidarity fund, this disaster can be considered a major natural disaster. we voted yes.

in writing. - several member states paid less than the amount stipulated for their contributions to the union budget over several years, while others paid a higher amount, and these deviations were due to the significant statistical changes reported by the member states. it is also true that member states have in the past paid the full amount of their contributions to the union budget without significant delays and that certain member states benefited from the previous underestimation of their gni and were reluctant to pay the additional amounts due within the legal deadline. in view of this and in the interests of transparency, i believe that a report on the calculations and underlying data relating to the adjustments to the vat and gni balance sheet in the context of the budgetary procedure should be submitted to parliament annually, with sufficient time for its consideration, and that the decision of the member states on the dates and amounts of the payments should be notified to parliament.
in writing. in recent years, several member states have paid less than the amount stipulated for their contributions to the union budget, while others have paid more. these deviations were due to significant statistical changes reported by the member states. as a general rule, member states have in the past paid the full amount of their gni- and vat-based contributions to the eu budget without significant delays, even in times of crisis and severe budgetary pressure. while we acknowledge that the amounts of vat and gni-based own resources adjustments for 2014 are exceptionally high, we cannot help but question the reasons for this discrepancy, given the sophisticated mechanisms at the service of national accounts, in particular at the level of the countries where this issue arises. in this sense, we have doubts about this amendment, which is motivated by a statistical discrepancy which should be dealt with in its own way to prevent such situations from recurring. the most important thing is that the member states concerned pay what they owe, but we cannot fail to point out the particularly favourable conditions that are being provided, especially to a country like the united kingdom, which has long enjoyed unjustified and unfair prerogatives, such as the famous british cheque.

in writing. the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was set up to respond to major natural disasters and to express european solidarity to disaster-stricken regions in europe. the fund may provide financial assistance to member states and candidate countries negotiating their accession. the fund may also be mobilised in the event of regional disasters. this decision of the parliament and of the council aims to enter in the 2015 budget the amount of eur 50 million in commitment and payment appropriations, corresponding to the advances that will have to be paid more quickly and efficiently in the event of a natural disaster in the coming year. with this decision we are sending a clear political message of solidarity, while delivering real assistance to the affected citizens more quickly.
in writing. - the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was set up to respond to major natural disasters and to express european solidarity to disaster-stricken regions in europe. countries negotiating their accession may receive financial assistance if the total direct damage caused by the disaster exceeds eur 3 billion or 0.6% of the country's gross national income, whichever is the lower. the european parliament has strongly advocated in the relevant negotiations with the council the need to provide financial assistance to member states to respond to a disaster more quickly than would be required under the normal procedure. this position prevailed in the negotiations and a maximum amount of eur 50 million should be entered in the budget each year for this purpose. i agree that the amounts are entered in the 2015 budget.
in writing. the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was set up to respond to major natural disasters and to express european solidarity to disaster-stricken regions in europe. the fund may provide financial assistance to member states and countries negotiating their accession in the event of major natural disasters, if the total direct damage caused by the disaster exceeds eur 3 billion in 2011 prices or 0,6% of the country's gross national income, whichever is the lower. it can also be mobilized in the event of a regional disaster. i hope that with the amendments that have been introduced this instrument will become faster and more effective. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was set up to respond to major natural disasters and to express european solidarity with the people of the affected regions. the conditions for mobilising the eusf are laid down in council regulation (ec) no 2012/2002, which, in its current version, provides for the possibility to mobilise the fund to a maximum amount of eur 50.000.000 for the payment of advances, including the entry of the corresponding appropriations in the general budget of the union (cf. article 4a (4)). this is a new provision designed to ensure that, following a preliminary assessment by the commission, financial assistance (in the form of advances) can be provided quickly and efficiently to member states to respond to disasters that may occur. the objective of this decision is precisely to enter in the 2015 budget the amount of eur 50 million in commitment and payment appropriations, corresponding to the advances to be paid in the event of a natural disaster in the coming year. i voted in favour of the proposal because i believe it is essential to create the conditions for rapid response to natural disasters.
in writing. the european union has set up the solidarity fund (eusf) as a way of responding in a solidarity-based and targeted way to regions affected by large-scale natural disasters. the conditions for mobilising this fund are laid down in council regulation (ec) no 2012/2002, with an annual ceiling of eur 500 000 000, of which eur 50 000 000 may be mobilised for the payment of advances. i therefore support the proposal to enter in the 2015 budget the amount of eur 50 million in commitment and payment appropriations (corresponding to any advances that may have to be paid) to respond more quickly and more effectively to minimising the effects of an unforeseen natural disaster. this appropriation is intended to cover the financing of the european union agency for fundamental rights (the 'agency') and of the european police college (the 'agency').
in writing. having regard to the interinstitutional agreement of 2 december 2013 between the european parliament, the council and the commission on budgetary discipline, on cooperation in budgetary matters and on sound financial management, and in particular point 11 thereof, the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2015, the european union solidarity fund is hereby mobilised to provide the sum of eur 50 000 000 in commitment and payment appropriations for the payment of advances. we have nothing to object to.

in writing. regulation 1071/2009 lays down common rules on the exercise of the occupation of road haulage operator, which contribute, among other factors, to increasing road safety and the level of professional qualification of hauliers. it is incumbent upon the european commission, by means of delegated acts, to draw up a list of the categories, types and degrees of seriousness of serious infringements of community rules. i consider that the list drawn up does not meet the requirements of parliament and in some cases exceeds the power delegated to it, and that this draft regulation is therefore not compatible with the objective and content of the basic regulation 1071/2009 and that the commission should withdraw this draft regulation and submit a new one to parliament.
in writing. this resolution opposes the adoption of the draft commission regulation which complements an existing one (ec/1071/2009) concerning the classification of serious infringements of union rules which may lead to the loss of the competence of road hauliers. the resolution considers that the list of infringements and the degree of seriousness of the infringements presented by the commission is incomplete and should be rejected as such. we support this position. the list contains gaps in the area of illegal cabotage and its impact on road workers and is not balanced with national regulations, in particular with regard to social issues. the minimalist nature of the commission's proposal is a good indication of the interests the commission serves and the objectives it pursues. the legislative framework in force at eu level has always given priority to the objectives of promoting the sacrosanct free competition (and the inevitable monopolistic concentration that always follows it) in order to achieve the said internal market, to the detriment of the objectives of defending and strengthening the promotion of the health and safety of workers in the sector.
in writing. i agree that the draft commission regulation is not compatible with the objective and content of regulation (ec) no 1071/2009 of the european parliament and of the council of 21 october 2009 establishing common rules as regards the requirements for the exercise of the occupation of road transport operator and repealing council directive 96/26/ec. it is appropriate for the commission to present a new list of serious infringements of union rules which may lead to the loss of the road transport operator's fitness to perform the transport service.
in writing. the completion of an internal market in road transport with conditions of fair competition would certainly improve the quality of service and increase road safety. however, the draft commission regulation does not explicitly and sufficiently exhaustively list serious infringements of union rules that could lead to the loss of the road haulier's fitness to carry out the transport operation, nor does it provide for rules on illegal cabotage, despite its potential to create a risk of death or serious injury. since the draft regulation is not compatible with the objective pursued, nor with the content of the regulation of the european parliament and of the council of 21 october 2009, i voted in favour of this resolution calling on the commission to withdraw the draft regulation as regards the classification of serious infringements of union rules which may lead to the loss of the road haulage operator's fitness to operate.
in writing. this resolution opposes the proposal from the delegation of power to the commission to draw up a list of the categories, types and degrees of seriousness of offences which lead to the loss of the road haulage operator's competence, in order to adapt annexes i, ii and iii to the regulation in question. the resolution considers that the proposed document is incompatible with the objective of the existing regulation, as the list contains gaps in the area of illegal cabotage and its impact on road workers, and is not balanced with national regulations, particularly as regards social issues. this is an instrument which, by helping to enforce the labour law of each member state, protects workers with regard to maximum driving time and minimum rest periods, improving working conditions and road safety. however, it also has its negative aspects, since it is part of the objective of ensuring the completion of an internal eu road transport market which requires the uniform application of common rules for access to the activity of road haulage or road passenger transport operator, an objective which, in the neoliberal conditions in which the union market is immersed, has dire consequences, in particular for the survival of micro and smes.
in writing. fuel suppliers shall report life cycle greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions per unit of fuel energy and energy supplied. it is known that there are significant differences in ghg emission intensity between fuels such as traditional crude oil and unconventional feedstocks (e.g. oil sands), with emissions on average higher in the latter. however, the commission ignores these differences and assumes common emission values for the different fuels. a clear favour to multinationals involved in the exploitation of unconventional fuels, which grossly underestimates the ghg emissions associated with them. this is an integral part of the free trade agreement which the european commission is negotiating with canada - a country with significant projects in the field of unconventional oil - and which is intended to please the economic groups concerned by this agreement. the resolution opposes the adoption of the draft directive and calls on the commission to withdraw it and to present a new one, based on the requirement to report default average ghg intensity values, broken down by type of raw material, for petrol and diesel fuel, while allowing suppliers to report actual values. we voted in favour.
in writing. directive 98/70/eu (revised) on the specification of petrol and diesel fuel requires suppliers to report annually on life cycle greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions per unit of fuel and energy supplied in each member state and to reduce the life cycle ghg emissions intensity of fuels supplied by 31 december 2020 by at least 6% compared to the european average of life cycle emissions per unit of energy produced from fossil fuels in 2010. i consider that the draft council directive is not compatible with the purpose and content of directive 98/70/eu. it would therefore be important for the commission to present a proposal compatible with that directive.

in writing. the european commission proposes to reduce the minimum conservation reference size for baltic cod from 38 to 35 cm. there are pertinent reasons for this. the data point to a reduction in the average size of cod in the baltic (after maturation), which has led to an increase in discards in recent years. reducing the minimum catch size will not increase mortality, as the fishing gear will remain the same. the opinion of the scientific, technical and economic committee for fisheries points out that there are no risks to the protection of juveniles, since spawning occurs at lengths of less than 35 cm due to the reduction of the average size. the 35 cm is already the minimum reference size for other fishing areas, such as the north sea. in view of the new rules of the common fisheries policy, which prohibit discards, failure to reduce the minimum size to 35 cm would mean that a considerable part of the fish landed could not enter the normal commercial circuit and would have to be sent for processing into flour. there is therefore a scientific basis for the commission's proposal, as well as strong economic and social reasons. that is why we voted against the resolution which sought to object to this proposal.
in writing. i agree that the reduction of the minimum conservation reference size for cod in the baltic sea proposed by the commission could harm the reproductive capacity of the stocks. i therefore vote in favour of this resolution, which seeks to put an end to this pretence.
in writing. i voted against this resolution establishing a return plan for the baltic sea because i consider that the reduction of the minimum reference size for cod conservation in the baltic sea will not affect the reproductive capacity of the stocks, as the council has decided to make reductions in the quotas of the total allowable catches (tacs) of 7% in the western baltic and 22% in the eastern baltic.

in writing. this resolution is intended to reject the commission delegated act concerning the insurance and reinsurance business and its exercise, in particular as regards the calibration of the risk factors used in the standard formula for the calculation of the solvency capital requirement, namely the classification and eligibility of own funds, the structure and calibration of the shareholder risk sub-module, the treatment of future premiums and the calculation of the risk margin. the delegated act adopted by the commission on 10 october, in addition to not taking into account the technical recommendations of caesspcr/eiopa, results in a significantly lower calibration of the risk factors used in the standard formula for the calculation of the solvency capital requirement, which clearly works in favour of the insurance industry and is contrary to the interests of policyholders in defending and protecting themselves against the risks taken by insurance undertakings. reasons why we voted for it.
