the treaty of lisbon has conferred on the european parliament competences in the field of internal security, in particular with regard to the internal security strategy. at the end of the previous one, parliament shall approve what it considers should be the priorities of the internal security strategy for 2015-2019. the aim is to ensure democratic control and respect for fundamental rights, thus contributing to a genuine area of freedom, security and justice.
the reference to the emergence of new security threats since the establishment of the current esi, citing the examples of cybersecurity, trafficking in human beings, the fight against terrorism and related issues, as well as organised crime, money laundering and corruption, is proof of the failure of the eu's policy guidelines and the responsibilities of this same strategy in the period that is now ending. we must reject the hypocritical version of the security problem which conceals its own responsibilities. one example is human trafficking, which continues to be a tragedy for thousands of people, and in particular for immigrants who are pushed into the hands of criminal organizations by the repressive and criminalising policies of eu immigration. another example is the support of terrorist organisations through the provision of arms, training and funding, with the aim of destabilising countries such as syria. this resolution confirms that the security problems will never be solved by those who not only largely caused them but are preparing policies that will aggravate them.
in writing. the lisbon treaty laid the foundations for the development of an eu security policy, closely shared by the eu and the member states, based on the rule of law, respect for fundamental rights and solidarity, subject to democratic oversight at european and national level and respecting the principle of subsidiarity. the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon gives the european parliament the role of a full-fledged actor in security policy matters, with a view to ensuring democratic control, and thus authorises parliament to participate actively in the definition of priorities in this area and to engage with all relevant actors at eu and national level with a view to developing a comprehensive, targeted and effective security policy in the eu. in the face of the new challenges facing the eu, it is necessary to draw up a new esi for the next four years, which takes into account all the new threats and challenges that arise. that is why i am voting in favour.
following the treaty of lisbon, which laid the foundations for the development of a security policy for the european union (eu) and gave the european parliament the role of a full-fledged actor in security policy matters, empowering it to engage in dialogue with all national and community actors with a view to developing a comprehensive, targeted and effective security policy in the eu. whereas the security situation in europe has changed radically in recent years due to the emergence of new conflicts, becoming a cross-border and cross-sectoral problem, and whereas freedom, security and justice are objectives which must be pursued in parallel; whereas the development of a new internal security strategy (iss) for the next four years should take into account new security threats and the entry of the charter of fundamental rights into eu law; the radicalisation and the rapid growth in the number of eu nationals joining terrorist organisations and then returning to the european territory is worrying. finally, stressing the need to ensure adequate financial resources for the proper implementation of the measures provided for in the esi, i voted in favour of this resolution on the renewal of the esi.
in writing. at a time when, according to a recent europol assessment, we are witnessing an increase in serious and organised crime and, at the same time, threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts, i consider it extremely important, i would even say fundamental, that a renewal of the eu's internal security strategy (iss) be carried out for the next four years. i would therefore stress the relevance of the oral question which gave rise to this resolution, which i voted in favour of. i would also point out that it is essential, in order to promote the effectiveness of the esi, that a thorough analysis of security threats is carried out in close cooperation between europol, other relevant eu bodies and the member states, especially as the lisbon treaty has laid the foundations for the development of a security policy that is shared with the member states. a policy based on the rule of law, respect for fundamental rights and in which the european parliament plays a fully-fledged role in the process, with a view to democratic control and the development of a comprehensive, well-oriented and effective policy in the european union.

in writing. - for more than half a century, the achievement of a just and lasting peace between israelis and palestinians has been a matter of great concern to the international community, including the european union. it is noted that the united nations general assembly decided on 29 november 2012 to grant palestine the status of a non-member observer state to the un. it should be noted that the recognition of the state of palestine is a matter for the member states. this does not mean that political resolutions cannot be adopted on the subject. i therefore support the recognition of the palestinian state and the two-state solution, believing that both sides must go hand in hand with the deepening of the peace negotiations, which must progress. the solution of two-state coexistence must be based on the 1967 borders and jerusalem as the capital of both, i.e. a secure state of israel and an independent, democratic, territorially continuous and viable state of palestine living side by side in peace and security, which implies the recognition of the right to self-determination and full respect for international law.
in writing. we voted in favour of this resolution. despite its shortcomings and limitations, it is a minimal sign of recognition of the inalienable right of the palestinian people to a state. we cannot fail to point out some of the negative aspects of the resolution, namely: - the insistence on security applied only to the state of israel (as if palestine did not need security), seeking to create the idea that the borders of the state of palestine are drawn in accordance with this objective; - the distinction between terrorism and violence and the condemnation of all violent protest, thus denying the right of palestinians to revolt and resist the israeli occupation; - the absence of any reference to united nations resolutions (181, 194, 248, 332) or to the withdrawal of troops from the occupied territories, which, among other objectives, constitutes a way of marginalizing the un in this process; - it calls for a common eu position, which in the current context, when there are countries such as sweden that have already recognised palestine, means an attempt to limit the sovereign power of the member states to decide on recognition, and a brake on countries that want to recognise the state of palestine.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this joint resolution because i believe that the european parliament should join the various national parliaments which have already called for the recognition of the state of palestine. however, i refused to co-sign it on behalf of my political group because i consider that the compromise solution reflected in the first paragraph of this joint resolution falls short of what i believe the ep's position should be by urging all eu member states to recognise the state of palestine. the statement that the european parliament agrees with the principle of palestinian self-determination is nothing new, it is a position repeatedly expressed by this parliament in all the resolutions in which it has called for coexistence between the two states, the state of israel and the state of palestine. the movement for the universal recognition of the state of palestine is growing. apart from the palestinians, israel needs the establishment of an independent, democratic and secure state in its neighbourhood.

in writing. we agree that the steel sector and the steel industry have always been one of the pillars of industrial economies. we are therefore surprised that the resolution does not consider how wrong the eu's policy towards the sector has been, allowing such inequalities and transfers to the private sector to be dug up within and between member states, particularly in portugal where the sector has already been quite developed and is now deeply constrained. we support the resolution when it calls for the development of industrial production in all member states, when it warns of energy prices and environmental issues, or when it stresses the need to invest in research and innovation. however, we regret that no concrete proposals are being made at social level to preserve existing jobs and to prevent the creation of precarious jobs in the sector. as regards state aid to energy-intensive industries, it is argued that it should not distort the internal market by ensuring a level playing field for undertakings. in this chapter, the limitations imposed by the treaties are aimed at preventing the necessary support for national production and enterprises by imposing the law of the strongest and monopolistic concentration at eu level. that is why we abstained.
european economic recovery depends to a large extent on the existence of a solid manufacturing industry in which the steel industry plays a central role and that manufacturing industry depends on domestic demand and supply. it is therefore necessary to speed up the preparation of the industrial policy package announced for the first part of 2015 in order to revive european industry on the world market, to ensure a level playing field and to ensure high social and environmental standards in the european union, while pushing for reciprocity from third countries. an ambitious approach to reindustrialisation in the context of the europe 2020 mid-term review is of vital importance to achieve a genuine eu industrial policy and to relaunch the eu's industrial competitiveness at global level. a policy to encourage industrial production is essential to achieve job creation and economic growth. that is why i am voting in favour.
the steel sector plays a key role in europe's economy and industry, providing more than 350 000 direct jobs and several million jobs in related industries, including the recycling supply chain. in recent years, the steel industry has faced some difficulties, caused in particular by an investment crisis, a slump in global demand, rising energy costs and the increased outsourcing of european production. it is therefore necessary to adopt measures to support this sector, aimed at removing obstacles and threats to its competitiveness, promoting its sustainability and making it able to react to changing conditions on european and non-european markets. the resolution contains a set of proposals aimed at protecting the eu steel industry and its workers. i voted in favour of the proposed measures because i believe that they will generally help to make the eu steel industry more competitive at international level.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal because i believe that the european union needs a functioning, competitive and secure steel industry that can contribute to growth and prosperity in europe. it is true that this sector has suffered a sharp decline in demand, leading to increased unemployment, but it is also true that the eu must preserve the activities which constitute its industrial fabric, ensuring the security of energy supply through internal demand. as such, i support the commission's action plan for the steel sector, but draw attention to the need to draw up an analysis report on the current situation of the steel industry on our continent, analysing its economic, social and environmental impact and reflecting on medium and long-term support initiatives. finally, i would point out the need to place this support within a wider framework of support for european manufacturing industry, since only in this way (in a sound way and by investing in research, innovation, the qualification of human resources and energy efficiency, and possibly by using community funds) can its competitiveness be ensured, its added value stimulated and its important social role enhanced.

in writing. in 2013, more than 100,000 migrants attempted to cross the mediterranean, of whom more than 500 are estimated to have died or disappeared. according to the iom, 2014 was the deadliest year for migrants, with an estimated 3,000 people dying trying to cross the mediterranean. in fact, experts confirm that the likelihood of migrants dying while making this crossing has been increasing in recent years. this year, new rules for search and rescue operations in frontex joint operations, for which i was rapporteur, come into force. this new instrument does not, however, cover strictly national search and rescue operations. in view of the migratory pressure in the mediterranean, this dual legal system can be problematic. one year after parliament's resolution on the lampedusa tragedy, this resolution is on the right track: we must tackle the root of the problems. however, we must also deal with what is happening in the mediterranean quickly. or we risk it becoming a graveyard.
in writing. this resolution insists on support for an immigration policy which is responsible for the deaths of thousands of people in the mediterranean, the overwhelming majority of them young people seeking to flee war, crime, unemployment, poverty and hunger, in search of better living conditions for themselves and their families, despite the risks of the crossing. strengthening border and security policy and advocating the improvement of the future role of frontex makes clear the intention to maintain and deepen a policy that has turned the eu into a fortress where, in order to arrive, migrants have to submit to trafficking and criminal networks that proliferate in the shadow of the repression and criminalization of migrants. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the right-wing and social-democratic parties' call for these policies to be deepened allows us to anticipate the limits of the possible establishment of a committee of inquiry. we voted against it.

in writing. the different conflicts in the middle east have intensified migration flows to the member states of the european union, and the various shipwrecks in the mediterranean have raised the alarm about the ongoing humanitarian situation (more than 3000 deaths in 2014). considering that the italian rescue operation, called mare nostrum, will be phased out and the contributions to the joint operation triton are uncertain, it is important to reiterate the need for a coordinated policy at european level (through frontex and the eaggf) and, it is also important that the eu takes its share of responsibility and solidarity towards the member states hosting the largest number of refugees. similarly, voluntary return policies need to be encouraged, while ensuring the protection of the rights of all migrants and providing safe and legal access to the eu asylum system. finally, it is necessary to consider an analysis of how the funds for internal affairs are spent in this context, in particular in the fight against smuggling and trafficking. for these reasons, i voted in favour of this resolution calling for parliament to draw up a strategic own-initiative report before the end of 2015.

mr president-in-office of the council, mr commissioner, in 2007 and in 2006, this parliament investigated this case through a committee which i had the honour of chairing. some said at the time that it was impossible for a state governed by the rule of law like the united states of america to commit the illegal acts that were attributed to it. the us authorities claimed that the allegations were unfounded. they lied! in september 2006 we had a witness we hadn't asked for: george w. bush, then president of the united states of america, confirmed to the world the extraordinary rendition programme and acknowledged that the abductions were true, that detainees were not subjected to a court, that secret prisons existed, but he vehemently denied that torture was used. he lied, once again, as the us senate report just published showed. this senate report leaves us with four important messages. first, it takes courage to have moral authority, as senator feinstein pointed out, and well, only a mature democracy is able to review its own mistakes and contribute to preventing them from being repeated in the future. second, we cannot give up on bringing the truth to the surface. it is not obvious that the truth will always come out, especially when national governments create obstacles to the deepening of what has happened, without our making an effort. i repeat what i have said here more than once: under no circumstances can state secrets override fundamental, inalienable rights. this parliament must continue its efforts and contribute to the full clarification of what has happened in the european union. thirdly, the ends do not justify the means. torture is not morally acceptable, it is condemned by international law and it is not even effective, as this report proves and as senator mccain has already said. and finally, there is a deficit in the democratic control of the secret services. the report is proof that for several years democratic control over the secret services has not worked. the secret services must be subject to greater democratic control and this must also happen in the european union. answer according to the "blue card" procedure. i'm sure i agree with you completely. the added value of the inquiry is not just to ascertain responsibility. that is important, but as i said, we must hold everyone accountable, those who did it, those who authorised it, and those who kept it quiet. but above all, the added value of the survey is to ensure that we learn from the past and that we learn from the lessons so that we do not repeat the same mistakes in the future.
the senate report confirms everything that the european parliament and council of europe reports have already exposed since 2007, but adds startling new details, both about the torture and other crimes practiced by the cia in the extraordinary renditions program, about the network of secret prisons to relocate and outsource torture to assad, gaddafi or mubarak's stooges, and about the extent of the lies and omissions of the cia and the bush administration to deceive congress and the american and global public. several european governments may also have been misled, but others knew and acquiesced to the cia operation. the senate blocks the names of 25 european countries. it is up to this parliament to say what they are. some of the accomplices did more than just authorize planes to fly over to transport the prisoners. the senate confirms that there have been secret arrests in europe. poland, lithuania and romania have already had to admit what they have denied before this parliament. the european parliament has a duty to re-establish a mechanism for checking the participation of the member states of the european union in this programme carried out on behalf of the united states. it is essential to end impunity. the first flights to guantanamo bay, on november 11, 2002, carried suspected terrorists across my country, portugal. between flights, overflying, stopovers, technical stops, between 2002 and 2007 are more than a hundred times that the cia used portuguese territory in the process of committing these crimes. but it remains to be seen whether the portuguese authorities were just stupid and incompetent and deceived by the united states or were they complicit and active participants in this programme? it is yet to be ascertained whether the stopovers involved detention and torture on national soil, for example at the lages base in the azores. the government of my party - i say this with shame and bitterness - since 2006 has done everything to obstruct the knowledge of the truth by preventing a parliamentary inquiry, by hindering a judicial inquiry, by preventing scrutiny of the secret services, and by denying the european parliament and the national parliament lists of authorised flights to and from guantanamo, which i was able to obtain and hand over to the inquiry committee of this parliament. i would like to conclude, mr president, by saying that all these efforts were made to cover up his own responsibilities and not to jeopardise the chances of re-electing the former portuguese prime minister, durão barroso, as head of the european commission, who was an active accomplice in this cia programme between 2002 and 2005. the search for the truth in portugal is important for portugal and for europe. in writing. the main objective of the gsp is to facilitate access to the eu market for developing countries and territories by reducing customs duties on their goods. following the request submitted by the philippines, the special incentive arrangement for sustainable development and good governance, known as gsp+, is intended to provide duty-free access to approximately 66% of the total tariff lines under the normal gsp. since this special scheme is conditional on the implementation of ratification by the countries of relevant international conventions on sustainable development, it does not appear to me that the philippines fulfils the conditions for accessing this special scheme. i am not only referring to the issue of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing by this state, but above all to the findings of the un report on trafficking in human beings, which points to the existence of human trafficking, especially of women and children, for the purpose of labour exploitation in the agricultural, fisheries, construction, manufacturing and service sectors. for these reasons, i reject the granting of gsp+ status to the philippines.
in writing. - we regret that it was not possible to reach a qualified majority to approve parliament's resolution objecting to the delegated act granting gsp+ to the philippines. firstly, because the status is granted before the commission has withdrawn its notification of the philippines as a third country considered as non-cooperating in the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing. the commission notified the philippines that it may be considered a non-cooperating country in the fight against illegal fishing and initiated a procedure under which the philippines has a reasonable period to respond to the notification and justify the situation, which has not yet occurred. secondly, in view of the impact that the granting of this scheme to the philippines may have on the domestic canning industry. the portuguese market currently absorbs around 80% of the national production of canned tuna. given that the philippines, like thailand, is one of the world's leading producers of canned fish, especially canned tuna, any reduction of customs duties could result in large quantities of canned tuna from the philippines entering the domestic market, with inevitable negative effects on the domestic canning industry.
in writing. i have signed and voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the philippines should only have a special status in trade relations with the eu when it complies with all the required rules. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the conclusion of the agreement on the fishing rights of certain stocks in the north sea.
in writing. the generalised system of preferences consists of a general scheme and two special schemes, including the special incentive scheme for sustainable development and good governance (gsp+), without the levying of duties on imports from beneficiary countries in relation to 66% of all eu tariff lines. on 28 february 2014, the commission received a gsp+ application from the republic of the philippines, which it proposes to accept, pursuant to commission delegated regulation (c(2014) 05833 of 19 august 2014. given that, by decision of 10 june 2014, the commission notified the republic of the philippines of the risk of being identified as a non-cooperating third country in fighting illegal fishing (iuu), i believe that it is not appropriate to grant gsp+ status to the philippines at this stage. such a measure would introduce conditions of unfair competition for european fishermen, seriously damaging the interests of several member states, including portugal. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution which opposes the said delegated regulation, postponing the granting of gsp+ status to the philippines to a later stage, when the conditions for withdrawal of the notification under the iuu procedure are met.
in writing. because i believe that the european union must be a credible international actor and promote consistency in its action, because i believe that our partner third countries must abide by the same rules to which we are subject, namely those relating to human rights, labour, environmental protection and (good) governance, because i believe that our industrial sector, namely the canning industry (but also the textile and clothing and bicycle industry), must be protected from unfair competition by third country companies, i was one of the promoters of this resolution (and previously of the resolution on the same subject voted in the inta committee) which sought to prevent the immediate granting of a very broad set of customs benefits (gsp+) to the philippines. unfortunately, despite a higher number of votes in favour in plenary (313 votes in favour, 285 against), a qualified majority of 50% + 1 vote was needed to approve this resolution (376 votes against), which did not happen. we will therefore continue to monitor developments in this matter, including the commission's assessment of the philippines over the next year and the progress of the iuu investigation process in the philippines.
in writing. the gsp system consists of a general scheme and two special schemes, including the special incentive scheme for sustainable development and good governance (sgsp+), without the levying of any duties on imports from beneficiary countries in relation to 66% of all eu tariff lines. the commission, in its resolution of 17 november 2011 on combating illegal fishing worldwide, explicitly states that iuu fishing threatens the sustainability of fish stocks and that the concept of the responsibility of the marketing state as a means of blocking access to markets for iuu fishery products needs to be further developed. we support this regulation, but we also note the contradiction in the philippine process.
in writing. the outstanding banking union element concerns a delegated act concerning ex ante contributions to resolution financing mechanisms, which sets out how much banks need to pay to the resolution fund. one of the problems with this specific act is that it does not ensure that the fixed contributions reflect the risk profile of the banks in an appropriate way. in other words, healthy banks with conservative business models and their own institutional guarantee systems, such as cooperative banks that will probably never need any resolution fund, will be called upon to pay the risk that those who play in the financial markets will have to bear. this opens the way for an unfair distribution of the funding costs of the resolution funds which particularly harms local low-risk banks. the non-objection to this delegated act is an undemocratic act and an evasion of scrutiny of the commission's activities by the european parliament, an unacceptable blank cheque. apart from our position in principle on the banking union, there are plenty of reasons for our vote against it.
in writing. article 103 of the drrb directive provides that member states shall ensure that at least annual contributions are levied on credit institutions and investment firms authorised in their territory. those contributions shall be adjusted in proportion to the risk profile of the institutions in accordance with the criteria specified by the commission in a delegated act to be adopted pursuant to paragraph 7 of that regulation. on the basis of that empowerment, the commission adopted on 21 october 2014 a delegated regulation supplementing the drrb directive with regard to ex ante contributions to resolution financing arrangements. considering that, in order for the implementation of the srbd to proceed by 1 january 2015, it is necessary for the national resolution authorities to start calculating and collecting contributions as soon as possible and that the agreement on the council implementing regulation specifying the uniform conditions of application of regulation (eu) no 806/2014 as regards ex ante contributions to the single resolution fund is consistent with the delegated regulation concerned, i voted in favour of this decision not to raise objections to the same.
in writing. the outstanding element on banking union concerns a delegated act on ex ante contributions to resolution financing mechanisms, which sets out how much banks need to pay to the resolution fund. one of the problems with this specific act is that it does not ensure that the fixed contributions reflect the risk profile of the banks in an appropriate way. in other words, healthy banks with conservative business models and their own institutional guarantee systems, such as cooperative banks that will probably never need any resolution fund, will be called upon to pay for the risks of those who play in the financial markets. this opens the way for an unfair distribution of the financing costs of the resolution funds, which particularly harms local banks with low risk. the early withdrawal of a non-objection to this delegated act is not only an undemocratic act and an evasion of scrutiny of the commission's activities by the european parliament, but it is also a blank cheque which we cannot accept.

in writing. in recent years, georgia has made significant progress in reforms and in strengthening relations with the eu. in this process, the conclusion of the eu-georgia association agreement and the establishment of the deep and comprehensive free trade area (dcfta) in this context are of key importance, both for the mutual benefits they bring to the parties and as a sign of recognition of the efforts made by the georgian authorities to strengthen the stability and independence of the institutions and to consolidate the rule of law and the system for the protection of fundamental rights. the agreement now being concluded, it is important to ensure its implementation and to follow up reform efforts, particularly as regards the creation of the conditions for the construction of a free society based on democratic values and the strengthening of the independence of the judiciary, which must under no circumstances be used as an instrument of political revenge. the eu also calls on russia to fully respect georgia's sovereignty and territorial integrity, to withdraw recognition of the secession of abkhazia and the tskhinvali region/south ossetia, to end the occupation of these territories and to commit to non-use of force against georgia.
in writing. the association agreement between the european union and georgia, negotiated under the eastern partnership between 2012 and 2013, provides for the creation of a deep and comprehensive free trade area (dcfta) of mutual benefit. by committing to binding commitments to adopt common legislation, standards and values, georgia will offer its citizens a more stable, predictable and scrutinized legal framework and improve its access to the world's largest trading bloc. the eu will benefit from greater trade flows and better investment conditions in the country, promoting the modernisation of the economy and providing a more favourable and predictable political environment. the cfta is expected to increase eu-georgia trade by 12% for georgia's exports to the eu and by around 7.5% for eu imports, improving the current account situation of georgia. i therefore voted in favour of the conclusion of this agreement.
in writing. the association agreement (aa) between the european union (eu) and georgia, negotiated under the eastern partnership between 2012 and 2013, is modelled on the eu-ukraine association agreement, which is the most ambitious free trade agreement ever negotiated by the eu with a third country, excluding european economic area countries, with the creation of a deep and comprehensive free trade area (dcfta) with the eu. we do not see ourselves in these free trade agreements which represent in our era a new form of colonialism in a commercial and economic version. we are negotiating trade agreements which are not based on free trade but rather on mutual cooperation and respect for the specific characteristics of all parties. the agreement is another chapter in the siege of russia, and seeks to break historic ties of cooperation which reflect not only geographical proximity but also cultural identities. only then can one understand the offensive purposes used to demonize russia. we voted against it.
